verbose.help: Verbosity level. Higher values make the tools more talkative.

debug.help: Run the flow in debug mode: verbose logging, and exceptions are re-raised instead of being reported as a failure.

quiet.help: Run the flow quietly, unless `verbose` or `debug` is set.

redirect_stdout.help: Redirect stdout from execution of tools to files.

lib_paths.help: Additional libraries, as a list of (name, path) tuples. The name or the path can be none, but not both. GHDL and NVC take a relative path as relative to the design root.

docker.help: Run the tools in this Docker image, instead of the default image of the flow.

print_commands.help: Print the commands that the flow runs.

console_colors.help: Colorize tool output on the console.

bobj_dir.help: Directory for the packages bsc compiles (`.bo`/`.ba` files, `-bdir`), relative to the run directory.

info_dir.help: Directory for bsc's informational files (`-info-dir`), such as the schedules of `show_schedule` and the graphs of `sched_dot`, relative to the run directory. Defaults to `bobj_dir`.

cleanup_bobjs.help: Before compiling, remove the packages (`.bo`/`.ba`) that an earlier run compiled in `bobj_dir`. bsc recompiles a package (`-u`) only when its source is newer than its `.bo`, so without this a change of flags or macros alone is not compiled. Disable only to reuse the packages of a run with identical settings and sources. The Verilog modules that an earlier run generated are removed in either case, and bsc writes them again.

search_paths.help: Additional directories bsc searches for imported packages (`-p`), after the directories of the design's Bluespec sources and before bsc's own libraries, e.g. for libraries such as bsc-contrib's. Relative to the design root.

verilog_search_paths.help: Additional directories searched for the Verilog files of imported (`import "BVI"`) and library modules (`-vsearch`), before bsc's own Verilog library. The directories of the design's Verilog sources are always searched. Relative to the design root. Not used by Bluesim, which reads no Verilog.

fdir.help: Directory that relative file names are resolved against while bsc elaborates the design, e.g. files opened with `openFile` (`-fdir`); relative to the design root. Defaults to the run directory.

cpp.help: Run the C preprocessor on the sources before bsc's own preprocessor (`-cpp`), and define the design's macros for it too. BH (`.bs`) sources go through no other preprocessor, so this is the only way they see `rtl.defines`. They test a macro with `#ifdef`, where BSV uses `` `ifdef ``.

cpp_flags.help: Arguments passed to the C preprocessor (`-Xcpp`), one per item, with `cpp`.

aggressive_conditions.help: Propagate the implicit condition of an action in one branch of an `if` to the rule predicate together with that branch's condition, so the rule can fire when only the other branch is blocked (`-aggressive-conditions`). On by default since bsc 2026.07; turning it off can shorten compile times.

sched_conditions.help: Take method conditions into account when computing rule conflicts (`-sched-conditions`). On by default since bsc 2026.07; turning it off can shorten compile times.

split_if.help: Split rules at `if` statements in their actions, so the branches are scheduled as separate rules (`-split-if`). Can multiply the number of rules; the `(* split *)` attribute does it for individual rules. See also `lift`.

lift.help: Lift method calls out of the branches of `if` statements, calling a method once with a multiplexed argument (`-lift`). Recommended without `split_if`; bsc recommends turning it off with `split_if`.

let_gen.help: Generalize the types of untyped `let` bindings, as bsc did before 2026.07 (`-let-gen`). Only for code that relied on it; an explicit type signature is the fix.

resource_scheduling.help: When more rules call a method than it has ports: "off" fails the compilation (`-resource-off`); "simple" blocks rules, arbitrarily, until they fit (`-resource-simple`). Not for finished designs.

sat_solver.help: SMT solver bsc uses for disjointness tests and SAT (`-sat-yices` or `-sat-stp`). Change it only for scheduling or optimization performance problems.

check_assert.help: Check the assertions of bsc's `Assert` library, such as `staticAssert` and `dynamicAssert` (`-check-assert`). Without it they are ignored, so a testbench's `dynamicAssert` can never fail.

unspecified_to.help: Value the don't-care bits left in the generated code are tied to: "X" or "Z" (as in Verilog), "0", "1", or "A" for alternating ones and zeros (`-unspecified-to`). "X", the default, gives synthesis the most freedom; "X" and "Z" require `opt_undetermined_vals`.

opt_undetermined_vals.help: Let the Verilog backend choose don't-care values from their context (`-opt-undetermined-vals`), for better hardware.

optimize.help: Simplify the conditions of rules and `if`s during elaboration (`-O`, a hidden bsc flag, the same as `-opt-bool`): two-level minimization of a condition of up to 8 variables, bsc's BDD-based simplifier beyond. It can save a few percent of the logic after synthesis, but can multiply bsc's run time: the core of bluespec/Piccolo, which compiles in about 80 s without it, did not finish in 30 minutes with it.

extra_optimize_flags.help: Further bsc optimization flags: the `-opt-*` flags of `bsc -help-hidden` that bsc leaves off, e.g. ["-opt-bit-const"]. Measure before adopting one: "-opt-if-mux" enlarges some designs.

synthesize_to_boolean.help: Synthesize all primitive operators into simple boolean operations (`-synthesize`). It hides the arithmetic from a downstream synthesis tool: on the examples, their adders and multipliers then mapped to no carry chains or DSP blocks, for up to 2.4 times the LUTs.

remove_false_rules.help: Remove rules whose condition is provably false (`-remove-false-rules`). bsc warns about each.

remove_empty_rules.help: Remove rules whose bodies have no actions (`-remove-empty-rules`). bsc warns about each.

remove_starved_rules.help: Remove rules the generated schedule never fires (`-remove-starved-rules`). bsc warns about each; they usually point at a scheduling problem.

remove_unused_modules.help: Remove submodules not connected to any output from the generated Verilog (`-remove-unused-modules`), as synthesis would.

keep_fires.help: Keep every rule's `CAN_FIRE_` and `WILL_FIRE_` signals in the generated code, so waveforms show rule firings (`-keep-fires`).

keep_inlined_boundaries.help: Keep the boundaries of inlined registers and wires as signals (`-keep-inlined-boundaries`).

keep_method_conds.help: Keep the predicates of method calls inside rules as signals (`-keep-method-conds`).

readable_mux.help: Generate multiplexers as readable `case` statements (`-readable-mux`). bsc 2026.07.1 fails with an internal error on some designs without it.

remove_dollar.help: Use `_` rather than `$` between instance and port names in generated Verilog identifiers (`-remove-dollar`). Verilog output only.

reset_prefix.help: Name of the reset port of generated modules (`-reset-prefix`), e.g. "RST_P". bsc names it "RST_N" by default.

positive_reset.help: Make resets active-high: define `BSV_POSITIVE_RESET` for the Bluespec preprocessor, and at the top of every Verilog file in `artifacts.verilog` that bsc generated or copied from its library (they take their reset polarity from it). The design's own Verilog sources are passed on unchanged, preceded by `bsv_defines.v`, the first artifact, which defines the macro for those that read it. Consider naming the port with `reset_prefix`.

v95.help: Generate strict Verilog-95 (`-v95`), without the Verilog-2001 features bsc uses otherwise, such as named parameter passing and `$signed`.

use_dpi.help: Implement imported C functions with the SystemVerilog DPI rather than VPI in generated Verilog (`-use-dpi`). Required to simulate them with Verilator.

system_verilog_tasks.help: Keep SystemVerilog system tasks such as `$fatal` and `$error` in the generated Verilog (`-system-verilog-tasks`). Without it bsc lowers `$fatal` to `$display` and `$finish(1)`, which exits a Verilog simulation successfully.

verilog_filters.help: Commands bsc runs on each Verilog file it generates, in order, with the file's name as their only argument (`-verilog-filter`).

elab.help: Also write the elaborated and scheduled modules (`.ba` files, `-elab`), which Bluetcl needs to inspect a compiled design.

show_schedule.help: Write each generated module's schedule to a `.sched` file in `info_dir` (`-show-schedule`).

sched_dot.help: Write each generated module's scheduling graphs as `.dot` files in `info_dir` (`-sched-dot`).

show_rule_rel.help: Pairs of rules whose scheduling relationship bsc reports (`-show-rule-rel r1 r2`); ["*", "*"] reports every pair.

show_method_conf.help: Document the conflicts between the methods of each generated module in its Verilog (`-show-method-conf`).

show_method_bvi.help: Document each generated module's method schedule in its Verilog, in the form an `import "BVI"` of it takes (`-show-method-bvi`).

show_range_conflict.help: Include the conditions of the method calls when reporting a parallel composability error, G0004 (`-show-range-conflict`).

show_stats.help: Report package statistics after each compiler stage (`-show-stats`).

show_elab_progress.help: Trace the elaboration of modules, rules and methods, to locate where a compilation hangs (`-show-elab-progress`).

show_version.help: Record the compiler version in the generated files (`-show-version`).

show_timestamps.help: Record a timestamp in the generated files (`-show-timestamps`). Off, so that unchanged inputs regenerate identical files.

warn_method_urgency.help: Warn when the urgency between a method and a rule is chosen arbitrarily (`-warn-method-urgency`).

warn_action_shadowing.help: Warn when a rule's action is overwritten by a later rule in the same cycle (`-warn-action-shadowing`).

warn_undetermined_predicate.help: Warn when a rule or method predicate has an undetermined value (`-warn-undet-predicate`).

promote_warnings.help: Warnings reported as errors (`-promote-warnings`), by tag, or "ALL"/"NONE". Candidates are the scheduling warnings that can mean a design will not behave as written: ["G0009", "G0010", "G0117"] for a conflict added to break a cycle, a rule arbitrarily made more urgent than another, and an action shadowed by a later rule. None is promoted by default: working designs raise them by design (bluespec/Piccolo: 26 G0010 and 85 G0117), and promoting one changes no hardware, it only rejects those designs.

suppress_warnings.help: Warnings not reported (`-suppress-warnings`), by tag, e.g. ["G0021"], or "ALL"/"NONE".

demote_errors.help: Errors reported as warnings (`-demote-errors`), by tag, or "ALL"/"NONE". Not every error can be demoted.

continue_after_errors.help: Continue compiling other modules and stages after an error, to report more errors at once (`-continue-after-errors`).

steps_warn_interval.help: Warn each time elaboration has unfolded this many more function calls (`-steps-warn-interval`; bsc's own default is 100000).

steps_max_intervals.help: Give up elaborating after this many `steps_warn_interval` warnings (`-steps-max-intervals`; bsc's own default is 10). The default only stops runaway elaborations, since large designs legitimately take many steps.

haskell_runtime_flags.help: Flags for the Haskell run-time system bsc runs on, passed as `+RTS ... -RTS`: e.g. "-H1G" to suggest a 1 GB heap, "-K64M" to limit the stack.

extra_flags.help: Further bsc flags for every compilation, added after the ones these settings produce, so they take precedence (see `bsc -help` and `bsc -help-hidden`).

verilog_out_dir.help: Directory for the generated Verilog and the library modules it uses, relative to the run directory. It is the flow's: bsc overwrites the modules it generates, the library modules are copied over, and an earlier run's generated modules are removed before bsc compiles.

verilog_primitives.help: Which versions of bsc's Verilog library modules to use: the generic ones, or those tuned for "vivado" or "quartus" synthesis (block RAMs and a few others, from `$BLUESPECDIR/Verilog.Vivado` or `Verilog.Quartus`).

timeout.help: Stop and fail each subprocess invocation that contains simulation after this many seconds of wall-clock time. An invocation can combine analysis, elaboration and simulation. The limit applies to each invocation, not to their total. None sets no limit.

vcd.help: Write a VCD waveform to this file. `true` writes `dump.vcd`; a name without an extension gets `.vcd`; `false` or an empty name writes none. A simulator that cannot write VCD refuses it, and names its own waveform settings.

stop_time.help: Stop the simulation at this simulated time. Accepts a number of nanoseconds or a string with a unit, e.g. "100us".

cocotb.help: Settings for the cocotb testbench, used when `tb.cocotb` is set.

cocotb.coverage.help: Collect coverage data if supported by simulation tool.

cocotb.reduced_log_fmt.help: Display shorter log lines in the terminal.

cocotb.resolve_x.help: How to resolve bits with a value of X, Z, U or W when they are converted to an integer.

cocotb.testcase.help: Names of the cocotb tests to run; all of them if empty. A name selects exactly the test of that name (`check` never selects `foo_check`); on cocotb 2.x it may be qualified by its module (`tb.check`). Can also be given as a comma-separated string.

cocotb.random_seed.help: Seed of the Python random module (`COCOTB_RANDOM_SEED`): the same seed recreates the same test stimulus. "random" lets cocotb draw a new seed on every run, so the flow then always runs and is never reused.

clocks.*.rise.help: Time of the rising edge of the clock, a time with a unit, such as `0.5 ns`.

clocks.*.uncertainty.help: Clock uncertainty, a time with a unit, such as `0.1 ns`.

clocks.*.skew.help: Clock skew, a time with a unit, such as `0.05 ns`.

clocks.*.port.help: The design port of the clock.

clocks.*.freq.help: Clock frequency, a frequency with a unit, such as `100 MHz`. Specify `freq` or `period`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

log_file.help: Path of the log file. When not set, the log goes only to stdout.

no_init.help: Do not load the home and local `.synopsys` initialization files.

sdc_files.help: List of user SDC constraint files.

py_script.help: Python script run inside nextpnr (`--run`), for custom constraints or analysis. Requires a nextpnr built with Python support.

write.help: Write the post-routing design to this JSON file.

sdf.help: Write post-routing timing to this SDF file, for timing-annotated netlist simulation.

log.help: File nextpnr writes its log to.

report.help: File that nextpnr writes its JSON report of utilization and timing to. The flow reads its results from this file.

detailed_timing_report.help: Ask nextpnr for a detailed timing report for each path. This report is unstable and can crash nextpnr.

placed_svg.help: Render the placed design to this SVG file.

routed_svg.help: Render the routed design to this SVG file.

parallel_refine.help: Enable the parallel placement refinement of nextpnr. It is faster on many cores. Only some nextpnr builds have it.

chipdb.help: An existing Himbaechel Xilinx chip database file. Without it, Xeda prepares a chip database in a shared cache under the run root. The cache entry is named by the content of the files that make it.

delay_matrix.help: Xilinx interconnect delay model. `build` measures it for each tile offset (the default of the backend). `off` uses the tuned formula.

hold_fix.help: Xilinx: fix hold-time violations after routing. `true` uses the default pass limit of the backend (8). A positive number sets the pass limit.

hold_detour_max.help: Xilinx: hold deficit in ns up to which hold fixing uses a routing detour instead of a feedthrough LUT.

placement.help: Xilinx placement dump in JSON (cell to tile, site and bel). It is always written in the run directory, and the LUT count is read from it. The default is `outputs/<design>_placement.json`.

clock.period.help: Clock period, a time with a unit, such as `10 ns`. Specify `period` or `freq`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

clock.rise.help: Time of the rising edge of the clock, a time with a unit, such as `0.5 ns`.

clock.uncertainty.help: Clock uncertainty, a time with a unit, such as `0.1 ns`.

clock.skew.help: Clock skew, a time with a unit, such as `0.05 ns`.

clock.port.help: The design port of the clock.

clock.freq.help: Clock frequency, a frequency with a unit, such as `100 MHz`. Specify `freq` or `period`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

verbose.help: Verbosity level. Higher values make the tools more talkative.

debug.help: Run the flow in debug mode: verbose logging, and exceptions are re-raised instead of being reported as a failure.

quiet.help: Run the flow quietly, unless `verbose` or `debug` is set.

redirect_stdout.help: Redirect stdout from execution of tools to files.

lib_paths.help: Additional libraries, as a list of (name, path) tuples. The name or the path can be none, but not both. GHDL and NVC take a relative path as relative to the design root.

docker.help: Run the tools in this Docker image, instead of the default image of the flow.

print_commands.help: Print the commands that the flow runs.

console_colors.help: Colorize tool output on the console.

timeout.help: Stop and fail each subprocess invocation that contains simulation after this many seconds of wall-clock time. An invocation can combine analysis, elaboration and simulation. The limit applies to each invocation, not to their total. None sets no limit.

fail_severity.help: The least severe runtime diagnostic that fails the simulation: warning, error, failure or fatal. Failure and fatal have the same rank. Diagnostics below the threshold are recorded. Assertions that the design disables explicitly keep the documented behavior of the simulator. A nonzero exit status always fails.

vcd.help: Write a VCD waveform to this file. `true` writes `dump.vcd`; a name without an extension gets `.vcd`; `false` or an empty name writes none. A simulator that cannot write VCD refuses it, and names its own waveform settings.

stop_time.help: Stop the simulation at this simulated time. Accepts a number of nanoseconds or a string with a unit, e.g. "100us".

cocotb.help: Settings for the cocotb testbench, used when `tb.cocotb` is set.

cocotb.coverage.help: Collect coverage data if supported by simulation tool.

cocotb.reduced_log_fmt.help: Display shorter log lines in the terminal.

cocotb.resolve_x.help: How to resolve bits with a value of X, Z, U or W when they are converted to an integer.

cocotb.testcase.help: Names of the cocotb tests to run; all of them if empty. A name selects exactly the test of that name (`check` never selects `foo_check`); on cocotb 2.x it may be qualified by its module (`tb.check`). Can also be given as a comma-separated string.

cocotb.random_seed.help: Seed of the Python random module (`COCOTB_RANDOM_SEED`): the same seed recreates the same test stimulus. "random" lets cocotb draw a new seed on every run, so the flow then always runs and is never reused.

cocotb.gpi_extra.help: A comma-separated list of extra libraries that are dynamically loaded at runtime.

one_shot.help: Run analysis, elaboration and execution in one `nvc` command. If false, run each step as a separate command.

ignore_time.help: Do not check the timestamps of source files when the corresponding design unit is loaded from a library.

heap_size.help: Maximum size of the simulation heap, in bytes. The heap holds the temporary allocations of processes and the allocations of the VHDL `new` operator. A `k`, `m` or `g` suffix selects kilobytes, megabytes or gigabytes. The default is 16 megabytes.

messages.help: Format of error and informational messages. The default, `full`, is easy to read. The `compact` format is easy for tools to parse.

std_error.help: Print messages at the selected severity or higher to stderr instead of stdout. The default sends all messages to stderr. The levels are `note`, `warning`, `error` and `failure`.

warn_error.help: Treat the warnings of the analysis as errors (`-Werror`).

werror.help: Treat the warnings of the analysis as errors (`-Werror`).

analysis_flags.help: Extra flags passed to `nvc -a` when analyzing sources.

check_synthesis.help: Warn about common coding mistakes that can cause problems in synthesis, such as signals missing from a process sensitivity list.

psl_in_comments.help: Enable parsing of PSL directives in comments during analysis.

relaxed.help: Disable some pedantic LRM conformance checks and rules that later standards relaxed.

elab_flags.help: Extra flags passed to `nvc -e` during elaboration.

cover.help: Kinds of code coverage to collect (`--cover`).

jit.help: Defer native code generation to run time (`--jit`). Normally NVC compiles all code ahead of time during elaboration. With this setting, NVC compiles each function on a background thread after the interpreter has executed it often enough. This greatly reduces elaboration time, at the cost of more memory and CPU use while the simulation runs. It helps short simulations, where ahead-of-time compilation gains little.

no_collapse.help: Preserve both signals when a port map directly connects signals at adjacent hierarchy levels. By default, NVC collapses them into the upper-level signal. Preserving both improves debugging at some performance cost.

no_save.help: Do not save the elaborated design to a file (`--no-save`). Normally NVC saves the elaborated design in the work library, and the simulator loads it from there quickly. Without the file, the simulator elaborates the design again on each run. This helps when debugging elaboration.

optimization_level.help: Optimization level (`-O`), from 0 to 3. Higher levels can speed up the simulation but slow down elaboration.

print_verbose.help: Print resource usage after each elaboration step (`--verbose`).

run_flags.help: Extra flags passed to `nvc -r` when running the simulation.

ieee_warnings.help: Turn the warnings of the standard IEEE packages on or off. NVC's default is on.

fst.help: Write the waveform as an FST file: a name in the run directory, or a location it is delivered to ($PWD/..., $DESIGN_ROOT/..., $DESIGN_DIR/... or an absolute path). `true` writes `dump.fst`; a name without an extension gets `.fst`. NVC writes one waveform: set only one of `fst` and `vcd`.

wave_arrays.help: Include memories and nested arrays in the waveform. True includes all of them, an integer N only arrays with up to N elements, and false none. Large arrays cost performance, memory and disk space.

wave_include_glob.help: Include the signals that match this glob pattern in the waveform. Examples: `:top:*:x`, `*:x`, `:top:sub:*`. See https://www.nickg.me.uk/nvc/manual.html#SELECTING_SIGNALS. Needs `vcd` or `fst`.

wave_exclude_glob.help: Exclude the signals that match this glob pattern from the waveform. Examples: `:top:*:x`, `*:x`, `:top:sub:*`. See https://www.nickg.me.uk/nvc/manual.html#SELECTING_SIGNALS. Needs `vcd` or `fst`.

stop_delta.help: Stop the simulation after this many delta cycles at the same time.

vhpi.help: VHPI libraries to load at startup.

shuffle.help: Run processes in random order. The VHDL standard does not specify the execution order of processes, and simulators differ in subtle ways. This setting helps to find code that depends on a particular order. Use it only for debugging: it slows the simulation considerably and can make the result non-deterministic.

stats.help: Print a summary of the time taken and memory used at the end of the run.

verbose.help: Verbosity level. Higher values make the tools more talkative.

debug.help: Run the flow in debug mode: verbose logging, and exceptions are re-raised instead of being reported as a failure.

quiet.help: Run the flow quietly, unless `verbose` or `debug` is set.

redirect_stdout.help: Redirect stdout from execution of tools to files.

lib_paths.help: Additional libraries, as a list of (name, path) tuples. The name or the path can be none, but not both. GHDL and NVC take a relative path as relative to the design root.

docker.help: Run the tools in this Docker image, instead of the default image of the flow.

print_commands.help: Print the commands that the flow runs.

console_colors.help: Colorize tool output on the console.

clocks.help: Clock constraints of the design, by clock name.

clocks.*.period.help: Clock period, a time with a unit, such as `10 ns`. Specify `period` or `freq`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

clocks.*.rise.help: Time of the rising edge of the clock, a time with a unit, such as `0.5 ns`.

clocks.*.uncertainty.help: Clock uncertainty, a time with a unit, such as `0.1 ns`.

clocks.*.skew.help: Clock skew, a time with a unit, such as `0.05 ns`.

clocks.*.port.help: The design port of the clock.

clocks.*.freq.help: Clock frequency, a frequency with a unit, such as `100 MHz`. Specify `freq` or `period`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

fpga.help: FPGA device. Accepts a full part identifier as a string (e.g. "xc7a100tftg256-2L") or a mapping of the FPGA fields. A part identifier alone means `part: <identifier>` wherever layers merge. Over a mapping, it changes the part and keeps the other fields that the mapping wrote (a speed grade, for example).

fpga.part.help: Full part identifier of the device.

board.help: Target development board. Fills in `fpga` (and board-specific constraint files) from the board database. See `xeda list-boards`. A bundled board is found by its name in any letter case; a name in a custom database is case-sensitive.

custom_boards_file.help: Path to a board database, in TOML or YAML (by the file's suffix: `.toml`, `.yaml` or `.yml`), used instead of the bundled database. Relative paths are resolved against the design directory; a board's local `lpf` resolves relative to this file. The board names in it are case-sensitive.

reset.help: Reset the FPGA after loading the bitstream (`--reset`).

cable.help: Programming cable to use, for example "ft2232". Takes precedence over the cable implied by `board`.

write_flash.help: Program nonvolatile flash (`--write-flash`). Needs the FPGA device (`fpga.part`, or a `board` that has one): the flash is programmed through a bridge made for the part.

verify.help: Verify the SPI flash after programming. Needs `write_flash`.

usb_serial_num.help: Serial number of the FTDI probe to use (`--ftdi-serial`). Selects one of several probes of the same kind.

index_chain.help: Index of the device in the JTAG chain.

file_type.help: Bitstream type when extension detection is insufficient.

target_flash.help: Flash chip to program on boards with two (`--target-flash`).

skip_load_bridge.help: Skip loading the SPI bridge during flash programming.

clock.period.help: Clock period, a time with a unit, such as `10 ns`. Specify `period` or `freq`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

clock.rise.help: Time of the rising edge of the clock, a time with a unit, such as `0.5 ns`.

clock.uncertainty.help: Clock uncertainty, a time with a unit, such as `0.1 ns`.

clock.skew.help: Clock skew, a time with a unit, such as `0.05 ns`.

clock.port.help: The design port of the clock.

clock.freq.help: Clock frequency, a frequency with a unit, such as `100 MHz`. Specify `freq` or `period`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

docker.help: Run the tools in this Docker image, instead of the default image of the flow.

print_commands.help: Print the commands that the flow runs.

console_colors.help: Colorize tool output on the console.

platform.help: Name of a bundled ASIC platform (see `xeda list-platforms`). It names the standard cell library and the technology files that the flow works on. Give `platform_file` for a platform that Xeda does not ship; then `platform` can be left out, and if given it must be the `name` of that file.

platform_file.help: Residue file of a platform (YAML). A file that sets `extends` to a bundled platform changes only what it gives. A file without `extends` is a complete platform. A relative path is relative to the design root.

corner.help: Name of the corner of the platform, or one of its aliases. The default is the default corner of the platform. A flow works on one corner: a list of corners is refused.

liberty.help: Standard cell (Liberty) libraries that the flow reads for mapping and timing, instead of the Liberty files of the corner of the platform. Xeda reads each file as it is (`yosys` gives each to `dfflibmap` and to `abc`). Without them, the flow uses the Liberty files of the platform. The platform still gives everything else, and its files must be installed. The files of a producer and its consumer agree, in the same order.

library.help: Standard cell (Liberty) libraries that the flow reads for mapping and timing, instead of the Liberty files of the corner of the platform. Xeda reads each file as it is (`yosys` gives each to `dfflibmap` and to `abc`). Without them, the flow uses the Liberty files of the platform. The platform still gives everything else, and its files must be installed. The files of a producer and its consumer agree, in the same order.

dont_use_cells.help: Standard cells that the flow must not use, in addition to the cells that the platform lists. The default is none.

pdk_provider.help: Where the PDK files of the platform come from. `orfs`: a sparse checkout of OpenROAD-flow-scripts. `ciel`: a PDK build that `ciel` installs. `lambdapdk`: a sparse checkout of lambdapdk. `directory`: a directory that holds the files in a known layout. The default is the provider that the platform names; the platform must have an entry for the provider.

pdk_version.help: Version of the PDK files: the commit (`orfs`, `lambdapdk`) or the hash (`ciel`). For `directory`, a version that Xeda checks against the directory when it can, and `unpinned` when you give none. The default is the version that the platform pins for `pdk_provider`. The version is part of the identity of the run.

pdk_root.help: Directory of the PDK store. `None` means `~/.ciel`. Variables such as `$HOME` expand in it, and a relative path is relative to the design root. It tells where the files are, so it is no part of the identity of the run: the run depends on the content of the files it reads.

hierarchical.help: Keep the hierarchy of the design: OpenROAD links the netlist with `link_design -hier` and reads each database with `read_db -hier`. The database does not tell how it was read, so every OpenROAD flow of a chain must agree on this setting. It is separate from the hierarchy that `yosys` keeps.

wire_rc.help: Resistance and capacitance of the wires, which replace the values of the platform leaf by leaf: the layers and vias that you list replace the ones of the platform with the same name, and the others stay. The default is the wire RC of the platform. The database stores no wire RC, so every OpenROAD flow of a chain must agree on this setting.

wire_rc.signal_layer.help: Layer whose resistance and capacitance estimate a signal net.

wire_rc.clock_layer.help: Layer whose resistance and capacitance estimate a clock net.

wire_rc.layers.help: Resistance and capacitance per micrometer of each layer, in the units of the library: the units of the Liberty file. On the command line, give a pair as `resistance,capacitance`.

wire_rc.vias.help: Resistance of each via, by via name, in the units of the library: the resistance unit of the Liberty file.

write_gds.help: Write the GDSII layout of the routed design with KLayout. It needs the KLayout files and the GDSII files of the platform.

save_images.help: Save images of the routed design in the directory `images` of the run directory. It needs an OpenROAD build that includes the GUI, and the Qt platform plugin `offscreen`. OpenROAD v2.0-26132-g6b305a712 on macOS has no such plugin and stops with GUI-0077.

netlist_power_pins.help: Write the power and ground pins in the netlist `netlist` (`write_verilog -include_pwr_gnd`). A netlist for LVS needs them, and a simulation does not.

write_timing_model.help: Write a Liberty timing model of the routed design as `timing_model` (`write_timing_model`), for the timing analysis of a design that uses the block. After the reports, the flow sets the source latency of the clocks to 0 and writes the model, so the reports and the verdict read the constraints of the design.

fail_timing.help: The flow fails if the routed design does not meet timing.

fail_drc.help: The flow fails if the detailed route leaves design rule violations.

fail_antenna.help: The flow fails if antenna violations remain after the repair.

detailed_route.end_iteration.help: The most optimization iterations (`-droute_end_iter`). The tool clamps larger values to 64. The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

detailed_route.reroute_seed.help: The seed that shuffles the nets to reroute (`-or_seed`). A developer option of the router. Unset: no shuffling.

detailed_route.reroute_swap_factor.help: The factor that sets how many swaps the shuffle makes (`-or_k`): the number of swaps is the factor times the number of nets to reroute. Needs `reroute_seed`.

detailed_route.drc_report_step.help: Write a DRC report every this many iterations (`-drc_report_iter_step`). 0 writes no report during the route. The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

detailed_route.via_in_pin.help: The range of layers where a via may sit inside a pin (`-via_in_pin_bottom_layer`, `-via_in_pin_top_layer`). Unset: the flow gives the router no range. No platform gives one.

detailed_route.via_in_pin.bottom.help: The lowest layer where a via may sit inside a pin (`-via_in_pin_bottom_layer`).

detailed_route.via_in_pin.top.help: The highest layer where a via may sit inside a pin (`-via_in_pin_top_layer`).

detailed_route.via_access_layer.help: A pin on this layer or below is reached by vias only (`-via_access_layer`). Unset: the router decides.

detailed_route.min_access_points.help: The least number of access points that the router finds for each pin of a standard cell or a macro (`-min_access_points`). Unset: the default of the router.

detailed_route.pin_access.help: The router analyzes the access to the pins itself. False skips that analysis (`-no_pin_access`): the router then works with the access points that an earlier `pin_access` left in the database, which `openroad_grt` runs with `pin_access.enabled`.

detailed_route.via_generation.help: The router makes vias for the pins and the wide wires besides the vias of the technology. False allows only the vias of the technology (`-disable_via_gen`).

detailed_route.repair_pdn_vias_layer.help: The layer of the vias of the power grid that the router removes where they cause design rule violations (`-repair_pdn_vias`). A platform whose first two metal layers carry the power rails in parallel needs it. Unset: the router removes none.

detailed_route.clean_patches.help: Remove the patch wires that the router does not need (`-clean_patches`).

detailed_route.save_guide_updates.help: Save the changes that the router makes to the route guides (`-save_guide_updates`).

detailed_route.verbose.help: The level of the messages of the router (`-verbose`). The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

detailed_route.default_vias.help: The vias that the router prefers, by name, one command each (`detailed_route_set_default_via`). The command has no entry in the help of OpenROAD. Empty: the router chooses.

detailed_route.unidirectional_layers.help: The layers where the router allows wires in the preferred direction only, one command each (`detailed_route_set_unidirectional_layer`). The command has no entry in the help of OpenROAD. Empty: the layers keep the direction rule of the technology.

detailed_route.require_routed.help: The flow fails when a net is unrouted after the route and the antenna repair (`design_is_routed`). OpenROAD-flow-scripts fails then. False keeps the partial route and goes on, so the later checks and the outputs describe it.

detailed_route.snapshots.help: Save the database after each iteration that leaves violations (`set_debug_level DRT snapshot 1`) as `drt_iter<n>.odb` in the run directory, for each iteration `n` up to `end_iteration`. A database is large, so use it for a small design.

detailed_route.extra_args.help: More flags for `detailed_route`. Each flag must be `-db_process_node`, followed by its value. The router uses it to select the via rules of one process node, which the platform of the node gives.

ndr.help: The non-default routing rules for the detailed route.

ndr.rules.help: The rules to create, by name (`create_ndr`). The database keeps them.

ndr.rules.*.width.help: The width of the wires, by layer. A key is a layer name or a range `first:last` of routing layers. A value is a length with a unit, such as `0.14 um`, or a factor of the default width, written `*2`. A layer that no key names keeps its default width.

ndr.rules.*.spacing.help: The spacing of the wires, by layer. A key is a layer name or a range `first:last` of routing layers. A value is a length with a unit, such as `0.14 um`, or a factor of the default spacing, written `*2`.

ndr.rules.*.vias.help: The vias that the nets of the rule may use, by name.

ndr.assignments.help: The rule of each net, by net name (`assign_ndr -net`). A rule is one of `rules` or a rule that the database already holds.

ndr.clock_rule.help: The rule for all clock nets (`assign_ndr -all_clocks`). A rule is one of `rules` or a rule that the database already holds. Unset: no rule for the clock nets.

antenna.help: The repair of the antenna violations of the detailed route.

antenna.repair.help: Repair the antenna violations of the detailed route. OpenROAD-flow-scripts does it. The flow skips the repair, with a note in the log, when the platform says that the router cannot use its diode. The check of the antenna violations runs in every case.

antenna.reroute_iterations.help: The most rounds of repair and reroute. The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

antenna.method.help: How `repair_antennas` fixes a violation. `diode` inserts diodes only (`-diode_only`), `jumper` moves wire to a higher layer only (`-jumper_only`), and `both` tries jumpers and then diodes. The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts, which names neither flag. The command reads the diffusion area of the diode to judge a violation, with every method, so a platform without a usable diode skips it.

antenna.ratio_margin_percent.help: Repair a violation when the antenna ratio comes within this share of its limit, in percent (`-ratio_margin`). The margin costs area. Unset: the default of the tool, 0.

antenna.diode_cell.help: The diode cell that `repair_antennas` inserts. Unset: the antenna cell of the platform. A cell named here is used even where the platform says that the router cannot use its diode.

fill.help: The filler cells that fill the gaps in the rows.

fill.cells.help: The filler cells, as glob patterns of cell names (`filler_placement`). The flow places them after the last change of the route. An empty list places no filler. Unset: the value of the platform.

fill.decap_cells.help: The decoupling capacitor cells, as glob patterns of cell names. They fill the same gaps, and the flow gives them to the same `filler_placement` command, before `cells`. No platform gives any. Empty: no decap cell.

fill.prefix.help: The prefix of the names of the filler instances (`-prefix`). Unset: the default of the tool, `FILLER_`.

fill.check.help: Check the placement after the filler cells are in (`check_placement`). The check stops the flow on an illegal placement. OpenROAD-flow-scripts does it.

extraction.help: The extraction of the parasitics of the routed design.

extraction.method.help: `rcx` extracts the parasitics with OpenRCX, with the rules of the platform. `estimate` estimates them from the detailed route (`estimate_parasitics`). `auto` uses `rcx` when the platform has the rules, and `estimate` otherwise.

extraction.rules_file.help: The rules file of OpenRCX (`set_extraction_rules_file`). A relative path is relative to the design root. Unset: the rules file of the platform.

extraction.model_index.help: The index of the process corner in the rules file (`define_process_corner -ext_model_index`). The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

extraction.corner_index.help: The corner to extract (`-corner`). Unset: the default of the tool, all.

extraction.corner_count.help: The number of corners to extract (`-corner_cnt`). Unset: the default of the tool, 1.

extraction.max_res.help: The resistors in series merge up to this resistance, a resistance with a unit, such as `50 ohm` (`-max_res`). Unset: the default of the tool, 50 ohm.

extraction.coupling_threshold.help: A coupling capacitance below this value counts as a capacitance to the ground, a capacitance with a unit, such as `0.1 fF` (`-coupling_threshold`). Unset: the default of the tool, 0.1 fF.

extraction.cc_model.help: The number of tracks on each side of a wire that count for its lateral coupling (`-cc_model`). Unset: the default of the tool, 10.

extraction.context_depth.help: The number of layers above and below a wire that count for its capacitance (`-context_depth`). Unset: the default of the tool, 5.

extraction.lef_values.help: Take the resistance (`res`, `-lef_res`) or the resistance and the capacitance (`rc`, `-lef_rc`) of the wires from the LEF files and not from the rules file. `none` takes both from the rules file. OpenROAD v2.0-26132-g6b305a712 crashes with `rc` (signal 11 in `dbVia::getBottomLayer`, called from `extMain::getShapeRC`) on a routed nangate45 design; no upstream issue is known.

extraction.merge_via_res.help: Merge the resistance of a via into the wire next to it. False keeps the resistance of the vias apart (`-no_merge_via_res`).

extraction.skip_over_cell.help: Ignore the shapes inside the cells when OpenRCX looks for the neighbors of a wire (`-skip_over_cell`).

extraction.model_version.help: The version of the extraction model (`-version`): 1.0 or 2.0. Unset: the default of the tool, 1.0.

extraction.scale.help: The factors that scale the extracted parasitics.

extraction.scale.res.help: The factor for the resistance of the wires (`-res_factor`). Unset: 1.

extraction.scale.cc.help: The factor for the coupling capacitance between wires (`-cc_factor`). Unset: 1.

extraction.scale.gnd.help: The factor for the capacitance of the wires to the ground (`-gndc_factor`). Unset: 1.

reports.help: The text reports of the final process.

reports.timing.help: The report of the timing paths, `reports/timing.rpt`.

reports.timing.enabled.help: Write the report of the timing paths. OpenROAD-flow-scripts does it.

reports.timing.paths.help: The number of paths to report in each path group (`-group_path_count`). The default is the one of the tool.

reports.timing.format.help: How the report shows a path (`-format`). The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts. With `json` the report ignores `fields`.

reports.timing.fields.help: The columns that the report adds to a path (`-fields`). The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

reports.timing.unconstrained.help: Report the paths without a constraint too (`-unconstrained`). OpenROAD-flow-scripts does it.

reports.clock_skew.help: Report the clock skew (`report_clock_skew`) in `reports/clock_skew.rpt` and put the skew of the setup and hold checks in the results. OpenROAD-flow-scripts can switch it off since it can take long on a large design.

reports.power.help: Write the power report (`report_power`) to `reports/power.rpt`. The total power in the results does not depend on it.

reports.check_setup.help: Write the sanity checks of the constraints (`check_setup -verbose`) to `reports/check_setup.rpt`.

ir_drop.help: The analysis of the IR drop of the power grid.

ir_drop.enabled.help: Analyze the IR drop of the power grid, for each supply net that the platform gives a voltage. The analysis only reports, and it never fails the run. On a platform that gives no voltage for any supply net, the flow skips the analysis, and the log says so.

ir_drop.nets.help: The supply nets to analyze, each with its voltage, a voltage with a unit, such as `1.1 V` (`set_pdnsim_net_voltage`). The analysis follows the order of the table. Unset: the power nets and then the ground nets of the platform, with the voltages that it gives.

ir_drop.source_type.help: How the analysis models the voltage sources (`-source_type`). `full` takes every node of the top layer as a source, `bumps` models a grid of bumps, and `straps` models the sources as straps. Unset: the default of the tool, `bumps`.

ir_drop.source.help: The geometry and the resistance of the voltage sources.

ir_drop.source.bump_dx.help: The pitch of the bumps along x, a length with a unit and a whole number of micrometers (`-bump_dx`). Unset: the default of the tool, 140 um.

ir_drop.source.bump_dy.help: The pitch of the bumps along y, a length with a unit and a whole number of micrometers (`-bump_dy`). Unset: the default of the tool, 140 um.

ir_drop.source.bump_size.help: The size of a bump, a length with a unit and a whole number of micrometers (`-bump_size`). Unset: the default of the tool, 70 um.

ir_drop.source.bump_interval.help: Fill every this many bumps of the grid (`-bump_interval`), to model the bumps that signals and other supplies take. Unset: the default of the tool, 3.

ir_drop.source.strap_track_pitch.help: The pitch of the straps that model the sources, in tracks of the top layer (`-strap_track_pitch`). Unset: the default of the tool, 10.

ir_drop.source.external_resistance.help: The resistance of the package and of the supply network outside the block, a resistance with a unit (`-external_resistance`). Unset: the default of the tool, 0 ohm.

ir_drop.vsrc_files.help: A file with the places of the voltage sources of a net, by net name (`-vsrc`). A relative path is relative to the design root. Unset for a net: the model of the sources decides.

ir_drop.instance_power.help: The power of the instances that replaces the computed power, by instance name, a power with a unit, such as `2 mW` (`set_pdnsim_inst_power`).

ir_drop.instance_voltages.help: Write the voltage of each instance for each net, as a CSV file `reports/irdrop_voltage_<n>.csv` (`-voltage_file`). Here `<n>` counts the nets from 1 in the order of the analysis.

ir_drop.electromigration.help: Report the current in each segment of the power grid for each net, as `reports/irdrop_em_<n>.csv` (`-enable_em`, `-em_outfile`).

ir_drop.spice.help: Write the SPICE netlist of the power grid of each net, as `reports/irdrop_spice_<n>.sp` (`write_pg_spice`).

ir_drop.decap.help: The decoupling capacitors to insert at the worst IR drop.

ir_drop.decap.enabled.help: Insert decoupling capacitor cells at the worst IR drop of a supply net. It needs `target_capacitance` and `cells`.

ir_drop.decap.target_capacitance.help: The capacitance to insert, in the units of the library: the capacitance unit of the Liberty files (`-target_cap`).

ir_drop.decap.cells.help: The decap cells to use, by name or glob pattern, each with its capacitance in the units of the library: the capacitance unit of the Liberty files (`-cells`).

ir_drop.decap.net.help: The supply net that gets the cells (`-net`). It is one of the nets of the analysis, and it is required when `ir_drop.nets` gives the nets. Unset: the first power net of the platform.

gds.help: The GDSII file of the routed design.

gds.seal_ring.help: A GDSII file with a seal ring, which KLayout merges into the layout. A relative path is relative to the design root. Needs `write_gds`.

gds.layer_map.help: A file that maps the layers of the LEF and DEF files to the layers and data types of the GDSII file. A relative path is relative to the design root. Unset: the map of the technology file of KLayout.

gds.cell_libraries.help: More GDSII or OASIS files to merge, after those of the platform: the layouts of macros and of other cells that the platform does not give. A relative path is relative to the design root.

gds.allow_empty.help: A regular expression for the names of the cells that may have no layout. The merge fails for any other cell of the design that no file gives. Unset: every cell needs a layout.

gds.conflict_resolution.help: What happens when a GDSII or OASIS file has a cell with the name of a cell that is in the layout already: add the content to the cell, overwrite the cell, rename the new cell, or skip the new cell. Unset: the default of KLayout, `add_to_cell`.

gds.lefdef_options.help: The options of the reader of the LEF and DEF files.

gds.lefdef_options.read_lef_with_def.help: Read the LEF files together with the DEF file. Unset: as the technology file of the platform says.

gds.lefdef_options.net_properties.help: Keep the name of the net as a property of its shapes. False removes the property and makes the layout smaller. Unset: as the technology file of the platform says.

gds.lefdef_options.instance_properties.help: Keep the name of the instance as a property of its cell instance. False removes the property. Unset: as the technology file of the platform says.

gds.lefdef_options.pin_properties.help: Keep the name of the pin as a property of its shapes. False removes the property. Unset: as the technology file of the platform says.

gds.timestamps.help: Write the time stamps of the cells into the GDSII file. False keeps the file the same from run to run.

verbose.help: Verbosity level. Higher values make the tools more talkative.

debug.help: Run the flow in debug mode: verbose logging, and exceptions are re-raised instead of being reported as a failure.

quiet.help: Run the flow quietly, unless `verbose` or `debug` is set.

redirect_stdout.help: Redirect stdout from execution of tools to files.

lib_paths.help: Additional libraries, as a list of (name, path) tuples. The name or the path can be none, but not both. GHDL and NVC take a relative path as relative to the design root.

docker.help: Run the tools in this Docker image, instead of the default image of the flow.

print_commands.help: Print the commands that the flow runs.

console_colors.help: Colorize tool output on the console.

platform.help: Name of a bundled ASIC platform (see `xeda list-platforms`). It names the standard cell library and the technology files that the flow works on. Give `platform_file` for a platform that Xeda does not ship; then `platform` can be left out, and if given it must be the `name` of that file.

platform_file.help: Residue file of a platform (YAML). A file that sets `extends` to a bundled platform changes only what it gives. A file without `extends` is a complete platform. A relative path is relative to the design root.

corner.help: Name of the corner of the platform, or one of its aliases. The default is the default corner of the platform. A flow works on one corner: a list of corners is refused.

liberty.help: Standard cell (Liberty) libraries that the flow reads for mapping and timing, instead of the Liberty files of the corner of the platform. Xeda reads each file as it is (`yosys` gives each to `dfflibmap` and to `abc`). Without them, the flow uses the Liberty files of the platform. The platform still gives everything else, and its files must be installed. The files of a producer and its consumer agree, in the same order.

library.help: Standard cell (Liberty) libraries that the flow reads for mapping and timing, instead of the Liberty files of the corner of the platform. Xeda reads each file as it is (`yosys` gives each to `dfflibmap` and to `abc`). Without them, the flow uses the Liberty files of the platform. The platform still gives everything else, and its files must be installed. The files of a producer and its consumer agree, in the same order.

dont_use_cells.help: Standard cells that the flow must not use, in addition to the cells that the platform lists. The default is none.

pdk_provider.help: Where the PDK files of the platform come from. `orfs`: a sparse checkout of OpenROAD-flow-scripts. `ciel`: a PDK build that `ciel` installs. `lambdapdk`: a sparse checkout of lambdapdk. `directory`: a directory that holds the files in a known layout. The default is the provider that the platform names; the platform must have an entry for the provider.

pdk_version.help: Version of the PDK files: the commit (`orfs`, `lambdapdk`) or the hash (`ciel`). For `directory`, a version that Xeda checks against the directory when it can, and `unpinned` when you give none. The default is the version that the platform pins for `pdk_provider`. The version is part of the identity of the run.

pdk_root.help: Directory of the PDK store. `None` means `~/.ciel`. Variables such as `$HOME` expand in it, and a relative path is relative to the design root. It tells where the files are, so it is no part of the identity of the run: the run depends on the content of the files it reads.

hierarchical.help: Keep the hierarchy of the design: OpenROAD links the netlist with `link_design -hier` and reads each database with `read_db -hier`. The database does not tell how it was read, so every OpenROAD flow of a chain must agree on this setting. It is separate from the hierarchy that `yosys` keeps.

wire_rc.help: Resistance and capacitance of the wires, which replace the values of the platform leaf by leaf: the layers and vias that you list replace the ones of the platform with the same name, and the others stay. The default is the wire RC of the platform. The database stores no wire RC, so every OpenROAD flow of a chain must agree on this setting.

wire_rc.signal_layer.help: Layer whose resistance and capacitance estimate a signal net.

wire_rc.clock_layer.help: Layer whose resistance and capacitance estimate a clock net.

wire_rc.layers.help: Resistance and capacitance per micrometer of each layer, in the units of the library: the units of the Liberty file. On the command line, give a pair as `resistance,capacitance`.

wire_rc.vias.help: Resistance of each via, by via name, in the units of the library: the resistance unit of the Liberty file.

repair_clock_inverters.help: Clone each inverter of the clock network that drives several loads, so that each clone drives one load (`repair_clock_inverters`, run before the clock tree). OpenROAD-flow-scripts runs it.

buffers.help: The buffers that the clock tree may use.

buffers.select.help: How the tool finds the clock buffers. `inferred` takes them from the Liberty files, without the cells that the platform and `dont_use_cells` exclude. `list` takes the cells of `cells` (`-buf_list`). `library` takes the buffers of the Liberty library `library` (`-library`). `footprint` takes the cells whose footprint in the Liberty file contains `footprint` (`set_cts_config -clock_buffer_footprint`). `name` takes the cells whose name contains `name_pattern` (`set_cts_config -clock_buffer_string`).

buffers.cells.help: The buffer cells that the clock tree may use. Needs `select: list`.

buffers.root.help: The buffer at the root of the clock tree (`-root_buf`). Unset: the tool chooses it, the first cell of `cells` when there is a list.

buffers.tree.help: The buffer inside the tree (`-tree_buf`). Unset: the tool chooses it.

buffers.sink.help: The buffer that drives each cluster of sinks (`-sink_clustering_buffer`). Unset: the tool chooses it.

buffers.library.help: The name of the Liberty library that the buffers come from. Needs `select: library`.

buffers.footprint.help: The text that the footprint of a clock buffer contains. Needs `select: footprint`. The tool also uses it to choose the buffers of the repair of the clock nets.

buffers.name_pattern.help: The text that the name of a clock buffer contains. Needs `select: name`. The tool's own default is `CLKBUF`.

sink_clustering.help: The grouping of the clock sinks under one buffer each.

sink_clustering.mode.help: `off` builds no clusters. `auto` builds clusters with the size and the diameter that the tool derives from the buffers (`-sink_clustering_enable`). `explicit` builds them with `size`, `max_diameter` or both.

sink_clustering.size.help: The most sinks in a cluster (`-sink_clustering_size`). Needs `mode: explicit`.

sink_clustering.max_diameter.help: The largest diameter of a cluster, a length with a unit (`-sink_clustering_max_diameter`). Needs `mode: explicit`.

sink_clustering.levels.help: Cluster the clusters again, with this many extra levels, when the design has more than 400 clusters (`-sink_clustering_levels`). Needs clustering: not with `mode: off`. Unset: no second level.

sink_clustering.buffer_cap_derate.help: The share of the maximum capacitance of a buffer that the tool counts when it chooses the root and sink buffers itself, from 0 to 1 (`-sink_buffer_max_cap_derate`). A small value favors strong buffers, and 1 applies no derating. Unset: the default of the tool, 0.01.

macro_clustering.help: The grouping of the macro sinks, which the tool clusters on their own.

macro_clustering.size.help: The most macro sinks in a cluster (`-macro_clustering_size`). Unset: the default of the tool, 4.

macro_clustering.max_diameter.help: The largest diameter of a cluster of macro sinks, a length with a unit (`-macro_clustering_max_diameter`). Unset: the default of the tool, 50.

tree.help: The shape of the clock tree.

tree.style.help: `lut` builds the tree with the lookup table of the characterization, and the tool decides where the buffers go. `simple_segments` puts a buffer every `buffer_distance`.

tree.buffer_distance.help: The distance between the buffers of a wire, a length with a unit (`-distance_between_buffers`). Needs `style: simple_segments`.

tree.branch_buffer_distance.help: A branch at least this long gets a buffer at its end point, a length with a unit (`-branching_point_buffers_distance`). Needs `style: simple_segments`. Unset: no buffer at the end of a branch.

tree.wire_unit.help: The shortest wire segment that the characterization tests, a length with a unit and a whole number of micrometers (`-wire_unit`). Unset: the tool derives it from the height of the buffer that it characterizes.

tree.clustering_exponent.help: The power that the clustering of the sinks (CKMeans) puts on the distance between a sink and the mean of its cluster (`-clustering_exponent`). Unset: the default of the tool, 4.

tree.clustering_unbalance_ratio.help: The largest share of the sinks that one cluster may take in the clustering of the sinks, from 0 to 1 (`-clustering_unbalance_ratio`). 0.5 splits the sinks of a region in two equal halves. Unset: the default of the tool, 0.6.

tree.static_layers.help: The number of top levels of the tree that have fixed buffers (`-num_static_layers`). Unset: the default of the tool, 0.

tree.obstruction_aware.help: Keep the clock buffers off blockages and macros. False passes `-no_obstruction_aware`. The default is the one of the tool.

balance.help: The balance of the clock latencies between macros and registers, and of the loads at the leaves.

balance.delay_buffer_derate.help: The share of the delay buffers that the tool inserts to balance the latencies of macros and registers (`-delay_buffer_derate`). 1 inserts all of them, and 0 inserts none. Needs `insertion_delay`. Unset: the default of the tool, 1.

balance.insertion_delay.help: Take the insertion delay of the sinks (`min_clock_tree_path` and `max_clock_tree_path` in the Liberty file of a macro) into account when the tool builds and balances the tree. False passes `-no_insertion_delay`, and the tool then does not balance the latencies of macros and registers. The default is the one of the tool.

balance.dummy_load.help: Add dummy loads (`clkload` cells) at the leaves of the tree to balance the loads. False passes `-dont_use_dummy_load`. The default is the one of the tool.

ndr.help: The non-default routing rule of the clock nets.

ndr.strategy.help: The clock nets that get the NDR with twice the default spacing (`-apply_ndr`). The leaf nets never get it. `none` applies no rule, `root_only` applies it to the trunk at the root, `half` to the first half of the levels of the tree, and `full` to every level. Unset: the default of the tool, `half`.

characterization.help: The characterization of the clock buffers, from which the tool builds its lookup table.

characterization.max_slew.help: The largest slew that the characterization tests, a time with a unit, such as `250 ps` (`-max_slew`). The flow converts it to seconds, which the command takes. Set it with `max_cap`: the tool uses the limits only when both are set, and takes both from the Liberty files when one is missing. It ignores a single limit without a message (`TechChar.cpp`, seen with OpenROAD v2.0-26132-g6b305a712).

characterization.max_cap.help: The largest capacitance that the characterization tests, a capacitance with a unit, such as `0.1 pF` (`-max_cap`). The flow converts it to farads, which the command takes. Set it with `max_slew`: see there.

characterization.slew_steps.help: The number of steps on the slew axis of the characterization (`-slew_steps`). Unset: the default of the tool, 7. The README of OpenROAD says 12.

characterization.cap_steps.help: The number of steps on the capacitance axis of the characterization (`-cap_steps`). Unset: the default of the tool, 20. The README of OpenROAD says 34.

clock_nets.help: The clock roots to build trees for: nets, or pins that drive a net (`-clk_nets`). A name holds no white space. Empty: the tool finds all clock roots.

skip_nets.help: The nets that the tool leaves out: a clock root skips the whole clock, and a sub-net skips that net (`set_cts_config -skip_nets`). A name is a pattern of `get_nets`.

repair_clock_nets.help: The buffering of the long wire from the clock port to the root buffer.

repair_clock_nets.when.help: `off` leaves the wire as it is. `in_cts` repairs it inside `clock_tree_synthesis` (`-repair_clock_nets`), before the tool balances the latencies. `after` runs `repair_clock_nets` after the clock tree. The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

repair_clock_nets.max_wire_length.help: Buffer each clock wire that is longer than this length, a length with a unit (`repair_clock_nets -max_wire_length`). Needs `when: after`: the repair inside `clock_tree_synthesis` takes no length. Unset or 0: the length that gives the least wire delay for the wire RC.

legalize.help: The legalization of the placement after the clock tree and after the repair.

legalize.cell_padding.help: The empty sites that each cell keeps on its left and on its right (`set_placement_padding -global -left N -right N`), in sites. The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts. Use the value of `detailed_placement.cell_padding` of `openroad_place`, so that both legalizations leave the same space.

legalize.max_displacement.help: The farthest that a cell moves to find a legal site, as two lengths with units, for x and y (`-max_displacement`). The tool takes whole micrometers. Unset: the default of the tool, which sets no limit of its own.

legalize.legalizer.help: The engine that legalizes the placement. `negotiation` is the default of the tool and handles dense designs. `diamond` is the earlier search (`-use_diamond_legalizer`). It is faster, and it cannot handle dense designs.

repair.help: The repair of the timing after the clock tree (`repair_timing`), with propagated clocks. It repairs setup and hold.

repair.enabled.help: Run `repair_timing` at this point of the flow.

repair.fix.help: The checks to repair: `setup`, `hold`, or `setup_and_hold`, which repairs setup first and then hold (`-setup`, `-hold`, or neither).

repair.setup_margin.help: Repair until the setup slack is at least this margin (`-setup_margin`), a time with a unit, such as `50 ps`. The hold repair keeps this margin of setup slack too. The default is the one of the tool and of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

repair.hold_margin.help: Repair until the hold slack is at least this margin (`-hold_margin`), a time with a unit, such as `20 ps`. The default is the one of the tool and of OpenROAD-flow-scripts. Not with `fix: setup`.

repair.allow_setup_violations.help: Let the hold repair insert buffers that cause setup violations (`-allow_setup_violations`). Without it, the repair inserts none of them. Not with `fix: setup`.

repair.tns_end_percent.help: The share of the endpoints with a setup violation that the repair works on, in percent (`-repair_tns`). 0 repairs only the worst path. The default is the one of the tool and of OpenROAD-flow-scripts. Not with `fix: hold`.

repair.sequence.help: The setup moves, in the order that the repair tries them (`-sequence`). Empty: the default sequence of the tool. A move that `moves` switches off must not appear. `reroute` needs the parasitics of a global route. Not with `fix: hold`.

repair.phases.help: The phases of the setup repair, in order (`-phases`). Empty: the default phases of the tool. A phase that its switch turns off (`last_gasp` for `LAST_GASP`, `moves.crit_vt_swap` and `moves.vt_swap` for `CRIT_VT_SWAP`) must not appear. `REROUTE` needs the parasitics of a global route. Not with `fix: hold`.

repair.moves.help: The setup moves that the repair may not use. Not with `fix: hold`.

repair.moves.pin_swap.help: Allow the move that swaps the pins of a gate. False adds `-skip_pin_swap`, since a pin swap changes the connections of the gate.

repair.moves.gate_cloning.help: Allow the move that clones a gate to split its load. False adds `-skip_gate_cloning`, since cloning adds cells.

repair.moves.size_down_fanout.help: Allow the move that sizes down the gates on a net with many loads, off the critical path. False adds `-skip_size_down`. The default sequence of the tool does not use this move, so the switch matters only when `sequence` names `size_down_fanout` or `size`.

repair.moves.buffering.help: Allow the moves that buffer a net again (`buffer`) and that split off the loads behind a buffer (`split`). False adds `-skip_buffering`.

repair.moves.buffer_removal.help: Allow the move that removes a buffer from a critical path. False adds `-skip_buffer_removal`.

repair.moves.buffer_to_inverters.help: Allow the move that replaces a buffer with two inverters. False adds `-skip_buffer_to_inverters`. The default sequence of the tool does not use this move, so the switch matters only when `sequence` names `buffer_to_inverters`.

repair.moves.vt_swap.help: Allow the move that swaps a cell for a cell of another threshold voltage. False adds `-skip_vt_swap`, which also stops the critical swap that ends the repair. The move has an effect only when the library has such cells.

repair.moves.crit_vt_swap.help: Allow the swap of threshold voltage that ends the repair, on the cells of the critical paths. False adds `-skip_crit_vt_swap`. The swap has an effect only when the library has cells of several threshold voltages.

repair.last_gasp.help: Run the last pass of the setup repair, a greedy sizing of the cells. False adds `-skip_last_gasp`, which saves run time and area. Not with `fix: hold`.

repair.crpr.help: Remove the clock reconvergence pessimism from the paths during the repair. False adds `-skip_crpr`, which saves run time at the cost of area and power. The timing that the repair sees then keeps the pessimism.

repair.match_cell_footprint.help: Swap a cell only for a cell with the same footprint in the Liberty file (`-match_cell_footprint`). Unset: the value of the platform.

repair.max_buffer_percent.help: The most hold buffers that the repair inserts, in percent of the cells (`-max_buffer_percent`). Unset: the default of the tool, 20. Needs hold repair: not with `fix: setup`.

repair.max_iterations.help: The most iterations of the setup repair and of the hold repair (`-max_iterations`). Unset: no limit, which is the `-1` of the tool.

repair.max_passes.help: The most passes of one run of the repair (`-max_passes`). The tool calls it an option for debugging. Unset: the default of the tool, 10000.

repair.max_repairs_per_pass.help: The most repairs in one pass on the worst paths (`-max_repairs_per_pass`). The number goes down to 1 for the last violations. Unset: the default of the tool, 1. Not with `fix: hold`.

repair.recover_power_percent.help: Trade positive slack for power on this share of the paths, in percent (`-recover_power`). The command then recovers power and repairs neither setup nor hold, so every other leaf of this call must keep its default, except `match_cell_footprint`. The documentation of OpenROAD advises the parasitics of a global route for it. Unset: no power recovery.

hierarchical.help: Keep the hierarchy of the design: OpenROAD links the netlist with `link_design -hier` and reads each database with `read_db -hier`. The database does not tell how it was read, so every OpenROAD flow of a chain must agree on this setting. It is separate from the hierarchy that `yosys` keeps.

wire_rc.help: Resistance and capacitance of the wires, which replace the values of the platform leaf by leaf: the layers and vias that you list replace the ones of the platform with the same name, and the others stay. The default is the wire RC of the platform. The database stores no wire RC, so every OpenROAD flow of a chain must agree on this setting.

wire_rc.signal_layer.help: Layer whose resistance and capacitance estimate a signal net.

wire_rc.clock_layer.help: Layer whose resistance and capacitance estimate a clock net.

wire_rc.layers.help: Resistance and capacitance per micrometer of each layer, in the units of the library: the units of the Liberty file. On the command line, give a pair as `resistance,capacitance`.

wire_rc.vias.help: Resistance of each via, by via name, in the units of the library: the resistance unit of the Liberty file.

pin_access.help: The `pin_access` command, which finds the access points of the pins before the global route.

pin_access.enabled.help: Run `pin_access` before the global route. OpenROAD-flow-scripts runs it. `detailed_route` finds the access points again if it does not get them from here.

pin_access.process_node.help: The name of a process node that selects via rules of that node (`-db_process_node`). In OpenROAD v2.0-26132 only `GF14_13M_3Mx_2Cx_4Kx_2Hx_2Gx_LB` has an effect. OpenROAD-flow-scripts takes the name from the platform variable `dbProcessNode`. Unset: the flow does not pass the flag.

pin_access.via_access_layer.help: The routing layer up to which the router reaches a pin only through vias (`-via_access_layer`). Unset: the flow does not pass the flag.

pin_access.via_in_pin.help: The range of layers where a via may sit inside a pin (`-via_in_pin_bottom_layer`, `-via_in_pin_top_layer`). Give `detailed_route` the same range. OpenROAD-flow-scripts takes the range from its platform; no platform of the model gives one. Unset: the flow does not pass the flags.

pin_access.via_in_pin.bottom.help: The lowest layer where a via may sit inside a pin (`-via_in_pin_bottom_layer`).

pin_access.via_in_pin.top.help: The highest layer where a via may sit inside a pin (`-via_in_pin_top_layer`).

pin_access.min_access_points.help: The fewest access points to find for each pin (`-min_access_points`). Unset: the default of the tool.

pin_access.verbose.help: The level of the log of the command (`-verbose`). Unset: the default of the tool, 1.

congestion.iterations.help: The number of iterations that remove the overflow (`-congestion_iterations`). Unset: 30, and 10 with `router.engine: cugr`, as OpenROAD-flow-scripts does. The tool uses 50, and 5 with CUGR.

congestion.report_step.help: Write the congestion report every this many iterations (`-congestion_report_iter_step`). 0 writes it at the end only. The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts. The tool uses 0.

congestion.allow.help: Finish the route when overflow remains, and write the result (`-allow_congestion`). The flow gives the flag to every incremental route and to `repair_antennas` too.

congestion.critical_nets_percent.help: The share of the nets with the worst slack that the router routes first when it removes overflow, in percent (`-critical_nets_percentage`). The router estimates the slack from the parasitics of its own route. Unset: the default of the tool.

congestion.macro_extension.help: The halo around each macro in which the router reduces the capacity, in global routing cells (`set_macro_extension`). Unset: the default of the tool, 0. The database does not store it.

congestion.region_adjustments.help: Cuts in the routing capacity of one layer in a region, which spread the routes away from it (`set_global_routing_region_adjustment`). The flow sets them in this process, since the database does not store them.

router.help: The global router: its engine, resistance-aware routing, the random order of the nets, the weights of the Steiner trees and the nets to route.

router.engine.help: The global router. `fastroute` is the default one. `cugr` is the second router of OpenROAD, which its README calls not ready for production (`-use_cugr`). The tool keeps the choice across the incremental routes.

router.resistance_aware.help: Assign layers and route in 3D with the resistance of the wires in mind (`-resistance_aware`). The README of OpenROAD calls it not ready for production. The flow gives the flag to each route that ends an increment too. With CUGR it has an effect only when `congestion.critical_nets_percent` is not 0.

router.res_aware_nets_percent.help: The share of the nets that the router treats resistance-aware, in percent (`-res_aware_nets_percentage`). Unset: the default of the tool, 15. Needs `resistance_aware`.

router.seed.help: The seed that shuffles the order of the nets (`set_global_routing_random -seed`). Unset: the order is fixed. A seed of 0 shuffles nothing, so the setting refuses it. The database does not store the seed.

router.capacity_perturbation_percent.help: The share of the edges whose capacity the router changes at random, in percent (`-capacities_perturbation_percentage`). Unset: the default of the tool, 0. Needs `seed`. OpenROAD v2.0-26132 stops with signal 11 in `perturbCapacities` for 5 percent on a design of 72 nets, and runs with 1 percent. No upstream issue exists.

router.perturbation_amount.help: By how much the router changes the capacity of such an edge (`-perturbation_amount`). Unset: the default of the tool, 1. Needs `seed`.

router.steiner_alphas.help: The weights of the Steiner tree builder, one call of `set_routing_alpha` each, in order. The tool has a default for all nets. The database does not store them.

router.batch_width.help: The most batches in a wave of the batched routing (`-snapshot_batched_width`). The README of OpenROAD advises it for exploration only. Unset: no batching. Only the default router uses it.

router.grid_origin.help: The origin of the routing grid, two lengths with units: x, y (`-grid_origin`, which takes database units: the flow converts). The flow gives it to every route, because the tool resets the origin at each call without it, and the origin shifts the guides that the call writes. Unset: the origin of the die.

router.skip_fanout_above.help: Give no route to a net with more pins than this (`-skip_large_fanout_nets`). The detailed router skips it too. The README of OpenROAD advises it for estimation flows. Unset: no limit. In OpenROAD v2.0-26132, a net without a route stops the following steps: `repair_design` ends with signal 11 in `getPinGridPositions`, and `check_antennas` stops with ANT-0008 where `repair.strategy` is `none`. It was seen with a design of 72 nets. No upstream issue exists.

router.only_nets.help: Route only these nets, by name or pattern (`set_nets_to_route`). The other nets get no guides, so the detailed router leaves them open. For debugging. Empty: every net. A net without a route stops the following steps in OpenROAD v2.0-26132: `repair_design` ends with signal 11 in `getPinGridPositions`. It was seen with a design of 72 nets. No upstream issue exists.

legalize.help: The legalization of the placement after each repair of the route.

legalize.cell_padding.help: The empty sites that each cell keeps on its left and on its right (`set_placement_padding -global -left N -right N`), in sites. The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts. Use the value of `detailed_placement.cell_padding` of `openroad_place`, so that both legalizations leave the same space.

legalize.max_displacement.help: The farthest that a cell moves to find a legal site, as two lengths with units, for x and y (`-max_displacement`). The tool takes whole micrometers. Unset: the default of the tool, which sets no limit of its own.

legalize.legalizer.help: The engine that legalizes the placement. `negotiation` is the default of the tool and handles dense designs. `diamond` is the earlier search (`-use_diamond_legalizer`). It is faster, and it cannot handle dense designs.

repair.help: The repair of the design after the global route.

repair.strategy.help: `none` runs no repair after the route. `incremental` runs `repair_design` and `repair_timing`, with an incremental global route and a legalization around each of them. The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

repair.wns_polish.help: After the repair, run one more `repair_timing -setup -sequence "vt_swap reroute"` on the worst paths. Unset: the value of the platform (`opt_post_grt_wns`, a switch), and on where the platform gives none, as in OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

repair.recover_power_percent.help: Trade positive slack for power on this share of the paths, in percent (`repair_timing -recover_power`). Unset: no power recovery. The flow runs the recovery only without the WNS polish.

repair.design.help: The call of `repair_design` after the route.

repair.design.enabled.help: Run `repair_design` at this point of the flow.

repair.design.slew_margin_percent.help: Repair the slew with this margin, in percent of the limit (`-slew_margin`). The default is the one of the tool and of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

repair.design.cap_margin_percent.help: Repair the capacitance with this margin, in percent of the limit (`-cap_margin`). The default is the one of the tool and of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

repair.design.max_wire_length.help: Buffer each wire that is longer than this length, a length with a unit (`-max_wire_length`). Unset: the flow does not pass the flag.

repair.design.match_cell_footprint.help: Swap a cell only for a cell with the same footprint in the Liberty file (`-match_cell_footprint`). Unset: the value of the platform.

repair.design.reroute.help: Reroute wires with resistance-aware routing to fix slew violations (`-reroute`). The tool calls it experimental. It needs the parasitics of a global route, so only the call after global routing accepts it.

repair.timing.help: The call of `repair_timing` after the route. It repairs setup and hold.

repair.timing.enabled.help: Run `repair_timing` at this point of the flow.

repair.timing.fix.help: The checks to repair: `setup`, `hold`, or `setup_and_hold`, which repairs setup first and then hold (`-setup`, `-hold`, or neither).

repair.timing.setup_margin.help: Repair until the setup slack is at least this margin (`-setup_margin`), a time with a unit, such as `50 ps`. The hold repair keeps this margin of setup slack too. The default is the one of the tool and of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

repair.timing.hold_margin.help: Repair until the hold slack is at least this margin (`-hold_margin`), a time with a unit, such as `20 ps`. The default is the one of the tool and of OpenROAD-flow-scripts. Not with `fix: setup`.
