repair.timing.allow_setup_violations.help: Let the hold repair insert buffers that cause setup violations (`-allow_setup_violations`). Without it, the repair inserts none of them. Not with `fix: setup`.

repair.timing.tns_end_percent.help: The share of the endpoints with a setup violation that the repair works on, in percent (`-repair_tns`). 0 repairs only the worst path. The default is the one of the tool and of OpenROAD-flow-scripts. Not with `fix: hold`.

repair.timing.sequence.help: The setup moves, in the order that the repair tries them (`-sequence`). Empty: the default sequence of the tool. A move that `moves` switches off must not appear. `reroute` needs the parasitics of a global route. Not with `fix: hold`.

repair.timing.phases.help: The phases of the setup repair, in order (`-phases`). Empty: the default phases of the tool. A phase that its switch turns off (`last_gasp` for `LAST_GASP`, `moves.crit_vt_swap` and `moves.vt_swap` for `CRIT_VT_SWAP`) must not appear. `REROUTE` needs the parasitics of a global route. Not with `fix: hold`.

repair.timing.moves.help: The setup moves that the repair may not use. Not with `fix: hold`.

repair.timing.moves.pin_swap.help: Allow the move that swaps the pins of a gate. False adds `-skip_pin_swap`, since a pin swap changes the connections of the gate.

repair.timing.moves.gate_cloning.help: Allow the move that clones a gate to split its load. False adds `-skip_gate_cloning`, since cloning adds cells.

repair.timing.moves.size_down_fanout.help: Allow the move that sizes down the gates on a net with many loads, off the critical path. False adds `-skip_size_down`. The default sequence of the tool does not use this move, so the switch matters only when `sequence` names `size_down_fanout` or `size`.

repair.timing.moves.buffering.help: Allow the moves that buffer a net again (`buffer`) and that split off the loads behind a buffer (`split`). False adds `-skip_buffering`.

repair.timing.moves.buffer_removal.help: Allow the move that removes a buffer from a critical path. False adds `-skip_buffer_removal`.

repair.timing.moves.buffer_to_inverters.help: Allow the move that replaces a buffer with two inverters. False adds `-skip_buffer_to_inverters`. The default sequence of the tool does not use this move, so the switch matters only when `sequence` names `buffer_to_inverters`.

repair.timing.moves.vt_swap.help: Allow the move that swaps a cell for a cell of another threshold voltage. False adds `-skip_vt_swap`, which also stops the critical swap that ends the repair. The move has an effect only when the library has such cells.

repair.timing.moves.crit_vt_swap.help: Allow the swap of threshold voltage that ends the repair, on the cells of the critical paths. False adds `-skip_crit_vt_swap`. The swap has an effect only when the library has cells of several threshold voltages.

repair.timing.last_gasp.help: Run the last pass of the setup repair, a greedy sizing of the cells. False adds `-skip_last_gasp`, which saves run time and area. Not with `fix: hold`.

repair.timing.crpr.help: Remove the clock reconvergence pessimism from the paths during the repair. False adds `-skip_crpr`, which saves run time at the cost of area and power. The timing that the repair sees then keeps the pessimism.

repair.timing.match_cell_footprint.help: Swap a cell only for a cell with the same footprint in the Liberty file (`-match_cell_footprint`). Unset: the value of the platform.

repair.timing.max_buffer_percent.help: The most hold buffers that the repair inserts, in percent of the cells (`-max_buffer_percent`). Unset: the default of the tool, 20. Needs hold repair: not with `fix: setup`.

repair.timing.max_iterations.help: The most iterations of the setup repair and of the hold repair (`-max_iterations`). Unset: no limit, which is the `-1` of the tool.

repair.timing.max_passes.help: The most passes of one run of the repair (`-max_passes`). The tool calls it an option for debugging. Unset: the default of the tool, 10000.

repair.timing.max_repairs_per_pass.help: The most repairs in one pass on the worst paths (`-max_repairs_per_pass`). The number goes down to 1 for the last violations. Unset: the default of the tool, 1. Not with `fix: hold`.

repair.timing.recover_power_percent.help: Trade positive slack for power on this share of the paths, in percent (`-recover_power`). The command then recovers power and repairs neither setup nor hold, so every other leaf of this call must keep its default, except `match_cell_footprint`. The documentation of OpenROAD advises the parasitics of a global route for it. Unset: no power recovery.

antenna.help: The repair of the antenna violations of the global route.

antenna.repair.help: Run `repair_antennas` after the route. OpenROAD-flow-scripts runs it. The flow skips the command, with a note in the log, when the platform says that the router cannot use its diode. The check of the antenna violations runs in every case.

antenna.iterations.help: The most passes of `repair_antennas` (`-iterations`). The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

antenna.method.help: How `repair_antennas` fixes a violation. `diode` inserts diodes only (`-diode_only`), `jumper` moves wire to a higher layer only (`-jumper_only`), and `both` tries jumpers and then diodes. The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts, which names neither flag. The command reads the diffusion area of the diode to judge a violation, with every method, so a platform without a usable diode skips it.

antenna.ratio_margin_percent.help: Repair a violation when the antenna ratio comes within this share of its limit, in percent (`-ratio_margin`). The margin costs area. Unset: the default of the tool, 0.

antenna.diode_cell.help: The diode cell that `repair_antennas` inserts. Unset: the antenna cell of the platform. A cell named here is used even where the platform says that the router cannot use its diode.

verbose.help: Verbosity level. Higher values make the tools more talkative.

debug.help: Run the flow in debug mode: verbose logging, and exceptions are re-raised instead of being reported as a failure.

quiet.help: Run the flow quietly, unless `verbose` or `debug` is set.

redirect_stdout.help: Redirect stdout from execution of tools to files.

lib_paths.help: Additional libraries, as a list of (name, path) tuples. The name or the path can be none, but not both. GHDL and NVC take a relative path as relative to the design root.

docker.help: Run the tools in this Docker image, instead of the default image of the flow.

print_commands.help: Print the commands that the flow runs.

console_colors.help: Colorize tool output on the console.

clocks.help: Clock constraints of the design, by clock name.

clocks.*.period.help: Clock period, a time with a unit, such as `10 ns`. Specify `period` or `freq`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

clocks.*.rise.help: Time of the rising edge of the clock, a time with a unit, such as `0.5 ns`.

clocks.*.uncertainty.help: Clock uncertainty, a time with a unit, such as `0.1 ns`.

clocks.*.skew.help: Clock skew, a time with a unit, such as `0.05 ns`.

clocks.*.port.help: The design port of the clock.

clocks.*.freq.help: Clock frequency, a frequency with a unit, such as `100 MHz`. Specify `freq` or `period`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

platform.help: Name of a bundled ASIC platform (see `xeda list-platforms`). It names the standard cell library and the technology files that the flow works on. Give `platform_file` for a platform that Xeda does not ship; then `platform` can be left out, and if given it must be the `name` of that file.

platform_file.help: Residue file of a platform (YAML). A file that sets `extends` to a bundled platform changes only what it gives. A file without `extends` is a complete platform. A relative path is relative to the design root.

corner.help: Name of the corner of the platform, or one of its aliases. The default is the default corner of the platform. A flow works on one corner: a list of corners is refused.

liberty.help: Standard cell (Liberty) libraries that the flow reads for mapping and timing, instead of the Liberty files of the corner of the platform. Xeda reads each file as it is (`yosys` gives each to `dfflibmap` and to `abc`). Without them, the flow uses the Liberty files of the platform. The platform still gives everything else, and its files must be installed. The files of a producer and its consumer agree, in the same order.

library.help: Standard cell (Liberty) libraries that the flow reads for mapping and timing, instead of the Liberty files of the corner of the platform. Xeda reads each file as it is (`yosys` gives each to `dfflibmap` and to `abc`). Without them, the flow uses the Liberty files of the platform. The platform still gives everything else, and its files must be installed. The files of a producer and its consumer agree, in the same order.

dont_use_cells.help: Standard cells that the flow must not use, in addition to the cells that the platform lists. The default is none.

pdk_provider.help: Where the PDK files of the platform come from. `orfs`: a sparse checkout of OpenROAD-flow-scripts. `ciel`: a PDK build that `ciel` installs. `lambdapdk`: a sparse checkout of lambdapdk. `directory`: a directory that holds the files in a known layout. The default is the provider that the platform names; the platform must have an entry for the provider.

pdk_version.help: Version of the PDK files: the commit (`orfs`, `lambdapdk`) or the hash (`ciel`). For `directory`, a version that Xeda checks against the directory when it can, and `unpinned` when you give none. The default is the version that the platform pins for `pdk_provider`. The version is part of the identity of the run.

pdk_root.help: Directory of the PDK store. `None` means `~/.ciel`. Variables such as `$HOME` expand in it, and a relative path is relative to the design root. It tells where the files are, so it is no part of the identity of the run: the run depends on the content of the files it reads.

hierarchical.help: Keep the hierarchy of the design: OpenROAD links the netlist with `link_design -hier` and reads each database with `read_db -hier`. The database does not tell how it was read, so every OpenROAD flow of a chain must agree on this setting. It is separate from the hierarchy that `yosys` keeps.

wire_rc.help: Resistance and capacitance of the wires, which replace the values of the platform leaf by leaf: the layers and vias that you list replace the ones of the platform with the same name, and the others stay. The default is the wire RC of the platform. The database stores no wire RC, so every OpenROAD flow of a chain must agree on this setting.

wire_rc.signal_layer.help: Layer whose resistance and capacitance estimate a signal net.

wire_rc.clock_layer.help: Layer whose resistance and capacitance estimate a clock net.

wire_rc.layers.help: Resistance and capacitance per micrometer of each layer, in the units of the library: the units of the Liberty file. On the command line, give a pair as `resistance,capacitance`.

wire_rc.vias.help: Resistance of each via, by via name, in the units of the library: the resistance unit of the Liberty file.

input_delay_frac.help: The input delay of the generated constraints, as a fraction of the clock period, from 0 up to but not including 1. Used only when `input_delay` is unset.

output_delay_frac.help: The output delay of the generated constraints, as a fraction of the clock period, from 0 up to but not including 1. Used only when `output_delay` is unset.

input_delay.help: The input delay of the generated constraints, a time with a unit, such as `100 ps`. The flow converts it to the time unit of the platform. It takes precedence over `input_delay_frac`.

output_delay.help: The output delay of the generated constraints, a time with a unit, such as `100 ps`. The flow converts it to the time unit of the platform. It takes precedence over `output_delay_frac`.

sdc_files.help: More SDC files. The flow reads them after the constraints that it generates from `clocks`. A relative path is relative to the design root.

design.eliminate_dead_logic.help: Remove the standard cells that drive no output (`eliminate_dead_logic`) after the flow reads the netlist. OpenROAD-flow-scripts runs it before it writes the first database.

design.dont_touch.help: The instances and nets that the resizer must not change (`set_dont_touch`). Each item is a name or a glob pattern. The database stores the setting, so the later flows keep it.

floorplan.help: The size and the shape of the floorplan, and the cleanup of the netlist before the placement.

floorplan.sizing.help: How the floorplan gets its size. `utilization` computes the core from the area of the netlist, with `core_utilization_percent`, `aspect_ratio` and `core_margin`. `area` takes the die and the core from `die_area` and `core_area`. `def` takes the die, the core, the rows and the tracks from the file `def_file`.

floorplan.core_utilization_percent.help: The share of the core that the cells fill, in percent (`-utilization`). OpenROAD-flow-scripts leaves it to the design. The default is a middle value, not a tuned one. Needs `sizing: utilization`.

floorplan.aspect_ratio.help: The height of the core divided by its width (`-aspect_ratio`). Needs `sizing: utilization`.

floorplan.core_margin.help: The space between the core and the die (`-core_space`), lengths with units, such as `1 um`. One distance for all sides, or four: bottom, top, left, right. The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts. Needs `sizing: utilization`.

floorplan.die_area.help: The die, as lengths with units: a rectangle as 4 lengths (lower-left x, lower-left y, upper-right x, upper-right y), or a polygon as 8 or more lengths, the x and y of each corner in turn (`-die_area`). Needs `sizing: area`, and `core_area` too. OpenROAD needs both outlines to be polygons or both rectangles. A polygon has limits: the documentation of the power grid generator (`pdngen`) says it assumes a rectangular design, and `global_placement -place_ios` does not support a polygon die.

floorplan.core_area.help: The core, written as `die_area` (`-core_area`). A rectangle must lie inside the die. Needs `sizing: area`, and `die_area` too. A polygon has the limits of `die_area` for `pdngen` and for `global_placement -place_ios`.

floorplan.def_file.help: The DEF file that gives the die, the core, the rows and the tracks (`read_def -floorplan_initialize`). A relative path is relative to the design root. Needs `sizing: def`.

floorplan.site.help: The site of the rows (`-site`). Needs `sizing: utilization` or `sizing: area`. Unset: the value of the platform.

floorplan.additional_sites.help: More sites to make rows for (`-additional_sites`), for example for cells of double height. Needs `sizing: utilization` or `sizing: area`.

floorplan.flip_sites.help: The sites whose rows start flipped (`-flip_sites`), for cells of mixed height whose power pin sits on another side. No platform gives them. Needs `sizing: utilization` or `sizing: area`.

floorplan.row_parity.help: Force the number of rows to be odd or even (`-row_parity`). `none` leaves it free, which is the default of the tool. Needs `sizing: utilization` or `sizing: area`.

floorplan.row_gap.help: The space between the rows of two power domains, a length with a unit (`-gap`). Unset: the tool uses 6 times the least height of a site. Needs `sizing: utilization` or `sizing: area`.

floorplan.tracks.help: Where the routing tracks come from. `platform` makes the tracks that the platform lists, layer by layer. `from_tech` runs `make_tracks`, which takes the pitch of each layer from the LEF files. Unset: the tracks of the platform if it lists any, else those of the LEF files.

floorplan.placement_blockages.help: The regions where the placement keeps cells away (`create_blockage`). The database stores them.

floorplan.routing_blockages.help: The regions where the router keeps wires out (`create_obstruction`). The database stores them.

floorplan.check_setup.help: Report the unconstrained endpoints, the loops and the missing clocks (`check_setup`) before the floorplan. OpenROAD-flow-scripts runs it. It only reports.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.help: The cleanup of the netlist before the placement.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.mode.help: `repair_timing` repairs the setup with the options of `repair`. `remove_buffers` removes the buffers of the synthesis (`remove_buffers`). `none` cleans nothing. The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.repair.help: The options of the repair of the netlist. They act with `mode: repair_timing` only. To run no repair, set `mode: none`.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.repair.enabled.help: Run `repair_timing` at this point of the flow.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.repair.fix.help: The checks to repair: `setup`, `hold`, or `setup_and_hold`, which repairs setup first and then hold (`-setup`, `-hold`, or neither). The cleanup of the netlist repairs setup only. It runs before the placement, without parasitics.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.repair.setup_m.help: Repair until the setup slack is at least this margin (`-setup_margin`), a time with a unit, such as `50 ps`. The hold repair keeps this margin of setup slack too. The default is the one of the tool and of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.repair.hold_ma.help: Repair until the hold slack is at least this margin (`-hold_margin`), a time with a unit, such as `20 ps`. The default is the one of the tool and of OpenROAD-flow-scripts. Not with `fix: setup`.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.repair.allow_s.help: Let the hold repair insert buffers that cause setup violations (`-allow_setup_violations`). Without it, the repair inserts none of them. Not with `fix: setup`.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.repair.tns_end.help: The share of the endpoints with a setup violation that the repair works on, in percent (`-repair_tns`). 0 repairs only the worst path. The default is the one of the tool and of OpenROAD-flow-scripts. Not with `fix: hold`.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.repair.sequenc.help: The setup moves, in the order that the repair tries them (`-sequence`). Empty: the default sequence of the tool. A move that `moves` switches off must not appear. `reroute` needs the parasitics of a global route. Not with `fix: hold`. The default is the sequence of OpenROAD-flow-scripts at the floorplan.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.repair.phases.help: The phases of the setup repair, in order (`-phases`). Empty: the default phases of the tool. A phase that its switch turns off (`last_gasp` for `LAST_GASP`, `moves.crit_vt_swap` and `moves.vt_swap` for `CRIT_VT_SWAP`) must not appear. `REROUTE` needs the parasitics of a global route. Not with `fix: hold`.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.repair.moves.help: The setup moves that the repair may not use. Not with `fix: hold`.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.repair.moves.p.help: Allow the move that swaps the pins of a gate. False adds `-skip_pin_swap`, since a pin swap changes the connections of the gate.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.repair.moves.g.help: Allow the move that clones a gate to split its load. False adds `-skip_gate_cloning`, since cloning adds cells.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.repair.moves.s.help: Allow the move that sizes down the gates on a net with many loads, off the critical path. False adds `-skip_size_down`. The default sequence of the tool does not use this move, so the switch matters only when `sequence` names `size_down_fanout` or `size`.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.repair.moves.b.help: Allow the moves that buffer a net again (`buffer`) and that split off the loads behind a buffer (`split`). False adds `-skip_buffering`.
Allow the move that removes a buffer from a critical path. False adds `-skip_buffer_removal`.

Allow the move that replaces a buffer with two inverters. False adds `-skip_buffer_to_inverters`. The default sequence of the tool does not use this move, so the switch matters only when `sequence` names `buffer_to_inverters`.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.repair.moves.v.help: Allow the move that swaps a cell for a cell of another threshold voltage. False adds `-skip_vt_swap`, which also stops the critical swap that ends the repair. The move has an effect only when the library has such cells.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.repair.moves.c.help: Allow the swap of threshold voltage that ends the repair, on the cells of the critical paths. False adds `-skip_crit_vt_swap`. The swap has an effect only when the library has cells of several threshold voltages.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.repair.last_ga.help: Run the last pass of the setup repair, a greedy sizing of the cells. False adds `-skip_last_gasp`, which saves run time and area. Not with `fix: hold`. The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts at the floorplan.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.repair.crpr.help: Remove the clock reconvergence pessimism from the paths during the repair. False adds `-skip_crpr`, which saves run time at the cost of area and power. The timing that the repair sees then keeps the pessimism.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.repair.match_c.help: Swap a cell only for a cell with the same footprint in the Liberty file (`-match_cell_footprint`). Unset: the value of the platform.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.repair.max_buf.help: The most hold buffers that the repair inserts, in percent of the cells (`-max_buffer_percent`). Unset: the default of the tool, 20. Needs hold repair: not with `fix: setup`.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.repair.max_ite.help: The most iterations of the setup repair and of the hold repair (`-max_iterations`). Unset: no limit, which is the `-1` of the tool.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.repair.max_pas.help: The most passes of one run of the repair (`-max_passes`). The tool calls it an option for debugging. Unset: the default of the tool, 10000.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.repair.max_rep.help: The most repairs in one pass on the worst paths (`-max_repairs_per_pass`). The number goes down to 1 for the last violations. Unset: the default of the tool, 1. Not with `fix: hold`.

floorplan.netlist_cleanup.repair.recover.help: Trade positive slack for power on this share of the paths, in percent (`-recover_power`). The command then recovers power and repairs neither setup nor hold, so every other leaf of this call must keep its default, except `match_cell_footprint`. The documentation of OpenROAD advises the parasitics of a global route for it. Unset: no power recovery.

routing.help: The routing layers and the capacity of each layer. The database stores them, so the later flows keep them.

routing.signal_layers.help: The lowest and the highest layer for signal nets, written `min-max` (`set_routing_layers -signal`). Unset: the value of the platform.

routing.clock_layers.help: The lowest and the highest layer for clock nets, written `min-max` (`set_routing_layers -clock`). Unset: the value of the platform.

routing.layer_adjustments.help: The share of the routing capacity to keep free, from 0 to 1, by layer or layer range such as `metal2-metal3` (`set_global_routing_layer_adjustment`). Unset: the value of the platform.

tie.help: The tie cells that drive the constant nets.

tie.repair_fanout.help: Give each load of a tie cell its own copy of the cell (`repair_tie_fanout`). OpenROAD-flow-scripts runs it, before the removal of buffers.

tie.separation.help: The distance between a tie cell and its load, a length with a unit (`repair_tie_fanout -separation`). The default is the one of the tool and of OpenROAD-flow-scripts. Needs `repair_fanout`.

tie.max_fanout.help: The most loads for one copy of a tie cell (`repair_tie_fanout -max_fanout`). Unset: the flag is not passed. OpenROAD v2.0-26132 reads the value and does not pass it to the repair, so it has no effect there. No upstream issue exists yet. Needs `repair_fanout`.

tie.insert_cells.help: Insert a tie cell for each net that the netlist ties to a constant (`insert_tiecells`), before the repair of the fanout. The synthesis of xeda puts the tie cells in the netlist, so OpenROAD-flow-scripts does not run this.

tapcell.help: The well tap cells and the end cap cells.

tapcell.mode.help: `tap_endcap` places tap cells and end caps (`tapcell`). `cut_rows` cuts the rows around obstructions, without tap cells (`cut_rows`). `none` does neither. Unset: the value of the platform.

tapcell.distance.help: The distance between the tap cells in a row, a length with a unit (`tapcell -distance`). Needs `mode: tap_endcap`. Unset: the value of the platform.

tapcell.master.help: The tap cell (`tapcell -tapcell_master`). Needs `mode: tap_endcap`. Unset: the value of the platform.

tapcell.endcap_master.help: The end cap cell (`-endcap_master` of `tapcell` and of `cut_rows`). Needs `mode: tap_endcap` or `mode: cut_rows`. Unset: the value of the platform.

tapcell.row_min_width.help: Remove the pieces of a row that are narrower than this, a length with a unit (`-row_min_width` of `tapcell` and of `cut_rows`). They would be islands that the router cannot reach. Needs `mode: tap_endcap` or `mode: cut_rows`. Unset: the tool uses twice the width of the end cap, or 0 without an end cap.

tapcell.row_min_height.help: The least height of a stack of rows, a length with a unit (`-row_min_height` of `tapcell` and of `cut_rows`). Needs `mode: tap_endcap` or `mode: cut_rows`. Unset: the tool uses twice the height of the end cap plus the height of the tallest cell.

tapcell.nwell_masters.help: The tap cells by the kind of n-well. The platform gives none of them.

tapcell.nwell_masters.nwin2.help: The cell for a two-site tap with the n-well inside (`tapcell -tap_nwin2_master`). Needs `tapcell.mode: tap_endcap`. Unset: the flag is not passed.

tapcell.nwell_masters.nwin3.help: The cell for a three-site tap with the n-well inside (`tapcell -tap_nwin3_master`). Needs `tapcell.mode: tap_endcap`. Unset: the flag is not passed.

tapcell.nwell_masters.nwintie.help: The cell for a tie tap with the n-well inside (`tapcell -tap_nwintie_master`). Needs `tapcell.mode: tap_endcap`. Unset: the flag is not passed.

tapcell.nwell_masters.nwout2.help: The cell for a two-site tap with the n-well outside (`tapcell -tap_nwout2_master`). Needs `tapcell.mode: tap_endcap`. Unset: the flag is not passed.

tapcell.nwell_masters.nwout3.help: The cell for a three-site tap with the n-well outside (`tapcell -tap_nwout3_master`). Needs `tapcell.mode: tap_endcap`. Unset: the flag is not passed.

tapcell.nwell_masters.nwouttie.help: The cell for a tie tap with the n-well outside (`tapcell -tap_nwouttie_master`). Needs `tapcell.mode: tap_endcap`. Unset: the flag is not passed.

tapcell.corner_masters.help: The corner cells by the kind of n-well. The platform gives none of them.

tapcell.corner_masters.nwin.help: The cell for an outer corner with the n-well inside (`tapcell -cnrcap_nwin_master`). Needs `tapcell.mode: tap_endcap`. Unset: the flag is not passed.

tapcell.corner_masters.nwout.help: The cell for an outer corner with the n-well outside (`tapcell -cnrcap_nwout_master`). Needs `tapcell.mode: tap_endcap`. Unset: the flag is not passed.

tapcell.corner_masters.inner_nwin.help: The cell for an inner corner with the n-well inside (`tapcell -incnrcap_nwin_master`). Needs `tapcell.mode: tap_endcap`. Unset: the flag is not passed.

tapcell.corner_masters.inner_nwout.help: The cell for an inner corner with the n-well outside (`tapcell -incnrcap_nwout_master`). Needs `tapcell.mode: tap_endcap`. Unset: the flag is not passed.

pdn.help: The power grid over the standard cells.

pdn.mode.help: `generated` builds the grid from `grid`, or from the grid of the platform. `none` builds no grid.

pdn.grid.help: The grid: the supply nets, the connections of the pins to them, the rails, the straps, the rings, the pairs of layers that the vias connect, and the layers of the pins. Each leaf that you give, and that is not empty, replaces the same leaf of the grid of the platform. Needs `mode: generated`. Unset: the grid of the platform.

pdn.grid.global_connects.help: Connections of the pins of the instances to the nets.

pdn.grid.rails.help: Rails that follow the rows of cells. Each has a layer and a width, and may have a pitch and an offset, as lengths with units.

pdn.grid.straps.help: Stripes of the grid, with their options.

pdn.grid.connects.help: The vias between layers: a pair of layers, or an object with the layers and the options of the vias. If you replace the layers of `rails` or `straps`, give `connects` too, since the connections of the platform name its layers.

pdn.grid.pin_layers.help: Layers of the pins that connect to the grid.

pdn.grid.rings.help: Rings around the core. The platform gives none.

pdn.grid.starts_with.help: Whether the first stripe of the grid is power or ground (`define_pdn_grid -starts_with`). Unset: the tool starts with ground.

pdn.secondary_power.help: The secondary power nets of the voltage domain (`set_voltage_domain -secondary_power`). Needs `mode: generated`.

pdn.block_pins.help: Promote the straps of the layers in `grid.pin_layers` to pins of the block. False adds `-dont_add_pins` to `pdngen`, which makes no pins at all. Needs `mode: generated`.

pdn.skip_trim.help: Keep the metal stubs that the generator would remove (`pdngen -skip_trim`). Needs `mode: generated`.

pdn.check.help: The check of the grid after it is built.

pdn.check.mode.help: `off` runs no check. `warn` runs `check_power_grid` on the power net and the ground net and logs a warning when it fails. `fail` stops the flow when it fails. OpenROAD-flow-scripts runs no check.

pdn.check.require_terminals.help: Require that the grid reaches a terminal of the design (a pin or a pad). False passes `-dont_require_terminals`: a design without pads has no terminal on its power nets, and the check stops with PSM-0025 without that flag. Needs `mode` `warn` or `fail`.

io.help: The placement of the pins of the design.

io.flow.help: How the pins get their places. `skip_io_pass` places the cells without the pins first, then places the pins, then places the cells again. `concurrent` places the pins together with the cells (`global_placement -place_ios`), and the global placement legalizes them with the pin placer. `concurrent` gives the layers, `min_distance`, `min_distance_tracks` and `corner_avoidance` to `set_place_config` (the `-io_pin_` options) and needs OpenROAD 26Q4-11 or later, which has that command. It does not take `algorithm: annealing`. `fixed` keeps the pins that the floorplan already placed: it needs a DEF file with placed pins (`floorplan.sizing: def`) or `fixed_pins`, else the global placement stops with GPL-0326 on the unplaced pins. With `floorplan.sizing: def` the pins of the DEF file stay, except with `concurrent`. The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

io.horizontal_layers.help: The layers of the pins on the horizontal edges (`-hor_layers`). Unset: the value of the platform.

io.vertical_layers.help: The layers of the pins on the vertical edges (`-ver_layers`). Unset: the value of the platform.

io.min_distance.help: The smallest distance between two pins, a length with a unit (`-min_distance`). Not with `min_distance_tracks`. Unset: the default of the tool, 2 tracks.

io.min_distance_tracks.help: The smallest distance between two pins, in routing tracks (`-min_distance_in_tracks -min_distance`). OpenROAD takes a whole number of tracks. Not with `min_distance`. Unset: the default of the tool, 2 tracks.

io.corner_avoidance.help: The distance that the pins keep from the corners of the die, a length with a unit (`-corner_avoidance`). Unset: the default of the tool, 0.

io.algorithm.help: How the pins get their slots. `matching` assigns them with the Hungarian method, which is the default of the tool. `annealing` uses simulated annealing (`-annealing`), set by `annealing`. Only `flow: skip_io_pass` takes `annealing`.

io.annealing.help: The schedule of the simulated annealing. Needs `algorithm: annealing`, which needs `flow: skip_io_pass`.

io.annealing.temperature.help: The start temperature (`-temperature`). Unset: the default of the tool, 1.0.

io.annealing.max_iterations.help: The most iterations (`-max_iterations`). Unset: the default of the tool, 2000.

io.annealing.perturb_per_iter.help: The moves that each iteration tries (`-perturb_per_iter`). Unset: the tool derives the number from the number of pins.

io.annealing.alpha.help: The factor that lowers the temperature after each iteration, above 0 and up to 1 (`-alpha`). Unset: the default of the tool, 0.985.

io.exclude.help: The parts of the edges where no pin may sit (`exclude_io_pin_region`, one `-region` for each item).

io.groups.help: Pins that the pin placer puts next to each other. A group may be ordered and may keep to a part of an edge. A pin belongs to one group, else the tool stops (PPL-0104).

io.constraints.help: Pins, named or chosen by their direction, that the pin placer keeps to a part of an edge (`set_io_pin_constraint -region`).

io.mirrored_pins.help: Pairs of pins that the pin placer puts at mirrored places of opposite edges (`set_io_pin_constraint -mirrored_pins`). With `algorithm: matching`, OpenROAD v2.0-26132 can put another pin on the place that a mirrored pin takes, and the placement stops with PPL-0107 (seen on 3 of 4 trials on a netlist of 5 cells and 8 pins). `annealing` (only with `flow: skip_io_pass`) placed the pins in all of them. No upstream issue exists.

io.fixed_pins.help: Pins that the flow places by hand (`place_pin`) before any placement. They stay where they are. This works with every `flow` and with a floorplan from a DEF file.

io.pin_length.help: The length of the pin shapes.

io.pin_length.horizontal.help: The length of the pins on the horizontal edges, a length with a unit (`-hor_length`). Unset: the shortest length that meets the minimum area of the layer.

io.pin_length.vertical.help: The length of the pins on the vertical edges, a length with a unit (`-ver_length`). Unset: the shortest length that meets the minimum area of the layer.

io.pin_extension.help: How far the pin shapes stick out of the die.

io.pin_extension.horizontal.help: The extension of the pins on the horizontal edges, a length with a unit (`-hor_extension`). Unset: the default of the tool, 0.

io.pin_extension.vertical.help: The extension of the pins on the vertical edges, a length with a unit (`-ver_extension`). Unset: the default of the tool, 0.

io.pin_thickness.help: The width of the pin shapes.

io.pin_thickness.horizontal.help: The multiplier for the pins on the horizontal edges (`-hor_multiplier`). Unset: the default of the tool, 1.

io.pin_thickness.vertical.help: The multiplier for the pins on the vertical edges (`-ver_multiplier`). Unset: the default of the tool, 1.

global_placement.help: The global placement of the cells.

global_placement.density.mode.help: `fixed` uses `value`, or the density of the platform when `value` is unset (`-density`). `auto` computes the density from the design: the uniform density of the netlist, plus `headroom` of the space that is left. `uniform` uses the uniform density of the netlist (`-density uniform`). The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts without a headroom.

global_placement.density.value.help: The target density, from 0 to 1. Needs `mode: fixed`. Unset: the value of the platform.

global_placement.density.headroom.help: The share of the free space above the uniform density that the target adds, from 0 to 0.99. Needs `mode: auto`, and `mode: auto` needs it.

global_placement.cell_padding.help: The empty sites that each cell keeps on its left and on its right during the placement (`-pad_left`, `-pad_right`), in sites. The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

global_placement.timing_driven.enabled.help: Weight the nets by their slack during the placement (`-timing_driven`). The mode needs clocks in the SDC and the wire RC. It costs run time. The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

global_placement.timing_driven.reweight_.help: The overflows, in percent, at which the placement computes the net weights again (`-timing_driven_net_reweight_overflow`). Fewer values save run time. Unset: the default of the tool, 64 and 20.

global_placement.timing_driven.net_weigh.help: The weight of the most critical nets, as a multiple (`-timing_driven_net_weight_max`). Unset: the default of the tool, 5.

global_placement.timing_driven.nets_perc.help: The share of the nets that get a new weight, in percent (`-timing_driven_nets_percentage`). Unset: the default of the tool, 10.

global_placement.timing_driven.keep_resi.help: Below this overflow, from 0 to 1, the changes that the resizer makes inside the placement stay. Above it, the placement reverts them (`-keep_resize_below_overflow`). Unset: the default of the tool, 1, which keeps them all. OpenROAD-flow-scripts passes the value only when you set a variable for it.

global_placement.timing_driven.repair_ti.help: Repair the setup of the worst paths in the last timing-driven iteration, with a few moves that keep the topology (`-timing_driven_repair_timing`). The documentation of OpenROAD calls it experimental and not ready for production use.

global_placement.timing_driven.repair_tn.help: The share of the violating endpoints that this repair targets, in percent (`-timing_driven_repair_tns_end_percent`). Needs `repair_timing`. Unset: the default of the tool, 1.

global_placement.timing_driven.virtual_c.help: Build a light clock tree before each timing-driven iteration, to model the clock latency of each sink (`-virtual_cts`).
The largest insertion delay of the virtual clock tree, as a fraction of the clock period (`-virtual_cts_max_skew_fraction`). Needs `virtual_cts`. Unset: the default of the tool, 0.1.

global_placement.routability_driven.enab.help: Inflate the cells in congested regions during the placement (`-routability_driven`). The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

global_placement.routability_driven.esti.help: How the mode estimates the congestion. `rudy` is a fast estimate from the nets. `grt` runs the global router, which is more exact and costs much more run time (`-routability_use_grt`). The default is the one of the tool.

global_placement.routability_driven.targ.help: The congestion that the mode tries to reach (`-routability_target_rc_metric`). Raise it if the mode runs too long. Unset: the default of the tool, 1.01.

global_placement.routability_driven.chec.help: The overflow, from 0 to 1, at which the mode starts to check the congestion (`-routability_check_overflow`). Unset: the default of the tool, 0.3.

global_placement.routability_driven.snap.help: The overflow, from 0 to 1, at which the mode saves a snapshot to revert to (`-routability_snapshot_overflow`). Unset: the default of the tool, 0.6.

global_placement.routability_driven.max_.help: The cap on the density in this mode, from 0 to 1 (`-routability_max_density`). Unset: the default of the tool, 0.99.

global_placement.routability_driven.infl.help: The strength of the inflation (`-routability_inflation_ratio_coef`). Unset: the default of the tool, 2.

global_placement.routability_driven.max_.help: The largest inflation of one cell, as a ratio (`-routability_max_inflation_ratio`). Unset: the default of the tool, 3.

global_placement.routability_driven.min_.help: A tile with less congestion than this, from 0 to 1, does not inflate (`-routability_min_congestion_for_inflation`). Unset: the default of the tool, 0.95.

global_placement.routability_driven.max_.help: The most area that the inflation may add, as a fraction of the movable area (`-routability_max_inflation_total`). Unset: the default of the tool, 0.3.

global_placement.routability_driven.net_.help: The extra wirelength weight of the nets in congested tiles (`-routability_net_weight_max`). 1 adds none. Unset: the default of the tool, 1.

global_placement.routability_driven.cong.help: The share of the nets that get that weight, in percent (`-routability_congested_nets_percentage`). Unset: the default of the tool, 1.

global_placement.routability_driven.rc_c.help: The weights of the 0.5%, 1%, 2% and 5% most congested tiles in the average congestion, four numbers (`-routability_rc_coefficients`). Unset: the default of the tool, 1, 1, 0 and 0.

global_placement.initial_place.from_cent.help: Start every cell at the center of the core, also when the database has locations (`-force_center_initial_place`). OpenROAD-flow-scripts gives the flag to the main pass of the placement.

global_placement.initial_place.max_iter.help: The most iterations of the initial placement (`-initial_place_max_iter`). 0 skips the initial placement, which `-skip_initial_place` also does. Unset: the default of the tool, 20.

global_placement.initial_place.max_fanou.help: The initial placement ignores the nets with at least this many pins (`-initial_place_max_fanout`). Unset: the default of the tool, 200.

global_placement.nesterov.skip.help: Stop after the initial placement and run no solver (`-skip_nesterov_place`). The tool refuses it with `io.flow: concurrent` (GPL-0182).

global_placement.nesterov.min_phi_coef.help: The smallest factor of the step size of the solver (`-min_phi_coef`). Useful when the placement diverges. Unset: the default of the tool, 0.95.

global_placement.nesterov.max_phi_coef.help: The largest factor of the step size of the solver (`-max_phi_coef`). Unset: the default of the tool, 1.05.

global_placement.nesterov.init_density_p.help: The first weight of the density penalty (`-init_density_penalty`). Tune it when you start from placed cells. Unset: the default of the tool, 8e-5.

global_placement.nesterov.init_wirelengt.help: The first coefficient of the wirelength term (`-init_wirelength_coef`). Unset: the default of the tool, 0.25.

global_placement.nesterov.reference_hpwl.help: The wirelength change that the controller of the density penalty measures against, in the units of the library: database units, not micrometers (`-reference_hpwl`). 0 takes it from the wirelength of the design. Unset: the default of the tool, 0. The README of OpenROAD names 466e6, which is not the value in the source.

global_placement.nesterov.overflow.help: The overflow, from 0 to 1, at which the solver stops (`-overflow`). A larger value runs faster and spreads the cells less. Unset: the default of the tool, 0.1.

global_placement.nesterov.revert_on_dive.help: Save the state along the iterations, and go back to it if the solver diverges. False passes `-disable_revert_if_diverge`. The default is the one of the tool.

global_placement.nesterov.pin_density_ad.help: Adjust the area of each cell by the density of its pins. False passes `-disable_pin_density_adjust`. The default is the one of the tool.

global_placement.bin_grid_count.help: The number of bins of the density grid, in each direction (`-bin_grid_count`). It must be a power of two, such as 64 or 128, because the solver uses a Fourier transform. A grid much finer than the tool would choose can make the solver diverge (GPL-0305): 64 bins in each direction does so for a design of 400 cells on nangate45. The log of the placement shows the ideal count (GPL-0026). Unset: the tool chooses the number from the design.

global_placement.incremental.help: Place only the cells that have no location yet, and keep the others where they are (`-incremental`). OpenROAD-flow-scripts uses it after the swap of arithmetic modules. The tool refuses it with `io.flow: concurrent` (GPL-0170).

global_placement.congestion_heatmap.help: Run the global router after the placement for the congestion heatmap of the graphical interface (`-enable_routing_congestion`). It costs run time.

global_placement.random_seed.help: The seed that perturbs the cells at the start (`-random_seed`). Different seeds give different placements. Unset: the default of the tool, 1.

global_placement.perturb_distance.help: The radius of the perturbation at the start, a length with a unit; 99.5% of the offsets fall inside it (`-perturb_dist`, which takes nanometers: the flow converts). 0 um switches the perturbation off. Unset: the smaller of 0.5 micrometers and one row height.

global_placement.flop_clustering.help: The clustering of flip-flops into multibit cells.

global_placement.flop_clustering.enabled.help: Cluster the flip-flops (`cluster_flops`). The command runs after the global placement, and the flow estimates the parasitics again after it. A library with multibit cells often needs their sites in `floorplan.additional_sites`. OpenROAD-flow-scripts runs it only when a variable asks for it.

global_placement.flop_clustering.tray_we.help: The weight of the tray (`-tray_weight`). Unset: the default of the tool, 32.

global_placement.flop_clustering.timing_.help: The weight of the timing (`-timing_weight`). Unset: the default of the tool, 0.1.

global_placement.flop_clustering.max_spl.help: The largest set of flops that the clustering handles at once (`-max_split_size`). -1 splits nothing. Unset: the default of the tool, 500.

global_placement.flop_clustering.num_pat.help: The number of timing paths that the clustering considers (`-num_paths`). Unset: the default of the tool, 0.

global_placement.flop_clustering.clock_p.help: The credit for the clock tree power that banking saves (`-clock_power_weight`). A larger value gives a higher banking ratio. Unset: the default of the tool, 0, which gives no credit.

global_placement.clusters.help: Sets of instances that the placement keeps together as one cluster (`placement_cluster`), each a list of instance names or patterns. The documentation of OpenROAD advises it for small groups of gates. The cluster stands for the instances that exist when the main placement starts, so name no buffer that the flow removes.

resize.help: The optimization of the design after the global placement.

resize.remove_buffers.help: Remove the buffers of the synthesis before the global placement (`remove_buffers`), so that the repair chooses the buffering. Needs `global_placement.timing_driven.enabled`: OpenROAD-flow-scripts removes the buffers only with the timing-driven placement, and so does this flow.

resize.remove_buffers_instances.help: Remove only the buffers that these instances name (`remove_buffers`), each a name or a glob pattern. The command then removes them even when they are fixed or marked not to touch, and it never removes a buffer between an input port and an output port. A pattern that matches no instance stops the flow, since the command would remove every buffer. Empty: remove every buffer that is not fixed and not marked.

resize.buffer_ports.help: The buffers between the ports and the logic.

resize.buffer_ports.enabled.help: Put a buffer between each port and the cells that it drives or that drive it (`buffer_ports`). OpenROAD-flow-scripts runs it.

resize.buffer_ports.inputs.help: Buffer the input ports. The command gets neither `-inputs` nor `-outputs` when both are true, and it buffers both then. The flow gives `-inputs` when only this one is true.

resize.buffer_ports.outputs.help: Buffer the output ports. The flow gives `-outputs` when only this one is true.

resize.buffer_ports.cell.help: The buffer that the command puts at the ports (`-buffer_cell`). The cell must be a buffer, or the tool stops with RSZ-0211. Unset: the tool chooses the buffer.

resize.repair_design.help: The call of `repair_design` after the placement.

resize.repair_design.enabled.help: Run `repair_design` at this point of the flow.

resize.repair_design.slew_margin_percent.help: Repair the slew with this margin, in percent of the limit (`-slew_margin`). The default is the one of the tool and of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

resize.repair_design.cap_margin_percent.help: Repair the capacitance with this margin, in percent of the limit (`-cap_margin`). The default is the one of the tool and of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

resize.repair_design.max_wire_length.help: Buffer each wire that is longer than this length, a length with a unit (`-max_wire_length`). Unset: the flow does not pass the flag.

resize.repair_design.match_cell_footprin.help: Swap a cell only for a cell with the same footprint in the Liberty file (`-match_cell_footprint`). Unset: the value of the platform.

resize.repair_design.reroute.help: Reroute wires with resistance-aware routing to fix slew violations (`-reroute`). The tool calls it experimental. It needs the parasitics of a global route, so only the call after global routing accepts it.

resize.repair_timing.help: The call of `repair_timing` after the placement. It repairs setup and hold.

resize.repair_timing.enabled.help: Run `repair_timing` after the placement. OpenROAD-flow-scripts does not run it there by default.

resize.repair_timing.fix.help: The checks to repair: `setup`, `hold`, or `setup_and_hold`, which repairs setup first and then hold (`-setup`, `-hold`, or neither).

resize.repair_timing.setup_margin.help: Repair until the setup slack is at least this margin (`-setup_margin`), a time with a unit, such as `50 ps`. The hold repair keeps this margin of setup slack too. The default is the one of the tool and of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

resize.repair_timing.hold_margin.help: Repair until the hold slack is at least this margin (`-hold_margin`), a time with a unit, such as `20 ps`. The default is the one of the tool and of OpenROAD-flow-scripts. Not with `fix: setup`.

resize.repair_timing.allow_setup_violati.help: Let the hold repair insert buffers that cause setup violations (`-allow_setup_violations`). Without it, the repair inserts none of them. Not with `fix: setup`.

resize.repair_timing.tns_end_percent.help: The share of the endpoints with a setup violation that the repair works on, in percent (`-repair_tns`). 0 repairs only the worst path. The default is the one of the tool and of OpenROAD-flow-scripts. Not with `fix: hold`.

resize.repair_timing.sequence.help: The setup moves, in the order that the repair tries them (`-sequence`). Empty: the default sequence of the tool. A move that `moves` switches off must not appear. `reroute` needs the parasitics of a global route. Not with `fix: hold`.

resize.repair_timing.phases.help: The phases of the setup repair, in order (`-phases`). Empty: the default phases of the tool. A phase that its switch turns off (`last_gasp` for `LAST_GASP`, `moves.crit_vt_swap` and `moves.vt_swap` for `CRIT_VT_SWAP`) must not appear. `REROUTE` needs the parasitics of a global route. Not with `fix: hold`.

resize.repair_timing.moves.help: The setup moves that the repair may not use. Not with `fix: hold`.

resize.repair_timing.moves.pin_swap.help: Allow the move that swaps the pins of a gate. False adds `-skip_pin_swap`, since a pin swap changes the connections of the gate.

resize.repair_timing.moves.gate_cloning.help: Allow the move that clones a gate to split its load. False adds `-skip_gate_cloning`, since cloning adds cells.

resize.repair_timing.moves.size_down_fan.help: Allow the move that sizes down the gates on a net with many loads, off the critical path. False adds `-skip_size_down`. The default sequence of the tool does not use this move, so the switch matters only when `sequence` names `size_down_fanout` or `size`.

resize.repair_timing.moves.buffering.help: Allow the moves that buffer a net again (`buffer`) and that split off the loads behind a buffer (`split`). False adds `-skip_buffering`.

resize.repair_timing.moves.buffer_remova.help: Allow the move that removes a buffer from a critical path. False adds `-skip_buffer_removal`.

resize.repair_timing.moves.buffer_to_inv.help: Allow the move that replaces a buffer with two inverters. False adds `-skip_buffer_to_inverters`. The default sequence of the tool does not use this move, so the switch matters only when `sequence` names `buffer_to_inverters`.

resize.repair_timing.moves.vt_swap.help: Allow the move that swaps a cell for a cell of another threshold voltage. False adds `-skip_vt_swap`, which also stops the critical swap that ends the repair. The move has an effect only when the library has such cells.

resize.repair_timing.moves.crit_vt_swap.help: Allow the swap of threshold voltage that ends the repair, on the cells of the critical paths. False adds `-skip_crit_vt_swap`. The swap has an effect only when the library has cells of several threshold voltages.

resize.repair_timing.last_gasp.help: Run the last pass of the setup repair, a greedy sizing of the cells. False adds `-skip_last_gasp`, which saves run time and area. Not with `fix: hold`.

resize.repair_timing.crpr.help: Remove the clock reconvergence pessimism from the paths during the repair. False adds `-skip_crpr`, which saves run time at the cost of area and power. The timing that the repair sees then keeps the pessimism.

resize.repair_timing.match_cell_footprin.help: Swap a cell only for a cell with the same footprint in the Liberty file (`-match_cell_footprint`). Unset: the value of the platform.

resize.repair_timing.max_buffer_percent.help: The most hold buffers that the repair inserts, in percent of the cells (`-max_buffer_percent`). Unset: the default of the tool, 20. Needs hold repair: not with `fix: setup`.

resize.repair_timing.max_iterations.help: The most iterations of the setup repair and of the hold repair (`-max_iterations`). Unset: no limit, which is the `-1` of the tool.

resize.repair_timing.max_passes.help: The most passes of one run of the repair (`-max_passes`). The tool calls it an option for debugging. Unset: the default of the tool, 10000.

resize.repair_timing.max_repairs_per_pas.help: The most repairs in one pass on the worst paths (`-max_repairs_per_pass`). The number goes down to 1 for the last violations. Unset: the default of the tool, 1. Not with `fix: hold`.

resize.repair_timing.recover_power_perce.help: Trade positive slack for power on this share of the paths, in percent (`-recover_power`). The command then recovers power and repairs neither setup nor hold, so every other leaf of this call must keep its default, except `match_cell_footprint`. The documentation of OpenROAD advises the parasitics of a global route for it. Unset: no power recovery.

resize.max_utilization_percent.help: Stop the resizer when the cells fill this share of the core area, in percent (`-max_utilization`). It acts on `buffer_ports`, `repair_design` and `repair_timing` of this stage. Unset: no limit.

resize.opt_config.help: The limits of the sizing. The database keeps them for the later flows.

resize.opt_config.limit_sizing_area.help: Leave a cell out of the sizing when its area is above this multiple of the area of the cell it would replace (`-limit_sizing_area`). The area comes from the LEF files. Unset: no limit.

resize.opt_config.limit_sizing_leakage.help: Leave a cell out of the sizing when its leakage power is above this multiple of the leakage of the cell it would replace (`-limit_sizing_leakage`). The leakage is that of the corner of the flow. Unset: no limit.

resize.opt_config.keep_sizing_site.help: Keep the site type of a cell when the resizer sizes it, so that a short cell never becomes a tall cell and the other way round (`-keep_sizing_site`). It matters for designs with rows of different heights.

resize.opt_config.keep_sizing_vt.help: Keep the threshold voltage class of a cell when the resizer sizes it (`-keep_sizing_vt`). The tool tells the classes apart only where the LEF files define the layers of the classes in their obstructions.

resize.opt_config.early_sizing_cap_ratio.help: The ratio of the input pin capacitance to the output load that the first sizing of the gates keeps (`-set_early_sizing_cap_ratio`). OpenROAD-flow-scripts sets it from `EARLY_SIZING_CAP_RATIO`. Unset: the default of the tool.

resize.opt_config.early_buffer_sizing_ca.help: The same ratio for the first sizing of the buffers (`-set_early_buffer_sizing_cap_ratio`). Unset: the default of the tool.

resize.opt_config.disable_buffer_pruning.help: Keep all buffers as candidates, delay cells and slow buffers too, which helps the hold repair (`-disable_buffer_pruning`). Then every setup repair that may use the `vt_swap` move stops OpenROAD with a segmentation fault, also with a library that has no such cells. It was seen with the image `openroad/orfs:26Q4-132-g6b305a712` and with a local build. That includes the cleanup of the netlist at the floorplan. To avoid it, set `floorplan.netlist_cleanup.mode: none`, and `moves.vt_swap: false` in each other `repair_timing` call that repairs setup. The hold repair and `repair_design` are not affected.

resize.global_sizing.help: The options of the global sizing. The database keeps them for the later flows.

resize.global_sizing.presize_mode.help: How the global sizing starts (`-presize_mode`): `disabled` keeps the cells, `min_size_max_vt` replaces every cell with its equivalent of the smallest leakage, and `max_size_min_vt` with its equivalent of the largest leakage. Unset: `disabled`.

resize.global_sizing.include_clock_netwo.help: Let the global sizing size the instances of the clock network (`-include_clock_network`). Off, it leaves them alone.

resize.global_sizing.setup_slack_margin.help: The worst setup slack at which the global sizing stops, a time with a unit, such as `50 ps` (`-setup_slack_margin`). The command takes seconds, and not the time unit of the Liberty files as the margins of `repair_timing` do, so the flow converts the value. Unset: 0.

resize.global_sizing.max_iterations.help: The most outer iterations of the Lagrangian relaxation (`-max_iterations`). Unset: the default of the tool, 20.

resize.global_sizing.beta.help: The step size of the update of the multipliers (`-beta`). Unset: the default of the tool, 0.6.

resize.global_sizing.mu_exponent.help: The exponent that seeds the multipliers of the endpoints (`-mu_exponent`). Unset: the default of the tool, 2.0.

resize.global_sizing.lambda_floor.help: The lowest value of a multiplier, so that an arc that no path uses can come back (`-lambda_floor`). Unset: the default of the tool, 1e-12.

resize.global_sizing.timing_bias.help: The balance between the pressure of the timing and the cost of the leakage, without a unit (`-timing_bias`). Unset: the default of the tool, 64.0.

resize.global_sizing.budget_safety_facto.help: A factor of at most 1 on the budget that each gate gets for sizing down (`-budget_safety_factor`). Unset: the default of the tool, 1.0.

arith_swap.help: The swap of the arithmetic modules for faster or smaller variants.

arith_swap.enabled.help: Replace the wrapped arithmetic modules of the netlist (`replace_arith_modules`). It needs `hierarchical` and a netlist with wrapped operators.

arith_swap.path_count.help: The number of critical paths that the command analyzes to find the modules to swap (`-path_count`). Unset: the default of the tool, 1000.

arith_swap.target.help: The goal of the swap (`-target`). `setup` swaps for the fastest variants. The other goals are in the command, but the tool does not support them yet: it stops with RSZ-0155 as soon as it finds a module to swap, and the documentation of the tool lists them as not available yet. Unset: `setup`.

arith_swap.slack_threshold.help: The paths with a slack up to this value count as critical, a time with a unit, such as `50 ps` (`-slack_threshold`). The flow converts it to the time unit of the Liberty files. A positive value adds paths with a little positive slack. Unset: the default of the tool, 0.

detailed_placement.help: The legalization and the optimization of the placement.

detailed_placement.cell_padding.help: The empty sites that each cell keeps on its left and on its right during the legalization (`set_placement_padding -global -left N -right N`), in sites. The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

detailed_placement.max_displacement.help: The farthest that a cell moves to find a legal site, as two lengths with units, for x and y (`-max_displacement`). The tool takes whole micrometers. Unset: the default of the tool, which sets no limit of its own.

detailed_placement.legalizer.help: The engine that legalizes the placement. `negotiation` is the default of the tool and handles dense designs. `diamond` is the earlier search (`-use_diamond_legalizer`). It is faster, and it cannot handle dense designs.

detailed_placement.cell_padding_override.help: Other padding for some masters or some instances. A master wins over the global padding, and an instance wins over its master. Each item names `masters` or `instances`, with `left` and `right`.

detailed_placement.negotiation.help: The options of the negotiation legalizer. The diamond legalizer has none.

detailed_placement.negotiation.site_sear.help: The base number of sites that a cell may move to the left or to the right (`-site_search_window`), capped by `max_displacement`. 0 allows no horizontal move. Unset: the default of the tool, 20.

detailed_placement.negotiation.row_searc.help: The base number of rows that a cell may move up or down (`-row_search_window`), capped by `max_displacement`. 0 allows no change of row. Unset: the default of the tool, 5.

detailed_placement.negotiation.window_ex.help: Let the search window grow past its base size, to the size of the cell and when a macro or the boundary of the core cuts it short. False fixes the window (`-disable_window_extension`).

detailed_placement.negotiation.drc_penal.help: The priority of the cleanup of DRC violations, which grows with each iteration (`-drc_penalty`). A low value tolerates violations early, while overlaps go. 0 switches off the growing penalty. Unset: the default of the tool, 5.

detailed_placement.improve.help: The optimization of the placement after the legalization.

detailed_placement.improve.enabled.help: Run `improve_placement` after the legalization. It swaps and moves cells to shorten the wires. The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

detailed_placement.improve.max_displacem.help: The farthest that a cell moves in x and in y, as two integers in multiples of the row height (`-max_displacement`). 0 keeps the limit of the tool for that direction. The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

detailed_placement.improve.random_seed.help: The seed of the optimization (`-random_seed`). Unset: the default of the tool, 1.

detailed_placement.improve.extra_legaliz.help: Legalize once more inside the optimization (`-enable_extra_dpl`). The flow always gives the value, because the tool reads the environment variable `ENABLE_EXTRA_DPL` when it gets none.

detailed_placement.improve.global_swap.help: The options of the global swaps.

detailed_placement.improve.global_swap.p.help: The passes of the global swaps (`-passes`). Unset: the default of the tool, 2.

detailed_placement.improve.global_swap.t.help: The improvement of the wirelength below which a pass ends (`-tolerance`). Unset: the default of the tool, 0.01.
The share of the random moves among the moves of a pass, from 0 to 1 (`-tradeoff`). Unset: the default of the tool, 0.4.

detailed_placement.improve.global_swap.a.help: The weight of the cell area in the map of the utilization that steers the swaps (`-area_weight`). Unset: the default of the tool, 0.4.

detailed_placement.improve.global_swap.p.help: The weight of the pin count in that map (`-pin_weight`). Unset: the default of the tool, 0.6.

detailed_placement.improve.global_swap.c.help: The weight of the congestion that you give (`-congestion_user_weight`). Unset: the default of the tool, 35.0.

detailed_placement.improve.global_swap.s.help: The number of moves that the swaps sample (`-sampling_moves`). Unset: the default of the tool, 150.

detailed_placement.improve.global_swap.n.help: The number of moves between two normalizations of the costs (`-normalization_interval`). Unset: the default of the tool, 1000.

detailed_placement.improve.global_swap.p.help: The factor on the best wirelength of the profiling pass that sets the budget of the swaps (`-profiling_excess`). Unset: the default of the tool, 1.1.

detailed_placement.improve.global_swap.b.help: The factors on the budget of the wirelength, one for each stage of the swaps (`-budget_multipliers`). Unset: the default of the tool, 1.5, 1.25, 1.1 and 1.04.

detailed_placement.mirroring.help: Flip cells about the y axis where that shortens the wires (`optimize_mirroring`). The default is the one of OpenROAD-flow-scripts.

detailed_placement.check.help: What the flow does with an illegal placement (`check_placement`, which raises an error when a check fails). `fail` stops the flow. The default follows OpenROAD-flow-scripts, which does not catch the error and so stops on an illegal placement. `report` prints the violations and goes on.

detailed_placement.balance_rows.help: Balance the use of the rows of different types before the legalization (`balance_row_usage`). It is for designs with rows of different heights. OpenROAD-flow-scripts runs it only when `BALANCE_ROWS` says so.

clock.period.help: Clock period, a time with a unit, such as `10 ns`. Specify `period` or `freq`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

clock.rise.help: Time of the rising edge of the clock, a time with a unit, such as `0.5 ns`.

clock.uncertainty.help: Clock uncertainty, a time with a unit, such as `0.1 ns`.

clock.skew.help: Clock skew, a time with a unit, such as `0.05 ns`.

clock.port.help: The design port of the clock.

clock.freq.help: Clock frequency, a frequency with a unit, such as `100 MHz`. Specify `freq` or `period`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

verbose.help: Verbosity level. Higher values make the tools more talkative.

debug.help: Run the flow in debug mode: verbose logging, and exceptions are re-raised instead of being reported as a failure.

quiet.help: Run the flow quietly, unless `verbose` or `debug` is set.

redirect_stdout.help: Redirect stdout from execution of tools to files.

lib_paths.help: Additional libraries, as a list of (name, path) tuples. The name or the path can be none, but not both. GHDL and NVC take a relative path as relative to the design root.

docker.help: Run the tools in this Docker image, instead of the default image of the flow.

print_commands.help: Print the commands that the flow runs.

console_colors.help: Colorize tool output on the console.

clocks.help: Clock constraints of the design, by clock name.

clocks.*.period.help: Clock period, a time with a unit, such as `10 ns`. Specify `period` or `freq`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

clocks.*.rise.help: Time of the rising edge of the clock, a time with a unit, such as `0.5 ns`.

clocks.*.uncertainty.help: Clock uncertainty, a time with a unit, such as `0.1 ns`.

clocks.*.skew.help: Clock skew, a time with a unit, such as `0.05 ns`.

clocks.*.port.help: The design port of the clock.

clocks.*.freq.help: Clock frequency, a frequency with a unit, such as `100 MHz`. Specify `freq` or `period`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

fpga.help: FPGA device. Accepts a full part identifier as a string (e.g. "xc7a100tftg256-2L") or a mapping of the FPGA fields. A part identifier alone means `part: <identifier>` wherever layers merge. Over a mapping, it changes the part and keeps the other fields that the mapping wrote (a speed grade, for example).

fpga.part.help: Full part identifier of the device.

values: High Performance with Maximum Placement Effort
Superior Performance with Maximum Placement Effort
optimization_mode.help: Value of the Quartus `OPTIMIZATION_MODE` assignment. See https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/programmable/documentation/zpr1513988353912.html and https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/programmable/quartushelp/current/index.htm.

remove_redundant_logic.help: Let synthesis remove logic that cannot affect any output (the Quartus `REMOVE_REDUNDANT_LOGIC_CELLS` assignment).

auto_resource_sharing.help: Let synthesis share arithmetic operators between mutually exclusive operations, trading some speed for area.

retiming.help: Allow Quartus to move registers across combinational logic to balance path delays. This sets the `ALLOW_REGISTER_RETIMING` and `PHYSICAL_SYNTHESIS_REGISTER_RETIMING` assignments.

register_duplication.help: Allow the fitter to duplicate registers to reduce fanout and routing delay, at the cost of extra registers.

packed_registers.help: Value of the `AUTO_PACKED_REGISTERS_STRATIX` and `AUTO_PACKED_REGISTERS_CYCLONE` assignments, which control register packing.

gated_clock_conversion.help: Convert gated clocks into clock-enable logic, which is generally safer on FPGAs than true clock gating.

dsp_recognition.help: Infer DSP blocks from multipliers and MAC patterns. Disable to force everything into logic.

ram_recognition.help: Infer block RAM from memory patterns in the HDL.

rom_recognition.help: Infer ROM blocks from constant memory patterns.

fitter_effort.help: Fitter effort. "AUTO FIT" stops once timing is met, "STANDARD FIT" always optimizes fully, and "FAST_FIT" trades quality for compile time.

placement_effort_multiplier.help: Multiplier for the time the fitter spends on placement. The Quartus default is 1.0. A value must be greater than 0 and can be fractional. A value below 1 can shorten fitting time but can lower placement quality and design performance. A value above 1 increases placement time and quality, and may reduce routing time for designs with routing congestion. A value of 4 increases fitting time by about 2 to 4 times and may improve quality.

router_timing_optimization_level.help: Router effort for timing optimization. Higher effort increases compile time.

final_placement_optimization.help: When to run the final placement optimization pass after routing.

clock.period.help: Clock period, a time with a unit, such as `10 ns`. Specify `period` or `freq`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

clock.rise.help: Time of the rising edge of the clock, a time with a unit, such as `0.5 ns`.

clock.uncertainty.help: Clock uncertainty, a time with a unit, such as `0.1 ns`.

clock.skew.help: Clock skew, a time with a unit, such as `0.05 ns`.

clock.port.help: The design port of the clock.

clock.freq.help: Clock frequency, a frequency with a unit, such as `100 MHz`. Specify `freq` or `period`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

verbose.help: Verbosity level. Higher values make the tools more talkative.

debug.help: Run the flow in debug mode: verbose logging, and exceptions are re-raised instead of being reported as a failure.

quiet.help: Suppress informational output from VCS.

redirect_stdout.help: Redirect stdout from execution of tools to files.

lib_paths.help: Additional libraries, as a list of (name, path) tuples. The name or the path can be none, but not both. GHDL and NVC take a relative path as relative to the design root.

docker.help: Run the tools in this Docker image, instead of the default image of the flow.

print_commands.help: Print the commands that the flow runs.

console_colors.help: Colorize tool output on the console.

timeout.help: Stop and fail each subprocess invocation that contains simulation after this many seconds of wall-clock time. An invocation can combine analysis, elaboration and simulation. The limit applies to each invocation, not to their total. None sets no limit.

fail_severity.help: The least severe runtime diagnostic that fails the simulation: warning, error, failure or fatal. Failure and fatal have the same rank. Diagnostics below the threshold are recorded. Assertions that the design disables explicitly keep the documented behavior of the simulator. A nonzero exit status always fails.

vcd.help: Write a VCD waveform to this file. `true` writes `dump.vcd`; a name without an extension gets `.vcd`; `false` or an empty name writes none. A simulator that cannot write VCD refuses it, and names its own waveform settings.

stop_time.help: Stop the simulation at this simulated time. Accepts a number of nanoseconds or a string with a unit, e.g. "100us".

cocotb.help: Settings for the cocotb testbench, used when `tb.cocotb` is set.

cocotb.coverage.help: Collect coverage data if supported by simulation tool.

cocotb.reduced_log_fmt.help: Display shorter log lines in the terminal.

cocotb.resolve_x.help: How to resolve bits with a value of X, Z, U or W when they are converted to an integer.

cocotb.testcase.help: Names of the cocotb tests to run; all of them if empty. A name selects exactly the test of that name (`check` never selects `foo_check`); on cocotb 2.x it may be qualified by its module (`tb.check`). Can also be given as a comma-separated string.

cocotb.random_seed.help: Seed of the Python random module (`COCOTB_RANDOM_SEED`): the same seed recreates the same test stimulus. "random" lets cocotb draw a new seed on every run, so the flow then always runs and is never reused.

cocotb.gpi_extra.help: A comma-separated list of extra libraries that are dynamically loaded at runtime.

simv_flags.help: Extra arguments for the compiled simulator executable (`simv`). Ignored when `one_shot_run` is set.

sim_no_save.help: Pass `-no_save` so VCS does not write a restartable simulation snapshot.

generate_kdb.help: Generate the Verdi knowledge database (`-kdb`), which Verdi debugging needs. This slows elaboration.

vhdl_xlrm.help: Enable VHDL features beyond the LRM (`vhdlan -xlrm`).

one_shot_run.help: Run the simulation in the `vcs` step (`-R`), with no separate `simv` run. Ignores `simv_flags`.

ucli_script.help: UCLI (Universal Command Line Interface) script that drives the simulator executable (`simv`). Xeda always runs `simv` under UCLI with its own script.

gui.help: Start the GUI (Graphical User Interface) when the simulator runs. A string names the GUI: `dve` or `verdi`. With `true`, VCS starts Verdi if `VC_HOME` is set.

sdf_file.help: SDF file that back-annotates delays (VCS unified SDF feature).

sdf_instance.help: Hierarchy instance that is the root path of the back-annotation. Separate hierarchy levels with dots, for example `TB_NAME.UUT_NAME`. Required with `sdf_file`.

vcs_warn.help: Value of VCS' `+warn` option: a comma-separated list of warning IDs to enable, or `noID` to disable one.

vlogan_warns.help: Value of `+warn` for the Verilog analysis step (vlogan).

vcs_nowarn.help: Warning IDs to silence, passed as `-nowarn <id>` to VCS.

lint.help: Value of VCS' `+lint` option: a comma-separated list of lint checks to enable, or `noID` to disable one.

debug_access.help: Debug visibility level: true for `-debug_access+all`, false to disable, or a suffix string such as "+r" or "+class". More access means slower simulation.

debug_region.help: Restrict debug visibility to this region (`-debug_region=...`), e.g. "cell+encrypt", to keep the performance cost contained.

initreg.help: Initial value of registers (`+vcs+initreg`). Use `random` for random values.

lic_wait.help: How long to wait for a license when none is available (`vhdlan -licw`, `vcs -vc_lic_wait`).

vlogan_flags.help: Extra flags passed to `vlogan` when analyzing Verilog sources.

vhdlan_flags.help: Extra flags passed to `vhdlan` when analyzing VHDL sources.

vcs_flags.help: Extra flags passed to `vcs` during elaboration.

cflags.help: Flags passed through to the C compiler that builds the simulation executable. The defaults target the build machine, so the binary is not portable.

vcs_log_file.help: File VCS writes its elaboration log to.

fsdb.help: FSDB (Fast Signal DataBase) waveform file to write. `true` writes `dump.fsdb`.

fsdb_size_limit.help: FSDB size limit in MB (`+fsdb+dump_limit`). Unset uses the VCS default.

to_vcd.help: Convert the FSDB or VPD waveform to VCD (Value Change Dump) after the simulation. The VCD file lies beside the waveform and has its file name with a `.vcd` suffix.

vpd.help: VPD waveform file to write. `true` writes `dump.vpd`.

evcd.help: EVCD waveform file to write. `true` writes `dump.evcd`.

vpd_size_limit.help: VPD size limit in MB (`+vpdfilesize`). When the simulation reaches the limit, it overwrites older history. Needs `vpd`.

verbose.help: Verbosity level. Higher values make the tools more talkative.

debug.help: Run the flow in debug mode: verbose logging, and exceptions are re-raised instead of being reported as a failure.

quiet.help: Run the flow quietly, unless `verbose` or `debug` is set.

redirect_stdout.help: Redirect stdout from execution of tools to files.

lib_paths.help: Additional libraries, as a list of (name, path) tuples. The name or the path can be none, but not both. GHDL and NVC take a relative path as relative to the design root.

docker.help: Run the tools in this Docker image, instead of the default image of the flow.

print_commands.help: Print the commands that the flow runs.

console_colors.help: Colorize tool output on the console.

timeout.help: Stop and fail each subprocess invocation that contains simulation after this many seconds of wall-clock time. An invocation can combine analysis, elaboration and simulation. The limit applies to each invocation, not to their total. None sets no limit.

fail_severity.help: The least severe runtime diagnostic that fails the simulation: warning, error, failure or fatal. Failure and fatal have the same rank. Diagnostics below the threshold are recorded. Assertions that the design disables explicitly keep the documented behavior of the simulator. A nonzero exit status always fails.

vcd.help: Build the model with VCD tracing (`--trace-vcd`). `true` selects it; without cocotb, the testbench's `$dumpfile` and `$dumpvars` (or the design's own main) write and name the file, and a name or location here is refused. With cocotb, the value is the file cocotb writes: `true` writes `dump.vcd`, a name without an extension gets `.vcd`, and a location is delivered. Only one of `vcd`, `fst` and `saif` may be set.

stop_time.help: Stop the simulation at this simulated time. Accepts a number of nanoseconds or a string with a unit, e.g. "100us".

cocotb.help: Settings for the cocotb testbench, used when `tb.cocotb` is set.

cocotb.coverage.help: Collect coverage data if supported by simulation tool.

cocotb.reduced_log_fmt.help: Display shorter log lines in the terminal.

cocotb.resolve_x.help: How to resolve bits with a value of X, Z, U or W when they are converted to an integer.

cocotb.testcase.help: Names of the cocotb tests to run; all of them if empty. A name selects exactly the test of that name (`check` never selects `foo_check`); on cocotb 2.x it may be qualified by its module (`tb.check`). Can also be given as a comma-separated string.

cocotb.random_seed.help: Seed of the Python random module (`COCOTB_RANDOM_SEED`): the same seed recreates the same test stimulus. "random" lets cocotb draw a new seed on every run, so the flow then always runs and is never reused.

cocotb.gpi_extra.help: A comma-separated list of extra libraries that are dynamically loaded at runtime.

sim_dir.help: Directory, relative to the run directory, where Verilator writes the generated C++ and the built model.

compile_args.help: Extra arguments passed to the `verilator` command itself.

cflags.help: Extra flags for the C++ compiler (`verilator -CFLAGS`).

warn_flags.help: Verilator lint and warning flags, such as `-Wall` and `-Wno-WIDTH`. Verilator lints more strictly than most simulators.

warnings_fatal.help: Make a Verilator warning fail the run. Without it, the flow passes `-Wno-fatal`.

include_dirs.help: Directories searched for `include` files and missing modules (`-I`). Every file under them is an input of the run.

optimize.help: Optimization level for the generated model. `true` passes `-O3`, `false` passes no `-O` option, and a level of 0, 1, 2 or 3 passes `-O` with that level. Write the level only: `2`, not `-O2`.

timing.help: Enable Verilator's `--timing` support for delays and non-blocking event controls. Requires a compiler with C++20 coroutine support.
