Verilator's required C++ standard takes precedence over `-std=` in `cflags`. When it is off, Verilator ignores a delay and warns about it (`STMTDLY` for a statement, `ASSIGNDLY` for an assignment), so a testbench's `#100; $finish` ends at time 0.

model_args.help: Arguments passed to the model executable.

verilog_libs.help: Verilog library files (`-v`): their modules are elaborated only when instantiated.

build.help: Compile and link the generated C++ into an executable model. If false, Verilator only generates the sources. To build them, run make in `sim_dir` with the environment variable `MAKEFILES=xeda_hooks.mk`, which gives verilated.cpp the declaration of Xeda's hooks.

vpi.help: Enable VPI support in the model. VPI-based testbenches need it. Cocotb enables it without this setting.

no_deps.help: Pass `--no-MMD`, so Verilator does not emit make dependency files.

generate_systemc.help: Generate a SystemC model (`--sc`) instead of a plain C++ one.

generate_executable.help: Link a standalone executable (`--exe`). Without it, Verilator builds a library to embed. The `main` setting makes Verilator generate `main()`.

compiler.help: C++ compiler that builds the model, such as "clang++". The default is Verilator's own choice.

random_init.help: Randomize the initial value of uninitialized signals, which surfaces reset bugs a zero-initialized model would hide. The values come from `random_seed`. Off by default, as in Verilator; turning it on can hang a testbench that relies on an uninitialized clock, such as bsc's `main.v`. See `x_initial`.

random_seed.help: Seed of the random initialization (`+verilator+seed+`): the same seed gives the same run. "random" draws a new seed on every run, so the flow then always runs and is never reused.

x_initial.help: How uninitialized values are set at time 0: "unique" (random per run), "0", or "fast".

x_assign.help: How explicit assignments of X are resolved: "unique" (random per run), "0", "1", or "fast".

main.help: Let Verilator generate the `main` that runs the model (`--main`). Unset, it is true, unless the testbench uses cocotb, whose own main runs the model. Set it to false when the design's C++ sources hold `main` or `sc_main`; a C++ source with `main` unset is a helper (DPI), linked into the model. True is refused with cocotb.

fst.help: Build the model with FST tracing (`--trace-fst`), far more compact than VCD for long simulations. Used as `vcd` is: `true` selects the format.

saif.help: Build the model with SAIF tracing (`--trace-saif`), for power estimation. Used as `vcd` is: `true` selects the format.

threads.help: Number of threads of the model. 0 builds a model that is not thread-safe, 1 a thread-safe single-threaded model, and 2 or more a multithreaded model.

trace_underscore.help: Include signals whose names begin with an underscore in traces (`--trace-underscore`). Off, as in Verilator.

trace_structs.help: Trace structs and packed arrays with their field names, as separate signals instead of flat vectors (`--trace-structs`). Off, as in Verilator.

trace_threads.help: Number of threads used to write the waveform. Null leaves Verilator's default.

trace_max_width.help: Do not trace signals wider than this many bits. Null leaves Verilator's default.

trace_max_array.help: Do not trace arrays with more than this many elements. Null leaves Verilator's default.

verbose.help: Verbosity level. Higher values make the tools more talkative.

debug.help: Run the flow in debug mode: verbose logging, and exceptions are re-raised instead of being reported as a failure.

quiet.help: Run the flow quietly, unless `verbose` or `debug` is set.

clocks.*.rise.help: Time of the rising edge of the clock, a time with a unit, such as `0.5 ns`.

clocks.*.uncertainty.help: Clock uncertainty, a time with a unit, such as `0.1 ns`.

clocks.*.skew.help: Clock skew, a time with a unit, such as `0.05 ns`.

clocks.*.port.help: The design port of the clock.

clocks.*.freq.help: Clock frequency, a frequency with a unit, such as `100 MHz`. Specify `freq` or `period`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

fpga.part.help: Full part identifier of the device.

fail_timing.help: The flow fails if the design does not meet timing.

bitstream.help: Write the FPGA bitstream to this file, with Vivado's `write_bitstream`. A location is delivered there once the run succeeds. extra_reports.help: Write the clock utilization and methodology reports after routing. This takes more time. The flows that run without a project also write the DRC and power reports.

report_power.help: Write a power estimate (`power.xml`) with the reports after routing.

qor_suggestions.help: Run `report_qor_suggestions` and save the resulting RQS file.

num_critical_paths.help: The number of timing paths to write to the critical path reports.

default_max_input_delay.help: Default max delay to set on all non-clock input ports.

default_min_input_delay.help: Default min delay to set on all non-clock input ports.

default_max_output_delay.help: Default max delay to set on all output ports.

default_min_output_delay.help: Default min delay to set on all output ports.

suppress_msgs.help: Vivado message IDs to suppress, for example "Synth 8-7080". Vivado does not print suppressed messages, and they never trigger `fail_critical_warning`.

write_checkpoint.help: Write the routed design's Vivado checkpoint (.dcp). `vivado_synth` and `vivado_alt_synth` also write the one after synthesis, and the non-project flows (`vivado_alt_synth`, `vivado_impl`) the one after placement. The `vivado_power` flow needs this checkpoint.

write_netlist.help: Write the routed design's functional Verilog netlist and its constraints (XDC). The `vivado_postsynth_sim` flow needs this netlist.

write_timing_netlist.help: Write the routed design's timing Verilog netlist and its SDF timing annotation (`vivado_synth` writes the fast and the slow corner, the other flows the slow one). The `vivado_postsynth_sim` flow needs this netlist.

synth.help: Strategy and per-step options of the synthesis part of the Tcl script.

out_of_context.help: Synthesize out of context: `synth_design` gets `-mode out_of_context`. The synthesis options may hold that mode, which the flow keeps once, but no other `-mode`. The flow refuses another mode before the run.

impl.help: Strategy and per-step options of the implementation part of the Tcl script.

flatten_hierarchy.help: How synthesis flattens the design hierarchy: `full` flattens and does not rebuild, `rebuilt` flattens then restores the hierarchy for reporting, `none` preserves it throughout.

show_available_strategies.help: Show the available synthesis and implementation strategies.

set_synth_properties.help: Properties to set on the synthesis run (`synth_1`), by property name. A name with dots is one key. In YAML, write the setting as a block and each name as one key, for example `STEPS.SYNTH_DESIGN.ARGS.MAX_BRAM: 0`. On the command line, write `-s set_synth_properties.STEPS.SYNTH_DESIGN.ARGS.MAX_BRAM=0`. Values may be text, numbers or booleans.

set_impl_properties.help: Properties to set on the implementation run (`impl_1`), by property name. A name with dots is one key, as in `set_synth_properties`. Values may be text, numbers or booleans.

clocks.*.rise.help: Time of the rising edge of the clock, a time with a unit, such as `0.5 ns`.

clocks.*.uncertainty.help: Clock uncertainty, a time with a unit, such as `0.1 ns`.

clocks.*.skew.help: Clock skew, a time with a unit, such as `0.05 ns`.

clocks.*.freq.help: Clock frequency, a frequency with a unit, such as `100 MHz`. Specify `freq` or `period`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

fpga.part.help: Full part identifier of the device.

tcl_shell.help: Open an interactive Tcl shell after Vivado runs the flow script.

no_log.help: Pass -nolog to Vivado, so it does not write a vivado.log file.

fail_critical_warning.help: The flow fails if Vivado reports a critical warning.

fail_timing.help: The flow fails if the design does not meet timing.

bitstream.help: Write the FPGA bitstream to this file, with Vivado's `write_bitstream`. A location is delivered there once the run succeeds. In project mode, a .bin file that the `write_bitstream` step writes (`impl.steps.WRITE_BITSTREAM.ARGS.BIN_FILE`) goes beside it. If unset, the flow writes no bitstream.

extra_reports.help: Write the clock utilization and methodology reports after routing. This takes more time. The flows that run without a project also write the DRC and power reports.

report_power.help: Write a power estimate (`power.xml`) with the reports after routing.

qor_suggestions.help: Run `report_qor_suggestions` and save the resulting RQS file.

num_critical_paths.help: The number of timing paths to write to the critical path reports.

default_max_input_delay.help: Default max delay to set on all non-clock input ports.

default_min_input_delay.help: Default min delay to set on all non-clock input ports.

default_max_output_delay.help: Default max delay to set on all output ports.

default_min_output_delay.help: Default min delay to set on all output ports.

suppress_msgs.help: Vivado message IDs to suppress, e.g. "Synth 8-7080". Suppressed messages are not printed and never trigger `fail_critical_warning`.

write_checkpoint.help: Write the routed design's Vivado checkpoint (.dcp). `vivado_synth` and `vivado_alt_synth` also write the one after synthesis, and the non-project flows (`vivado_alt_synth`, `vivado_impl`) the one after placement. The `vivado_power` flow needs this checkpoint.

write_netlist.help: Write the routed design's functional Verilog netlist and its constraints (XDC). The `vivado_postsynth_sim` flow needs this netlist.

write_timing_netlist.help: Write the routed design's timing Verilog netlist and its SDF timing annotation (`vivado_synth` writes the fast and the slow corner, the other flows the slow one). The `vivado_postsynth_sim` flow needs this netlist.

synth.help: Synthesis run options: a Vivado `strategy` name (empty for the default) and per-step option overrides. See `show_available_strategies`.

out_of_context.help: Synthesize out of context: `synth_design` gets `-mode out_of_context`. The synthesis options may hold that mode, which the flow keeps once, but no other `-mode`. The flow refuses another mode before the run.

impl.help: Implementation run options: a Vivado `strategy` name (empty for the default) and per-step option overrides. See `show_available_strategies`.

flatten_hierarchy.help: How synthesis flattens the design hierarchy: `full` flattens and does not rebuild, `rebuilt` flattens then restores the hierarchy for reporting, `none` preserves it throughout.

show_available_strategies.help: Show the available synthesis and implementation strategies.

set_synth_properties.help: Properties to set on the synthesis run (`synth_1`), by property name. A name with dots is one key. In YAML, write the setting as a block and each name as one key, for example `STEPS.SYNTH_DESIGN.ARGS.MAX_BRAM: 0`. On the command line, write `-s set_synth_properties.STEPS.SYNTH_DESIGN.ARGS.MAX_BRAM=0`. Values may be text, numbers or booleans.

set_impl_properties.help: Properties to set on the implementation run (`impl_1`), by property name. A name with dots is one key, as in `set_synth_properties`. Values may be text, numbers or booleans.

gui.help: Open the created project in the Vivado GUI, which needs a display.

timeout.help: Stop and fail each subprocess invocation that contains simulation after this many seconds of wall-clock time. An invocation can combine analysis, elaboration and simulation. The limit applies to each invocation, not to their total. None sets no limit.

fail_severity.help: The least severe runtime diagnostic that fails the simulation: warning, error, failure or fatal. Failure and fatal have the same rank. Diagnostics below the threshold are recorded. Assertions that the design disables explicitly keep the documented behavior of the simulator. A nonzero exit status always fails.

vcd.help: Write a VCD waveform to this file. `true` writes `dump.vcd`; a name without an extension gets `.vcd`; `false` or an empty name writes none. A simulator that cannot write VCD refuses it, and names its own waveform settings.

stop_time.help: Stop the simulation at this simulated time. Accepts a number of nanoseconds or a string with a unit, e.g. "100us".

cocotb.help: Settings for the cocotb testbench, used when `tb.cocotb` is set.

cocotb.coverage.help: Collect coverage data if supported by simulation tool.

cocotb.reduced_log_fmt.help: Display shorter log lines in the terminal.

cocotb.resolve_x.help: How to resolve bits with a value of X, Z, U or W when they are converted to an integer.

cocotb.testcase.help: Names of the cocotb tests to run; all of them if empty. A name selects exactly the test of that name (`check` never selects `foo_check`); on cocotb 2.x it may be qualified by its module (`tb.check`). Can also be given as a comma-separated string.

cocotb.random_seed.help: Seed of the Python random module (`COCOTB_RANDOM_SEED`): the same seed recreates the same test stimulus. "random" lets cocotb draw a new seed on every run, so the flow then always runs and is never reused.

cocotb.gpi_extra.help: A comma-separated list of extra libraries that are dynamically loaded at runtime.

tcl_shell.help: Open an interactive Tcl shell after Vivado runs the flow script.

no_log.help: Pass -nolog to Vivado, so it does not write a vivado.log file.

saif.help: Write the switching activity to this SAIF file, for power estimation. `true` writes `outputs/<design>.saif`, the name that the run uses when a location is given.

elab_flags.help: Extra flags passed to `xelab` during elaboration.

analyze_flags.help: Extra flags passed to `xvlog`/`xvhdl` during analysis.

sim_flags.help: Extra flags passed to `xsim` at run time.

elab_debug.help: Debug level passed to `xelab -debug`, for example "typical" or "all". The default is "typical". Xeda refuses "off", because it needs the source information to read the diagnostics of the simulator.

sdf.help: SDF files that annotate the netlist with delays, per delay corner (min, typ, max), and an optional instance root.

debug_traces.help: Enable the debug tracing of the simulator (`ltrace` and `ptrace`). The output is very verbose and the simulation is slow.

prerun_time.help: Run the simulation for this long before the SAIF file is opened, for example "10ns". The activity of this time, such as an initial reset sequence, is not in the SAIF file, and its duration does not include it. The VCD (`vcd`) is not affected: it records from the start of the simulation.

work_lib.help: Name of the HDL working library.

xelab_log.help: File the elaboration (`xelab`) log is written to.

vcd_scope.help: Hierarchical scope to dump to the VCD. Empty means the whole testbench. Needs `vcd`.

vcd_level.help: How many hierarchy levels below `vcd_scope` to dump. 0 dumps every level. Needs `vcd`.

plugins.help: Yosys plugins to load with `plugin -i`, e.g. "ghdl" for VHDL input or "slang" for SystemVerilog.

flatten.help: Flatten the design hierarchy. Unset leaves the choice to the flow: `yosys` flattens when it maps to a liberty library (`liberty` or a `platform`) and keeps the hierarchy otherwise, and `yosys_sim` flattens only through CXXRTL's own `cxxrtl.flatten`.

read_verilog_flags.help: Flags passed to yosys' `read_verilog` for each Verilog source. They do not apply to the Verilog sources of a design that `slang` reads together with its SystemVerilog sources. When `yosys` maps to a liberty library, it refuses a flag that the script or a setting gives (`-defer`, `-D`, `-I`).

read_systemverilog_flags.help: Flags passed to the SystemVerilog front-end selected by `systemverilog`, `uhdm` or `slang`. The built-in reader (`default`) takes `read_verilog_flags` instead. With `slang`, they also apply to the Verilog sources, which the same `read_slang` reads when the design has a SystemVerilog source. A flag that the script gives to `read_slang` itself (`--top`, `-D`, `-I`, `-G`, `--blackboxed-module`, `--extern-modules`, `--best-effort-hierarchy`) is refused.

check_assert.help: Run yosys' `check -assert`. It fails the flow on structural problems such as combinational loops or multiply-driven wires.

rtl_verilog.help: Write the elaborated (pre-synthesis) design to this Verilog file. Useful for inspecting what yosys read.

rtl_json.help: Write the elaborated (pre-synthesis) design to this JSON file. Only the design's own modules are written, as for `rtl_verilog`: blackboxes and library cells are not.

rtl_graph.help: Render a `show` graph of the elaborated design to this file.

rtl_graph_flags.help: Flags passed to yosys' `show` when rendering `rtl_graph`.

ghdl.help: Settings for the ghdl-yosys plugin, used to read VHDL sources. Set automatically when the design has VHDL sources.

ghdl.verbose.help: Verbosity level. Higher values make the tools more talkative.

ghdl.debug.help: Run the flow in debug mode: verbose logging, and exceptions are re-raised instead of being reported as a failure.

ghdl.quiet.help: Run the flow quietly, unless `verbose` or `debug` is set.

ghdl.analysis_flags.help: Additional flags for the analysis phase.

ghdl.elab_flags.help: Additional flags for the elaboration phase.

ghdl.syn_bindings.help: Use synthesizer rules for component binding. During elaboration, if the VHDL LRM rules bind a component to no entity, look in every known library for an entity with the name of the component.

ghdl.warn_error.help: Treat every warning as an error.

ghdl.werror.help: Treat every warning as an error.

ghdl.elab_warn_error.help: Treat warnings as errors during elaboration.

ghdl.elab_werror.help: Treat warnings as errors during elaboration.

ghdl.relaxed.help: Relax some rules slightly, for compatibility with other simulators and synthesizers.

ghdl.clean_before_analyze.help: Run `ghdl remove` before analysis. It removes the work library and every file GHDL generated from it in the run directory.

ghdl.diagnostics.help: Enable both color and source line caret diagnostics.

ghdl.synopsys.help: Allow the Synopsys packages in the `ieee` library.

ghdl.psl_in_comments.help: Parse PSL assertions in comments (for VHDL-2002 and earlier).

ghdl.vendor_library.help: Treat every unit of this library as a black box.

ghdl.no_formal.help: Synthesize neither `assert` nor PSL. Required for the yosys+nextpnr flow.

ghdl.no_assert_cover.help: Pass `--no-assert-cover` to GHDL. Its help text reads: "Cover PSL assertion activation".

ghdl.assert_assumes.help: Treat all PSL asserts like PSL assumes.

ghdl.assume_asserts.help: Treat all PSL assumes like PSL asserts.

ghdl.verilog_output.help: Output file for the generated Verilog; by default `outputs/<design>.v`. If a directory is provided, each VHDL source file is converted to a Verilog file in that directory.

ghdl.clock.period.help: Clock period, a time with a unit, such as `10 ns`. Specify `period` or `freq`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

ghdl.clock.rise.help: Time of the rising edge of the clock, a time with a unit, such as `0.5 ns`.

ghdl.clock.uncertainty.help: Clock uncertainty, a time with a unit, such as `0.1 ns`.

ghdl.clock.skew.help: Clock skew, a time with a unit, such as `0.05 ns`.

ghdl.clock.port.help: The design port of the clock.

ghdl.clock.freq.help: Clock frequency, a frequency with a unit, such as `100 MHz`. Specify `freq` or `period`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

systemverilog.help: Front-end used for SystemVerilog sources: yosys' built-in reader (`default`), Surelog/UHDM (`uhdm`), or the slang plugin (`slang`). With `slang`, one `read_slang` reads the Verilog sources of a design that has a SystemVerilog source too.

use_slang_plugin.help: Load the slang plugin when `systemverilog` is "slang". Disable if slang is compiled into your yosys build.

verilog_lib.help: Verilog library files read with `-lib`: their modules are used only when instantiated, and are otherwise treated as black boxes.

set_attribute.help: Attributes to set, from a mapping or a JSON file, organized as attr_name -> (object_path -> attr_value).

set_mod_attribute.help: Module attributes to set, organized as attr_name -> (module_path -> attr_value).

prep.help: Run yosys' `prep` with these flags instead of the default elaboration sequence.

keep_hierarchy.help: Modules that must not be flattened, marked with the `keep_hierarchy` attribute. See also `flatten`.

defines.help: Verilog preprocessor macros passed as `-D<name>=<value>`, in addition to the design's own `defines`.

black_box.help: Modules to treat as black boxes: their contents are discarded and only their interface is kept.

top_is_vhdl.help: Whether the top module is VHDL. Unset: it is VHDL if the last source in a hardware description language that the flow reads is VHDL.

splitnets.help: Run `splitnets`, splitting multi-bit nets into individual bits. Unset: on when mapping to a liberty library, off otherwise.

splitnets_driver.help: Pass `-driver` to `splitnets`, so nets are split by their driver.

splitnets_ports.help: Pass `-ports` to `splitnets`, so module ports are split too.

synth_flags.help: Extra flags passed to yosys' `synth` command. When `yosys` maps to a liberty library, it refuses a flag that a setting or the script gives, and the error names the setting. With `arithmetic.wrap_operators`, the flags go to the coarse part of `synth` only, since wrapping replaces the fine part.

noabc.help: Do not run the `abc` step. Also pass `-noabc` to `synth`.

abc_dff.help: Run abc with `-dff`. Unset: off when mapping to a liberty library, on otherwise. A liberty mapping refuses `true`: it maps the flip-flops with `dfflibmap` before `abc` runs, so `-dff` has no effect there.

abc_flags.help: Extra flags passed to yosys' `abc`/`abc9`. When `yosys` maps to a liberty library, it refuses a flag that a setting gives, and the error names the setting.

abc_constr.help: Lines written to abc's constraint file, e.g. "set_driving_cell ..." or "set_load ...".

abc_script.help: Custom abc script, replacing the default mapping script: a script file, or the script itself written inline after a "+" ("+strash;map"). With `abc.mapper: abc_new` in `yosys`, the script works on a GIA and must end in a mapped one (`&nf`), and it replaces the scripts of wrapped operators. Advanced: a wrong script silently produces a poor or invalid netlist.

post_synth_rename.help: Flags passed to yosys' `rename` after synthesis, e.g. ["-hide"].

netlist.help: Write the synthesized gate-level netlist to this Verilog file. Set to null to skip.

netlist_verilog.help: Write the synthesized gate-level netlist to this Verilog file. Set to null to skip.

netlist_attrs.help: Include cell and wire attributes in the written Verilog netlist. Unset: included, except when mapping to a liberty library (that netlist is written for place and route). A netlist with wrapped operators (`arithmetic.wrap_operators`) keeps its attributes, and `false` is refused.

netlist_expr.help: Write expressions in the netlist instead of always fully mapping them. Null leaves yosys' default.

netlist_dec.help: Write constants in the netlist in decimal.

netlist_hex.help: Write constants in the netlist in hexadecimal. Unset: hexadecimal, except when mapping to a liberty library.

netlist_blackboxes.help: Include black-box modules in the written netlist.

netlist_simple_lhs.help: Write only simple left-hand sides in the netlist, for tools that cannot parse concatenations on the left of an assignment.

netlist_verilog_flags.help: Extra flags for `write_verilog`, in addition to those the `netlist_*` switches above imply. When `yosys` maps to a liberty library, it refuses a flag that a `netlist_*` switch gives.

netlist_src_attrs.help: Keep `src` attributes (source file and line) in the written netlists (JSON, Verilog and BLIF).

netlist_unset_attributes.help: Attributes to strip from the design before writing any netlist.

json_netlist.help: Write the synthesized netlist to this JSON file. Consumers such as `nextpnr` need it.

netlist_json.help: Write the synthesized netlist to this JSON file. Consumers such as `nextpnr` need it.

netlist_graph.help: Render a `show` graph of the synthesized netlist to this file.

netlist_graph_flags.help: Flags passed to yosys' `show` when rendering `netlist_graph`.

write_blif.help: Write the synthesized netlist to this BLIF file.

sta.help: Run a simple static timing analysis (implies `flatten`).

post_synth_opt.help: Run additional optimization after synthesis (gates and LUTs only). Unset: off. A liberty mapping runs no such step and refuses `true`. Use `coarse.opt_dff_sat` there.

ltp.help: Print the longest topological path in the design.

platform.help: Name of a bundled ASIC platform (see `xeda list-platforms`). It names the standard cell library and the technology files that the flow works on. Give `platform_file` for a platform that Xeda does not ship; then `platform` can be left out, and if given it must be the `name` of that file.

platform_file.help: Residue file of a platform (YAML). A file that sets `extends` to a bundled platform changes only what it gives. A file without `extends` is a complete platform. A relative path is relative to the design root.

corner.help: Name of the corner of the platform, or one of its aliases. The default is the default corner of the platform. A flow works on one corner: a list of corners is refused.

liberty.help: Standard cell (Liberty) libraries that the flow reads for mapping and timing, instead of the Liberty files of the corner of the platform. Xeda reads each file as it is (`yosys` gives each to `dfflibmap` and to `abc`). Without them, the flow uses the Liberty files of the platform. The platform still gives everything else, and its files must be installed. The files of a producer and its consumer agree, in the same order.

library.help: Standard cell (Liberty) libraries that the flow reads for mapping and timing, instead of the Liberty files of the corner of the platform. Xeda reads each file as it is (`yosys` gives each to `dfflibmap` and to `abc`). Without them, the flow uses the Liberty files of the platform. The platform still gives everything else, and its files must be installed. The files of a producer and its consumer agree, in the same order.

dont_use_cells.help: Standard cells that the flow must not use, in addition to the cells that the platform lists. The default is none.

pdk_provider.help: Where the PDK files of the platform come from. `orfs`: a sparse checkout of OpenROAD-flow-scripts. `ciel`: a PDK build that `ciel` installs. `lambdapdk`: a sparse checkout of lambdapdk. `directory`: a directory that holds the files in a known layout. The default is the provider that the platform names; the platform must have an entry for the provider.

pdk_version.help: Version of the PDK files: the commit (`orfs`, `lambdapdk`) or the hash (`ciel`). For `directory`, a version that Xeda checks against the directory when it can, and `unpinned` when you give none. The default is the version that the platform pins for `pdk_provider`. The version is part of the identity of the run.

pdk_root.help: Directory of the PDK store. `None` means `~/.ciel`. Variables such as `$HOME` expand in it, and a relative path is relative to the design root. It tells where the files are, so it is no part of the identity of the run: the run depends on the content of the files it reads.

gates.help: Map to this generic gate set instead of a liberty library, e.g. ["AND", "OR", "NOT"]. Accepts a comma-separated string. Refused together with `platform`, `platform_file` or `liberty`.

lut.help: Map to LUTs of this size instead of standard cells, e.g. "4" or a "<width>:<cost>" pair. Refused together with `platform`, `platform_file` or `liberty`.

stop_after.help: Stop the flow after this stage. "rtl" elaborates the design and writes the RTL outputs without synthesizing, so it writes no netlist and no report. A setting that asks for one is refused: `netlist_json`, `netlist_verilog`, `netlist_graph`, `write_blif`, `sta` and `ltp` must be null or false.

hierarchy.help: The hierarchy of the design during a mapping to a liberty library.

hierarchy.keep_min_cost.help: Keep each module whose cost is above this many NAND2 gate equivalents (`keep_hierarchy -min_cost`). Unset: flatten the design. Needs a yosys with Tcl: Xeda then runs a Tcl script.

hierarchy.keep_instances.help: Instances that keep their module. Each item is a yosys selection of cells, such as `top/u_core`, and gets the `keep_hierarchy` attribute before the design is flattened. Not with `flatten: false`, which keeps every module.

hierarchy.separator.help: The character that joins the names of the levels of a flattened design. Unset: `.`, the character of yosys. The place and route tool splits the names at its own divider. Not with `flatten: false`.

hierarchy.cross_boundary_opt.help: Optimize across the boundaries of the modules that stay separate (`synth -hieropt`): constants and unused ports pass through them. It acts only on modules that stay, such as `keep_hierarchy`, `hierarchy.keep_instances`, `hierarchy.keep_min_cost`, a `keep_hierarchy` attribute in the sources, or all modules with `flatten: false`. With `arithmetic.wrap_operators`, it acts in the coarse part only, since wrapping replaces the fine part of `synth`.

coarse.help: The coarse-grain passes of a mapping to a liberty library.

coarse.fsm.help: Extract and optimize finite state machines (`fsm`). False adds `-nofsm` to `synth`.

coarse.share.help: Merge operators that cannot be active together, with a SAT solver (`share`). False adds `-noshare` to `synth`.

coarse.latches.help: How `proc` reports an inferred latch. Unset: the default of yosys, which reports it in the log (`info` or `auto`, by release). `warn` prints a warning and `error` stops the run.

coarse.opt_dff_sat.help: Remove flip-flops that a SAT solver proves constant or equal to another (`-sat` on the `opt` after `synth`). It costs run time. `synth` does not run it.

arithmetic.help: The mapping of adders and other operators to a liberty library.

arithmetic.adder_architecture.help: Carry-lookahead architecture of the adders. `yosys` keeps the architecture of yosys (Brent-Kung); the other values add `-extra-map +/choices/<name>.v` to `synth`. Not with `wrap_operators`, which replaces that part of `synth`: choose the architectures in `wrapped_adders`.

arithmetic.adder_map.help: `platform` maps full adders to the full-adder cells of the platform (`extract_fa` and the map file of the platform, or `adder_map_file`) when there is a map. `none` maps no full adders.

arithmetic.adder_map_file.help: Verilog map of full adders, used with `extract_fa` instead of the map of the platform. Not with `adder_map: none`. The map runs only when the design has no operator wrapped yet (operator wrapping skips it, as OpenROAD-flow-scripts does).

arithmetic.wrap_operators.help: Wrap wide operators in modules with alternative architectures, for the place and route tool to choose from. Needs a yosys with Tcl: Xeda then runs a Tcl script. The netlist keeps its attributes. With `abc.mapper: abc_new`, ABC maps each wrapped operator with the script that the operator carries, as OpenROAD-flow-scripts does. With `abc`, ABC maps every module with the script of `abc.strategy`.

arithmetic.wrapped_adders.help: The architectures of the wrapped adders, in order. The first one builds the module that the design instantiates. Only the named architectures get a module. Unset: `han_carlson`, `kogge_stone`, `sklansky` and `brent_kung`, the order of OpenROAD-flow-scripts. Needs `wrap_operators`.

arithmetic.wrapped_multipliers.help: The architectures of the wrapped multipliers, in order. The first one builds the module that the design instantiates. Only the named architectures get a module. Unset: `booth`, then `base`. Needs `wrap_operators`.

arithmetic.alumacc.help: Warning: without the `$alu` and `$macc` cells, the adder architecture has nothing to map. True merges the arithmetic cells into them (`alumacc`). False adds `-noalumacc` to `synth`.

arithmetic.multiplier.help: `booth` maps multipliers to radix-4 Booth multipliers (`synth -booth`). The Booth pass has an effect on multipliers of at least 4x4 bits with at least 8 bits of result. Not with `wrap_operators`: the wrapped multipliers decide.

arithmetic.arith_tree.help: Convert chains of additions and `$macc` cells to carry-save adder trees (`synth -arith_tree`). Needs a yosys that has this option.

arithmetic.extract_fa.help: The options of `extract_fa`. They act only when the full-adder map runs: operator wrapping skips it when it extracts an operator, and a platform with no adder map has none to run.

arithmetic.extract_fa.max_depth.help: The deepest logic cone to search (`-d`). Unset: 20, the value of yosys.

arithmetic.extract_fa.max_breadth.help: The widest logic cone to search (`-b`). Unset: 6, the value of yosys.

memory.help: The mapping of memories to a liberty library.

memory.libmap.help: Memory library files (`memory_libmap -lib`). The script maps the memories that the coarse part of `synth` collected to the cells of the libraries. The cells need a map: see `techmap`. The format is the one of the `memlib` of yosys.

memory.techmap.help: Verilog map of the cells of the memory libraries (`techmap -map`), run after `memory_libmap`.

memory.max_bits.help: The largest memory that the synthesis turns into flip-flops, in bits (rows times width). A larger memory stops the run, or is shrunk with `mock_large`. Unset: no limit. The check runs on the memories after the coarse part of `synth`. Needs a yosys with Tcl: Xeda then runs a Tcl script.

memory.mock_large.help: Shrink each memory above `max_bits` to one row, as OpenROAD-flow-scripts does. The netlist is not a correct implementation then. The log lists the shrunk memories. Needs `max_bits` and a yosys with Tcl: Xeda then runs a Tcl script.

memory.keep_mocked.help: Give the module of each mocked memory the `keep_hierarchy` attribute, as OpenROAD-flow-scripts does. The attribute keeps the module separate only if nothing flattened it before. Needs `mock_large`.

memory.merge_ff.help: Merge flip-flops into the read ports of memories. False adds `-nordff` to `synth`.

memory.rw_check.help: Warning: with false, the netlist can differ from the simulation when a read and a write meet on one address. True keeps the value that the design defines. False marks every read port as returning any value then (`synth -no-rw-check`).

sequential.help: The mapping of latches, clock gates and flip-flops to a liberty library.

sequential.latch_map.help: `platform` maps latches with the latch map of the platform (or `latch_map_file`) when there is one. `none` maps no latches.

sequential.latch_map_file.help: Verilog map of latches, applied with `techmap -map` after `dfflegalize`, instead of the map of the platform. Not with `latch_map: none`.

sequential.clockgate_map.help: `platform` reads the file with the clock-gating cells of the platform (or `clockgate_map_file`) when there is one. `none` reads no such file.

sequential.clockgate_map_file.help: Verilog file with the clock-gating cells (`read_verilog -defer`), instead of the file of the platform. Not with `clockgate_map: none`.

sequential.dff_liberty.help: Liberty file for mapping flip-flops. It replaces the Liberty files on `dfflibmap`; `abc` still gets the Liberty files. Not with `dff_map`.

sequential.dff_map.help: Verilog map of flip-flops. Every module in the file names a flip-flop type that the netlist may keep, such as `$_DFF_P_`. The script legalizes the flip-flops to these types and applies the map with `techmap -map`, instead of running `dfflibmap`. Not with `dff_liberty`.

sequential.clock_gating.enabled.help: Infer clock gates after the latches are mapped and before the flip-flops are mapped. A design that wants a gate for an enable instantiates a clock-gating cell itself, with the map of `sequential.clockgate_map`.

sequential.clock_gating.pos_icg.help: The clock-gating cell for flip-flops on the rising edge: the cell, its enable port, its clock port and its gated clock port (`clockgate -pos`). The enable must be active high. Unset: yosys picks a cell from the Liberty files when neither this nor `neg_icg` is set, and gates no rising-edge flip-flop otherwise.

sequential.clock_gating.neg_icg.help: The clock-gating cell for flip-flops on the falling edge, in the form of `pos_icg` (`clockgate -neg`). Unset: see `pos_icg`.

sequential.clock_gating.min_width.help: Gate only the sets of at least this many flip-flops that share an enable (`clockgate -min_net_size`). Unset: the default of yosys.

sequential.clock_gating.tie_lo.help: Warning: a port that is tied low for good can disable the cell. A port of the clock-gating cell that the script ties to zero, such as a scan enable (`clockgate -tie_lo`). Needs `pos_icg` or `neg_icg`: a cell that yosys picks from the Liberty files lists its own tie-low ports.

sequential.retime_modules.help: Modules to retime: the flip-flops move over the logic to shorten the longest path (`abc -dff` with a retiming script). Each module must still be a module when the retiming starts: it is the top module, or the flattening keeps it (`keep_hierarchy`, a kept instance, a `keep_hierarchy` attribute in the sources or in `set_attribute`), or the design is not flattened. If a module is gone, the run stops with an error that names it. Retiming moves flip-flops, so the netlist does not match the names or the states of the RTL, and the run checks no equivalence.

sequential.tristate.help: `logic` converts the tri-state buffers that drive no output port to plain logic (`tribuf -logic`) after the coarse part of `synth`. `off` runs no such pass.

sequential.min_enable_fanout.help: Warning: this changes the netlist from the flip-flops on. Unmap a clock enable that fewer flip-flops share than this number into logic (`dfflegalize -mince`). Unset: keep every enable.

sequential.min_sync_reset_fanout.help: Warning: this changes the netlist from the flip-flops on. Unmap a synchronous set or reset that fewer flip-flops share than this number into logic (`dfflegalize -minsrst`). Unset: keep every set and reset.

abc.help: The mapping of the logic with ABC to a liberty library.

abc.strategy.help: The ABC mapping script. `area` and `speed` are the scripts of OpenROAD-flow-scripts, `speed_roundtrip` is the former speed script of Xeda (it moves the network between ABC and yosys in each round), and `yosys` keeps the default script of yosys. `area_0` to `area_2` and `delay_0` to `delay_3` are the strategies that LibreLane composes from the steps of ABC; the options below act on them only. `abc_script` replaces the script of the strategy.

abc.mapper.help: The yosys command that runs ABC. `abc_new` is experimental in yosys. It maps with a script that works on a GIA and ends in a mapped one (`&nf`). Unless `abc_script` gives one, it maps with the script `abc_speed_gia_only.script` of OpenROAD-flow-scripts. With `arithmetic.wrap_operators` and no `abc_script`, it gets no `-script`: each wrapped operator maps with the script it carries, and the rest of the design with the same gia-only script, which the flow sets as the default of `abc_new` (as OpenROAD-flow-scripts does). It refuses `abc.strategy` other than `area`: those scripts end in a network.

abc.driver_cell.help: Cell that ABC assumes drives the inputs (`set_driving_cell`). Unset: the cell of the platform.

abc.load.help: Load that ABC assumes on each output (`set_load`), a capacitance such as `3.9 fF`. Unset: the load of the platform.

abc.delay_target.help: Delay target of ABC (`-D`): a time such as `500 ps`, or `auto` for the period of the main clock. Unset: no `-D`.

abc.clock_derating.help: Warning: a large value makes ABC optimize for a period much shorter than the clock period, and that can grow the netlist. The part of the clock period that ABC leaves free, as a fraction: ABC gets the period times one minus this number. Needs `delay_target: auto`.

abc.buffering.help: End the composed script with `buffer`, `upsize` and `dnsize`, which buffer the high-fanout nets and size the cells. Needs a composed strategy. The default is the one of LibreLane.

abc.sizing.help: End the composed script with `upsize` and `dnsize`, which size the cells. Needs a composed strategy, and not `buffering`, which sizes too. The default is the one of LibreLane.

abc.max_fanout.help: The largest fanout that `buffer` leaves (`buffer -N`). Unset: the value of ABC, 10. Needs `buffering`.

abc.max_slew.help: The slew that `buffer` aims at (`buffer -S`): a time such as `100 ps`, at least 1 ps and a whole number of picoseconds, since ABC reads an integer. Unset: the value of ABC, 100 ps. Needs `buffering`.

abc.mfs3.help: Warning: this step can stop ABC. On some real designs, ABC stopped on an assertion in `Abc_TtExpand`, with area and delay strategies: for example all seven composed strategies on the aes design, and some delay strategies on gcd and on a small multiply-accumulate design. This happened with OSS CAD Suite yosys 0.69+286 and 0.70+179 (2026-10-13 and 2026-10-20), Homebrew yosys 0.69+post, and yosys 0.68 and 0.66 on Linux. The cause is a bug in `mfs3 -e -m` of ABC (unsorted supports in `src/opt/sfm/sfmDec.c`). Commit a4fb2d39c of berkeley-abc/abc fixes it; the ABC of yosys 0.70+179 (OSS CAD Suite 2026-10-20) does not include that commit. An ABC built without assertions can write a netlist that is not equivalent to the design instead. Where `mfs3` finished, it changed the area by at most 0.2%. Add a SAT-based remapping (`mfs3`) after the mapping.

abc.area_mapper.help: Warning: `nf` is less tested for these strategies. The mapper for area of the composed strategies `area_0` to `area_2` and `delay_3`: `amap`, or `&nf` on the AIG of ABC. The other delay strategies do not map for area.

abc.legacy_refactor.help: Warning: LibreLane calls the legacy commands less stable. Use `refactor` instead of `drf -l` in a composed strategy.

abc.legacy_rewrite.help: Warning: LibreLane calls the legacy commands less stable. Use `rewrite` instead of `drw -l` in a composed strategy.

abc.keep_ff.help: Keep the names of the flip-flop outputs that the retiming run of ABC moves (`abc -keepff`). Only the retiming run passes flip-flops through ABC, so this needs `sequential.retime_modules`.

abc.liberty_args.help: Extra arguments for the `read_lib` command that reads the Liberty files in ABC, such as "-G 250" (`abc -liberty_args`). Not with `mapper: abc_new`.

abc.dress.help: Warning: this option is experimental in ABC, and it has two known failures. With a Liberty library, `-dress` maps to LUTs instead of library cells (YosysHQ/yosys#3644, open since 2023). It fails when `abc` retimes (berkeley-abc/abc#445). Upstream ABC has a recent commit, "Skip incompatible name recovery after retiming (Issue #445)", so a newer ABC may fix the second failure. The option runs the `dress` command of ABC after the mapping, to keep the names of the original design (`abc -dress`). Not with `mapper: abc_new`, which has no such option.

finish.help: The last commands of a mapping to a liberty library, before the netlist is written.

finish.tie_undefined.help: The value of the undefined bits (`setundef`). `none` runs no `setundef`.

finish.tie_cells.help: Tie-high and tie-low cells that drive the constant nets (`hilomap`). Unset: the cells of the platform. Not with `insert_tie_cells: false`.

finish.insert_tie_cells.help: Drive the constant nets with tie cells (`hilomap`) when the platform or `tie_cells` names the cells. False runs no `hilomap`, so a constant stays a constant net.

finish.buffer_cell.help: Buffer cell, its input port and its output port, for `insbuf`. Unset: the minimum buffer of the platform. Not with `insert_buffers: false`.

finish.insert_buffers.help: Put a buffer on each wire that connects two ports directly (`insbuf`) when the platform or `buffer_cell` names the cell. False runs no `insbuf`; a design that synthesizes its modules one by one needs that.

finish.drop_formal.help: Remove the formal cells and the `$print` cells (`chformal -remove` and `delete t:$print`), which the place and route tools do not read. False keeps them.

finish.names.help: How the objects with private names get public names. `rename_wire` names each cell after the wire that it drives (`rename -wire`), before the mapping, so the name of a register shows in its flip-flop. `autoname` names every private object when the netlist is complete (`autoname`); the names can be long. `none` renames nothing.

finish.normalize_single_bit.help: Warning: this changes the declarations in the netlist. Write a one-bit vector as a scalar: remove the `single_bit_vector` attribute (`attrmap -remove`), so `[0:0]` does not appear.

finish.check_pre.help: Warning: this prints more checks in the log and fails nothing. Run `check` once before the synthesis, to find problems in the design as it is read.

finish.allow_tristate.help: Warning: a tri-state buffer in the netlist is not a mapped cell. Let the check of mapped cells pass the tri-state buffers (`check -allow-tbuf`).

techmap_files.help: Verilog techmap files of a mapping to a liberty library. Each one is applied with `techmap -map` at its `when` position: `pre_synth`, `post_coarse`, `pre_dff` or `post_dff`. A bare path is a map at `pre_dff`, after the latch map and before clock gating and the flip-flop mapping. Maps at one position run in the order of the list.

clock.period.help: Clock period, a time with a unit, such as `10 ns`. Specify `period` or `freq`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

clock.rise.help: Time of the rising edge of the clock, a time with a unit, such as `0.5 ns`.

clock.uncertainty.help: Clock uncertainty, a time with a unit, such as `0.1 ns`.

clock.skew.help: Clock skew, a time with a unit, such as `0.05 ns`.

clock.port.help: The design port of the clock.

clock.freq.help: Clock frequency, a frequency with a unit, such as `100 MHz`. Specify `freq` or `period`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

verbose.help: Verbosity level. Higher values make the tools more talkative.

debug.help: Run the flow in debug mode: verbose logging, and exceptions are re-raised instead of being reported as a failure.

quiet.help: Run the flow quietly, unless `verbose` or `debug` is set.

redirect_stdout.help: Redirect stdout from execution of tools to files.

lib_paths.help: Additional libraries, as a list of (name, path) tuples. The name or the path can be none, but not both. GHDL and NVC take a relative path as relative to the design root.

docker.help: Run the tools in this Docker image, instead of the default image of the flow.

print_commands.help: Print the commands that the flow runs.

console_colors.help: Colorize tool output on the console.

clocks.help: Clock constraints of the design, by clock name.

clocks.*.period.help: Clock period, a time with a unit, such as `10 ns`. Specify `period` or `freq`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

clocks.*.rise.help: Time of the rising edge of the clock, a time with a unit, such as `0.5 ns`.

clocks.*.uncertainty.help: Clock uncertainty, a time with a unit, such as `0.1 ns`.

clocks.*.skew.help: Clock skew, a time with a unit, such as `0.05 ns`.

clocks.*.port.help: The design port of the clock.

clocks.*.freq.help: Clock frequency, a frequency with a unit, such as `100 MHz`. Specify `freq` or `period`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

fpga.help: FPGA device. Accepts a full part identifier as a string (e.g. "xc7a100tftg256-2L") or a mapping of the FPGA fields. A part identifier alone means `part: <identifier>` wherever layers merge. Over a mapping, it changes the part and keeps the other fields that the mapping wrote (a speed grade, for example).

fpga.part.help: Full part identifier of the device.

log_file.help: File yosys writes its full log to, relative to the run directory. Set to null to log only to the console.

plugins.help: Yosys plugins to load with `plugin -i`, e.g. "ghdl" for VHDL input or "slang" for SystemVerilog.

flatten.help: Flatten the design hierarchy. `true` flattens before the RTL outputs are written and before synthesis. `false` keeps the hierarchy (`-noflatten` for the Lattice, iCE40 and Gowin passes). Unset: `true` for a Xilinx device, so the RTL outputs are flat too (`synth_xilinx` alone keeps the hierarchy, and flattening measured better). For the other families, unset leaves the choice to the pass, which flattens on its own. Under `synth_pass_only`, unset leaves the choice to the pass for every family.

read_verilog_flags.help: Flags passed to yosys' `read_verilog` for each Verilog source. They do not apply to the Verilog sources of a design that `slang` reads together with its SystemVerilog sources. Add `-noautowire` explicitly if its stricter undeclared-net behavior is required. Must be `[]` under `synth_pass_only`, which reads sources as plain `yosys <file>` does.

read_systemverilog_flags.help: Flags passed to the SystemVerilog front-end selected by `systemverilog`, `uhdm` or `slang`. The built-in reader (`default`) takes `read_verilog_flags` instead. With `slang`, they also apply to the Verilog sources, which the same `read_slang` reads when the design has a SystemVerilog source. A flag that the script gives to `read_slang` itself (`--top`, `-D`, `-I`, `-G`, `--blackboxed-module`, `--extern-modules`, `--best-effort-hierarchy`) is refused.

check_assert.help: Run yosys' `check -assert`. It fails the flow on structural problems such as combinational loops or multiply-driven wires.

rtl_verilog.help: Write the elaborated (pre-synthesis) design to this Verilog file. Useful for inspecting what yosys read.

rtl_json.help: Write the elaborated (pre-synthesis) design to this JSON file. Only the design's own modules are written, as for `rtl_verilog`: blackboxes and library cells are not.

rtl_graph.help: Render a `show` graph of the elaborated design to this file.

rtl_graph_flags.help: Flags passed to yosys' `show` when rendering `rtl_graph`.

ghdl.help: Settings for the ghdl-yosys plugin, used to read VHDL sources. Set automatically when the design has VHDL sources.

ghdl.verbose.help: Verbosity level. Higher values make the tools more talkative.

ghdl.debug.help: Run the flow in debug mode: verbose logging, and exceptions are re-raised instead of being reported as a failure.

ghdl.quiet.help: Run the flow quietly, unless `verbose` or `debug` is set.

ghdl.redirect_stdout.help: Redirect stdout from execution of tools to files.

ghdl.lib_paths.help: Additional libraries, as a list of (name, path) tuples. The name or the path can be none, but not both. GHDL and NVC take a relative path as relative to the design root.

ghdl.docker.help: Run the tools in this Docker image, instead of the default image of the flow.

ghdl.print_commands.help: Print the commands that the flow runs.

ghdl.console_colors.help: Colorize tool output on the console.

ghdl.clocks.help: Clock constraints of the design, by clock name.

ghdl.clocks.*.period.help: Clock period, a time with a unit, such as `10 ns`. Specify `period` or `freq`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

ghdl.clocks.*.rise.help: Time of the rising edge of the clock, a time with a unit, such as `0.5 ns`.

ghdl.clocks.*.uncertainty.help: Clock uncertainty, a time with a unit, such as `0.1 ns`.

ghdl.clocks.*.skew.help: Clock skew, a time with a unit, such as `0.05 ns`.

ghdl.clocks.*.port.help: The design port of the clock.

ghdl.clocks.*.freq.help: Clock frequency, a frequency with a unit, such as `100 MHz`. Specify `freq` or `period`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

ghdl.analysis_flags.help: Additional flags for the analysis phase.

ghdl.elab_flags.help: Additional flags for the elaboration phase.

ghdl.syn_bindings.help: Use synthesizer rules for component binding. During elaboration, if the VHDL LRM rules bind a component to no entity, look in every known library for an entity with the name of the component.

ghdl.warn_error.help: Treat every warning as an error.

ghdl.werror.help: Treat every warning as an error.

ghdl.elab_warn_error.help: Treat warnings as errors during elaboration.

ghdl.elab_werror.help: Treat warnings as errors during elaboration.

ghdl.relaxed.help: Relax some rules slightly, for compatibility with other simulators and synthesizers.

ghdl.clean_before_analyze.help: Run `ghdl remove` before analysis. It removes the work library and every file GHDL generated from it in the run directory.

ghdl.diagnostics.help: Enable both color and source line caret diagnostics.

ghdl.synopsys.help: Allow the Synopsys packages in the `ieee` library.

ghdl.psl_in_comments.help: Parse PSL assertions in comments (for VHDL-2002 and earlier).

ghdl.vendor_library.help: Treat every unit of this library as a black box.

ghdl.no_formal.help: Synthesize neither `assert` nor PSL. Required for the yosys+nextpnr flow.

ghdl.no_assert_cover.help: Pass `--no-assert-cover` to GHDL. Its help text reads: "Cover PSL assertion activation".

ghdl.assert_assumes.help: Treat all PSL asserts like PSL assumes.

ghdl.assume_asserts.help: Treat all PSL assumes like PSL asserts.

ghdl.verilog_output.help: Output file for the generated Verilog; by default `outputs/<design>.v`. If a directory is provided, each VHDL source file is converted to a Verilog file in that directory.

ghdl.clock.period.help: Clock period, a time with a unit, such as `10 ns`. Specify `period` or `freq`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

ghdl.clock.rise.help: Time of the rising edge of the clock, a time with a unit, such as `0.5 ns`.

ghdl.clock.uncertainty.help: Clock uncertainty, a time with a unit, such as `0.1 ns`.

ghdl.clock.skew.help: Clock skew, a time with a unit, such as `0.05 ns`.

ghdl.clock.port.help: The design port of the clock.

ghdl.clock.freq.help: Clock frequency, a frequency with a unit, such as `100 MHz`. Specify `freq` or `period`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

systemverilog.help: Front-end used for SystemVerilog sources: yosys' built-in reader (`default`), Surelog/UHDM (`uhdm`), or the slang plugin (`slang`). With `slang`, one `read_slang` reads the Verilog sources of a design that has a SystemVerilog source too.

use_slang_plugin.help: Load the slang plugin when `systemverilog` is "slang". Disable if slang is compiled into your yosys build.

verilog_lib.help: Verilog library files read with `-lib`: their modules are used only when instantiated, and are otherwise treated as black boxes.

set_attribute.help: Attributes to set, from a mapping or a JSON file, organized as attr_name -> (object_path -> attr_value).

set_mod_attribute.help: Module attributes to set, organized as attr_name -> (module_path -> attr_value).

prep.help: Run yosys' `prep` with these flags instead of the default elaboration sequence.

keep_hierarchy.help: Modules that must not be flattened, marked with the `keep_hierarchy` attribute. See also `flatten`.

defines.help: Verilog preprocessor macros passed as `-D<name>=<value>`, in addition to the design's own `defines`.

black_box.help: Modules to treat as black boxes: their contents are discarded and only their interface is kept.

top_is_vhdl.help: Whether the top module is VHDL. Unset: it is VHDL if the last source in a hardware description language that the flow reads is VHDL.

splitnets.help: Run `splitnets`, splitting multi-bit nets into individual bits.

splitnets_driver.help: Pass `-driver` to `splitnets`, so nets are split by their driver.

splitnets_ports.help: Pass `-ports` to `splitnets`, so module ports are split too.

synth_flags.help: Extra flags appended verbatim to the device-specific `synth_<family>` command of yosys, for flags that have no setting of their own.

noabc.help: Do not run the `abc` step. Also pass `-noabc` to `synth`.

abc_flags.help: Extra flags passed to yosys' `abc`/`abc9`. When `yosys` maps to a liberty library, it refuses a flag that a setting gives, and the error names the setting.

abc_constr.help: Lines written to abc's constraint file, e.g. "set_driving_cell ..." or "set_load ...".

abc_script.help: Custom abc script, replacing the default mapping script: a script file, or the script itself written inline after a "+" ("+strash;map"). With `abc.mapper: abc_new` in `yosys`, the script works on a GIA and must end in a mapped one (`&nf`), and it replaces the scripts of wrapped operators. Advanced: a wrong script silently produces a poor or invalid netlist.

post_synth_rename.help: Flags passed to yosys' `rename` after synthesis, e.g. ["-hide"].

netlist.help: Write the synthesized gate-level netlist to this Verilog file. Set to null to skip.

netlist_verilog.help: Write the synthesized gate-level netlist to this Verilog file. Set to null to skip.

netlist_attrs.help: Include cell and wire attributes in the written Verilog netlist.

netlist_expr.help: Write expressions in the netlist instead of always fully mapping them. Null leaves yosys' default.

netlist_dec.help: Write constants in the netlist in decimal.

netlist_hex.help: Write constants in the netlist in hexadecimal.

netlist_blackboxes.help: Include black-box modules in the written netlist.

netlist_simple_lhs.help: Write only simple left-hand sides in the netlist, for tools that cannot parse concatenations on the left of an assignment.

netlist_verilog_flags.help: Extra flags for `write_verilog`, in addition to those the `netlist_*` switches above imply. When `yosys` maps to a liberty library, it refuses a flag that a `netlist_*` switch gives.

netlist_src_attrs.help: Keep `src` attributes (source file and line) in the written netlists (JSON, Verilog and BLIF). On by default: nextpnr's reports cite them as source locations when it places this netlist.

netlist_unset_attributes.help: Attributes to strip from the design before writing any netlist.

json_netlist.help: Write the synthesized netlist to this JSON file. Consumers such as `nextpnr` need it.

netlist_json.help: Write the synthesized netlist to this JSON file. Consumers such as `nextpnr` need it.

netlist_graph.help: Render a `show` graph of the synthesized netlist to this file.

netlist_graph_flags.help: Flags passed to yosys' `show` when rendering `netlist_graph`.

write_blif.help: Write the synthesized netlist to this BLIF file.

sta.help: Run a simple static timing analysis (requires `flatten`).

post_synth_opt.help: Run additional optimization steps after synthesis.

ltp.help: Print the longest topological path in the design.

netlist_edif.help: The EDIF netlist for Vivado (`vivado_impl`), as a name in the run directory or a location to deliver it to. The flow writes it with `write_edif -pvector bra`, so Vivado reads every bus in the right order. It writes it only for a Xilinx device when the settings make the synthesis flat, because Vivado reads a flat netlist only. `flatten: false`, `keep_hierarchy`, `black_box` and `stop_after` prevent it.

synth_pass_only.help: Omit the preparation and cleanup that Xeda adds around the `synth_<family>` pass, which does its own elaboration and mapping. Pass flags and explicit ABC9 script choices apply in either mode. The flow reads the sources as a bare `yosys <files>` does, so the mode requires `read_verilog_flags: []`, `systemverilog: default` (the built-in reader of yosys) and no `read_systemverilog_flags`. It reads a Verilog source with plain `read_verilog` and a SystemVerilog source with `read_verilog -sv`, as the `type` of the source says. Yosys does the same by file suffix, unless the design gives a `type` that contradicts the suffix. To compare with a native yosys invocation, also match source paths and order. When false, Xeda elaborates and optimizes around the pass and gives ABC9 a delay derived from the clock. Every flag of the pass itself (`flatten`, `abc9`, `nobram`, `widemux`, `synth_flags`, ...) applies in either mode. A setting that would add a step before or after the pass, or make it read differently from `yosys <files>`, is refused.

abc9.help: Map LUTs with ABC9. `false` maps with classic ABC (`-noabc9`, or no `-abc9` where ABC9 is opt-in). Yosys 0.69 and newer require ABC9. For iCE40, the separate `noabc` setting selects the built-in LUT mapping.

flow3.help: Boolean ABC9 script choice: true selects `flow3`, false leaves the script to the synthesis pass. Use `abc9_script` for another named script; do not give both. Unset uses flow3 in Xeda's full recipe and leaves the pass's script in `synth_pass_only`. Has no effect unless ABC9 maps LUTs.

abc9_script.help: Select one of yosys's included ABC9 scripts in either synthesis mode: default, default.area, default.fast, flow, flow2, flow3 or flow3mfs. Unset uses flow3 in Xeda's full recipe and the synthesis pass's own choice in synth_pass_only. Has no effect when ABC9 mapping is disabled. Cannot be combined with the `flow3` setting.

retime.help: Retime flip-flops with ABC (`-retime`). Removed in yosys 0.69.

nobram.help: Do not map to block RAM cells.

nolutram.help: Do not use LUT RAM cells.

nowidelut.help: Disable wide LUT implementations that use hard MUX resources. Leave false to use the normal mapping choices of the family's synthesis pass.

widemux.help: Infer hard multiplexer resources for muxes with at least this many inputs. 0 disables it. The minimum is 2, and 5 or more is recommended.

pre_synth_opt.help: Run additional optimization steps before synthesis.

stop_after.help: Stop the flow after this stage. "rtl" elaborates the design and writes the RTL outputs without synthesizing, so it writes no netlist and no report. A setting that asks for one is refused: `netlist_json`, `netlist_verilog`, `netlist_graph`, `write_blif`, `sta` and `ltp` must be null or false.

clockgate_map.help: Verilog file with device-specific clock-gating cell mappings.

ice40_dsp.help: Infer UltraPlus MAC16 DSP cells with `synth_ice40 -dsp`.

ice40_device.help: iCE40 timing model. Unset: inferred from `fpga.device` or `fpga.type`.

clock.period.help: Clock period, a time with a unit, such as `10 ns`. Specify `period` or `freq`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

clock.rise.help: Time of the rising edge of the clock, a time with a unit, such as `0.5 ns`.

clock.uncertainty.help: Clock uncertainty, a time with a unit, such as `0.1 ns`.

clock.skew.help: Clock skew, a time with a unit, such as `0.05 ns`.

clock.port.help: The design port of the clock.

clock.freq.help: Clock frequency, a frequency with a unit, such as `100 MHz`. Specify `freq` or `period`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

verbose.help: Verbosity level. Higher values make the tools more talkative.

debug.help: Run the flow in debug mode: verbose logging, and exceptions are re-raised instead of being reported as a failure.

quiet.help: Run the flow quietly, unless `verbose` or `debug` is set.

redirect_stdout.help: Redirect stdout from execution of tools to files.

lib_paths.help: Additional libraries, as a list of (name, path) tuples. The name or the path can be none, but not both. GHDL and NVC take a relative path as relative to the design root.

docker.help: Run the tools in this Docker image, instead of the default image of the flow.

print_commands.help: Print the commands that the flow runs.

console_colors.help: Colorize tool output on the console.

timeout.help: Stop and fail each subprocess invocation that contains simulation after this many seconds of wall-clock time. An invocation can combine analysis, elaboration and simulation. The limit applies to each invocation, not to their total. None sets no limit.

fail_severity.help: The least severe runtime diagnostic that fails the simulation: warning, error, failure or fatal. Failure and fatal have the same rank. Diagnostics below the threshold are recorded. Assertions that the design disables explicitly keep the documented behavior of the simulator. A nonzero exit status always fails.

vcd.help: Write a VCD waveform to this file. `true` writes `dump.vcd`; a name without an extension gets `.vcd`; `false` or an empty name writes none. A simulator that cannot write VCD refuses it, and names its own waveform settings.

stop_time.help: Stop the simulation at this simulated time. Accepts a number of nanoseconds or a string with a unit, e.g. "100us".

cocotb.help: Settings for the cocotb testbench, used when `tb.cocotb` is set.

cocotb.coverage.help: Collect coverage data if supported by simulation tool.

cocotb.reduced_log_fmt.help: Display shorter log lines in the terminal.

cocotb.resolve_x.help: How to resolve bits with a value of X, Z, U or W when they are converted to an integer.

cocotb.testcase.help: Names of the cocotb tests to run; all of them if empty. A name selects exactly the test of that name (`check` never selects `foo_check`); on cocotb 2.x it may be qualified by its module (`tb.check`). Can also be given as a comma-separated string.

cocotb.random_seed.help: Seed of the Python random module (`COCOTB_RANDOM_SEED`): the same seed recreates the same test stimulus. "random" lets cocotb draw a new seed on every run, so the flow then always runs and is never reused.

cocotb.gpi_extra.help: A comma-separated list of extra libraries that are dynamically loaded at runtime.

log_file.help: File yosys writes its full log to, relative to the run directory. Set to null to log only to the console.

plugins.help: Yosys plugins to load with `plugin -i`, e.g. "ghdl" for VHDL input or "slang" for SystemVerilog.

flatten.help: Flatten the design hierarchy. Unset leaves the choice to the flow: `yosys` flattens when it maps to a liberty library (`liberty` or a `platform`) and keeps the hierarchy otherwise, and `yosys_sim` flattens only through CXXRTL's own `cxxrtl.flatten`.

read_verilog_flags.help: Flags passed to yosys' `read_verilog` for each Verilog source. They do not apply to the Verilog sources of a design that `slang` reads together with its SystemVerilog sources. When `yosys` maps to a liberty library, it refuses a flag that the script or a setting gives (`-defer`, `-D`, `-I`).

read_systemverilog_flags.help: Flags passed to the SystemVerilog front-end selected by `systemverilog`, `uhdm` or `slang`. The built-in reader (`default`) takes `read_verilog_flags` instead. With `slang`, they also apply to the Verilog sources, which the same `read_slang` reads when the design has a SystemVerilog source. A flag that the script gives to `read_slang` itself (`--top`, `-D`, `-I`, `-G`, `--blackboxed-module`, `--extern-modules`, `--best-effort-hierarchy`) is refused.

check_assert.help: Run yosys' `check -assert`. It fails the flow on structural problems such as combinational loops or multiply-driven wires.

rtl_verilog.help: Write the elaborated (pre-synthesis) design to this Verilog file. Useful for inspecting what yosys read.

rtl_json.help: Write the elaborated (pre-synthesis) design to this JSON file. Only the design's own modules are written, as for `rtl_verilog`: blackboxes and library cells are not.

rtl_graph.help: Render a `show` graph of the elaborated design to this file.

rtl_graph_flags.help: Flags passed to yosys' `show` when rendering `rtl_graph`.

ghdl.help: Settings for the ghdl-yosys plugin, used to read VHDL sources. Set automatically when the design has VHDL sources.

ghdl.verbose.help: Verbosity level. Higher values make the tools more talkative.

ghdl.debug.help: Run the flow in debug mode: verbose logging, and exceptions are re-raised instead of being reported as a failure.

ghdl.quiet.help: Run the flow quietly, unless `verbose` or `debug` is set.

ghdl.redirect_stdout.help: Redirect stdout from execution of tools to files.

ghdl.lib_paths.help: Additional libraries, as a list of (name, path) tuples. The name or the path can be none, but not both. GHDL and NVC take a relative path as relative to the design root.

ghdl.docker.help: Run the tools in this Docker image, instead of the default image of the flow.

ghdl.print_commands.help: Print the commands that the flow runs.

ghdl.console_colors.help: Colorize tool output on the console.

ghdl.clocks.help: Clock constraints of the design, by clock name.

ghdl.clocks.*.period.help: Clock period, a time with a unit, such as `10 ns`. Specify `period` or `freq`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

ghdl.clocks.*.rise.help: Time of the rising edge of the clock, a time with a unit, such as `0.5 ns`.

ghdl.clocks.*.uncertainty.help: Clock uncertainty, a time with a unit, such as `0.1 ns`.

ghdl.clocks.*.skew.help: Clock skew, a time with a unit, such as `0.05 ns`.

ghdl.clocks.*.port.help: The design port of the clock.

ghdl.clocks.*.freq.help: Clock frequency, a frequency with a unit, such as `100 MHz`. Specify `freq` or `period`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

ghdl.analysis_flags.help: Additional flags for the analysis phase.

ghdl.elab_flags.help: Additional flags for the elaboration phase.

ghdl.syn_bindings.help: Use synthesizer rules for component binding. During elaboration, if the VHDL LRM rules bind a component to no entity, look in every known library for an entity with the name of the component.

ghdl.warn_error.help: Treat every warning as an error.

ghdl.werror.help: Treat every warning as an error.

ghdl.elab_warn_error.help: Treat warnings as errors during elaboration.

ghdl.elab_werror.help: Treat warnings as errors during elaboration.

ghdl.relaxed.help: Relax some rules slightly, for compatibility with other simulators and synthesizers.

ghdl.clean_before_analyze.help: Run `ghdl remove` before analysis. It removes the work library and every file GHDL generated from it in the run directory.

ghdl.diagnostics.help: Enable both color and source line caret diagnostics.

ghdl.synopsys.help: Allow the Synopsys packages in the `ieee` library.

ghdl.psl_in_comments.help: Parse PSL assertions in comments (for VHDL-2002 and earlier).

ghdl.vendor_library.help: Treat every unit of this library as a black box.

ghdl.no_formal.help: Synthesize neither `assert` nor PSL. Required for the yosys+nextpnr flow.

ghdl.no_assert_cover.help: Pass `--no-assert-cover` to GHDL. Its help text reads: "Cover PSL assertion activation".

ghdl.assert_assumes.help: Treat all PSL asserts like PSL assumes.

ghdl.assume_asserts.help: Treat all PSL assumes like PSL asserts.

ghdl.verilog_output.help: Output file for the generated Verilog; by default `outputs/<design>.v`. If a directory is provided, each VHDL source file is converted to a Verilog file in that directory.

ghdl.clock.period.help: Clock period, a time with a unit, such as `10 ns`. Specify `period` or `freq`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

ghdl.clock.rise.help: Time of the rising edge of the clock, a time with a unit, such as `0.5 ns`.

ghdl.clock.uncertainty.help: Clock uncertainty, a time with a unit, such as `0.1 ns`.

ghdl.clock.freq.help: Clock frequency, a frequency with a unit, such as `100 MHz`. Specify `freq` or `period`; a consistent pair is also accepted.

systemverilog.help: SystemVerilog reader for CXXRTL. For common designs, the built-in reader generates cells that `write_cxxrtl` accepts. With `slang`, one `read_slang` reads the Verilog and SystemVerilog sources of the design and of the testbench, when they include a SystemVerilog source.

use_slang_plugin.help: Load the slang plugin when `systemverilog` is "slang". Disable if slang is compiled into your yosys build.

verilog_lib.help: Verilog library files read with `-lib`: their modules are used only when instantiated, and are otherwise treated as black boxes.

set_attribute.help: Attributes to set, from a mapping or a JSON file, organized as attr_name -> (object_path -> attr_value).

set_mod_attribute.help: Module attributes to set, organized as attr_name -> (module_path -> attr_value).

prep.help: Run yosys' `prep` with these flags instead of the default elaboration sequence.

keep_hierarchy.help: Modules that must not be flattened, marked with the `keep_hierarchy` attribute. See also `flatten`.

defines.help: Verilog preprocessor macros passed as `-D<name>=<value>`, in addition to the design's own `defines`.

black_box.help: Modules to treat as black boxes: their contents are discarded and only their interface is kept.

top_is_vhdl.help: Whether the top module is VHDL. Unset: it is VHDL if the last source in a hardware description language that the flow reads is VHDL.

cxxrtl.help: Settings for the generated CXXRTL C++ simulation model.

cxxrtl.filename.help: The C++ file that CXXRTL writes the simulation model to, as a name in the run directory (`<top>.cpp` by default). The C++ driver of the design includes the generated header `<name>.h`, so the setting takes a file name and no location. Use `--outputs-to` to copy the file elsewhere.
